is a deterministic partial constructor
\[
\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)
\]
and a deterministic extractor \(\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma}(c)\) with the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is defined and accepted if and only if the
six-clause predicate \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}(c,\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c))\) holds.
\item If \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is rejected, then
\(\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord of one
of the five obstruction skeletons in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}: missing submitted
evidence, missing assigned gate record, missing route or external decision field,
missing pinned discovery row, or unsupported command-run boundary.
\item For every properly stronger reading \(c^{+}\) of an accepted row, the same
extractor rejects \(c^{+}\) exactly at the first unpaid positive extension
coordinate of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}; if no such
coordinate is added, \(c^{+}\) is not distinct from \(c\) in the finite-record
preorder.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the publication-safety theorem has both a positive certificate
construction algorithm and a negative bad-subrecord extraction algorithm, each
bounded by the submitted schema fields.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The constructor is obtained by the ``Package-checker construction'' paragraph of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}: from the acceptance entry it reads
\(K\), \(\ell\), and \(E\); from record-gate soundness it reads the gate-pass rows
\(R\) assigned by \(\Gamma\); from the promotion hypothesis it reads \(H\) or the
no-crossing marker; from discovery routing it reads \(D\) exactly for discovery
claims; and from the evidence-level definition it reads \(B\), either the
path-verified boundary or the five command-run fields.  These are finite fields
on the submitted surface, so the constructor is deterministic and partial only
when a required field is absent.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, acceptance of the constructed tuple
is equivalent to \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}\), proving the first item.

For rejection, run the predicates \(P_1,\ldots,P_6\) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract} in order and return the finite
fields read by the first false predicate.  If the failure is not merely an
out-of-domain kind or level, it is one of the five substantive coordinates
\(E,R,H,D,B\).  The exhaustion argument of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} proves that these are
exactly the five listed obstruction skeletons, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:schema-partition-minimality} proves the required
inclusion-minimality relative to the schema partition and predicate order.  If the failure is an out-of-domain kind or level,
the same theorem reduces it to the corresponding assigned-gate or evidence-level
boundary obstruction, since \(K\) determines the finite gate set and \(\ell\)
determines the boundary obligation.

Finally let \(c^{+}\) be a proper stronger reading of an accepted row.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}, such a reading changes at
least one finite coordinate unless it is record-equivalent to \(c\).  The first
changed coordinate not supplied on the submitted support surface is read by one
of the six predicates and is therefore returned by the extractor.  If all changed
coordinates are supplied and pass their assigned gates, the enlarged tuple is a
new accepted certificate for the enlarged claim; if none are changed, the finite
preorder has not distinguished \(c^{+}\) from \(c\).\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Finite-record publication-safety maximality]
\label{prop:publication-safety-maximality}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, the
constructed certificate is a finite-record publication-safety certificate and is
maximal with respect to the finite submitted record surface, in the
schema-relative finite-record preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:finite-record-projection-preorder} and in the dependency
order isolated in Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-dependency-normal-form}.  More
precisely, let $c$ be an accepted load-bearing claim and let
$\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ be the certificate constructed in
that theorem.  If a stronger reading $c^{+}$ treats this finite-record
publication-safety certificate as external end-to-end workflow safety, compiler
correctness, current execution of unrecorded gates, proof-assistant correctness,
current formal-source currency, dynamic artifact semantics, or venue
safety/acceptance, then either $c^{+}$ is not a distinct finite-record consequence of
$\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)$, or its certificate must strictly enlarge one of
$K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B$ by adding the corresponding claim kind, evidence surface,
gate pass record, promotion or venue field, discovery-interface row, or
command-run tuple.  In the latter case, if the enlargement is absent,
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form} identifies the first missing
coordinate and a finite
bad subrecord is returned by Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} or by
one of the obstruction types of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The schema verifier used in Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} reads
only the tuple \((K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\), the dispatch table $\Gamma$, and the cited
submitted finite surfaces.  This is exactly the finite-coordinate determination
boundary of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  Hence two
surrounding implementations, formal-source trees, artifact runs, or venue states
that agree on those coordinates obtain the same verifier decision.  A purported
stronger reading which changes none of the coordinates is therefore invisible to
the certificate and cannot become a new accepted finite-record conclusion.

If the stronger reading is made load-bearing, it changes a coordinate in the
finite-record preorder.  External
compiler, proof-assistant, formal-source-currency, or artifact-semantics claims
add claim kinds and assigned gate records; fresh executions raise the evidence
boundary to command-run data; route or venue assertions add promotion or venue
surfaces; discovery-strengthening adds source-interface rows.  These are exactly
the finite fields tested by the clauses of
Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table}.  When the required
field is missing, Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form} supplies the
first missing coordinate, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} supplies the
failed acceptance clause, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} classifies the failure
as a missing evidence surface, gate record, promotion field, discovery-interface
row, or command-run escalation.\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current-package finite-record publication-safety instance]
\label{cor:publication-safety-current-package-instance}
For the current package, assume the support-surface condition delimited by
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:external-coordinate-admissibility-trichotomy}: the
exact supplemental \path{review_bundle/} directory is made reviewer-visible with
matching final digest records, or an archive-equivalent replacement with matching
final digest records is supplied.
Under that explicit availability condition, the finite pass-row components of
the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} are witnessed
by the machine-readable evidence map of
Proposition~\ref{prop:machine-readable-certificate-records}, the acceptance
ledger of
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-package-acceptance-certificate-ledger}, the
assigned-gate boundary of
Theorem~\ref{thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary}, and the four
path-complete case witnesses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}.  Therefore the current
package instantiates the construction theorem only as a finite-record
publication-safety certificate-construction and certificate-checking result for the finite records
actually supplied, with the bounded schema-relative package certificate exactness
isolated in Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}.  It is not,
without the separate extension coordinates listed in the boundary theorems, an
instance of gate implementation soundness, Lean/BEDC rebuild correctness,
artifact semantic validity, daemon behavior, upload, archive replacement,
upload-time venue compliance, or venue acceptance.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under the stated support-surface condition, each cited current-package result
supplies one finite hypothesis of the abstract interface.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-package-acceptance-certificate-ledger}
lists the accepted rows and their evidence surfaces.  The assigned-gate boundary
theorem gives the finite-record form of record-gate soundness and blocks an
unrecorded implementation-soundness reading.  The machine-readable certificate
records supply the schema mirror, pass-record rows, interface map, inventory,
verifier script, positive verifier log, negative fixture, and negative verifier
log when the exact review-bundle support surface is submitted with matching final
digests.  The positive log records the invocation
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py} and exit code
\path{0}; the negative log records the invocation
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py --negative-example review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example.json}
and the expected finite rejection \path{neg1: command-run fields incomplete}.
The case-witness proposition supplies
the finite case-study paths used by the accepted lesson rows.  Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} to these records gives the stated
bounded audit construction; Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}
is the row-frozen schema-relative exactness specialization.  The exclusions in
the statement follow because none of the cited current-package records contains
the extension coordinates required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}.\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-record boundary for external gate soundness]
\label{cor:finite-record-gate-soundness-boundary}
Under the hypotheses of the finite-record interface theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, the
finite-record publication-safety conclusion is invariant under replacement of the surrounding
implementation by any other implementation with the same submitted acceptance
entries, evidence surfaces, promotion fields, discovery-interface rows, and
evidence-level boundaries.  Therefore the theorem cannot be used, without an
additional submitted record-gate-soundness certificate, to infer external workflow
correctness, current execution of unrecorded gates, Lean correctness, artifact
semantic validity, or venue acceptance.  Conversely, any manuscript assertion
that tries to promote the finite certificate constructor to one of those stronger
implementation claims has a finite overclaim witness: either the required field
is absent from \(\mathcal C(c)\), or the row's declared evidence level exceeds
the cited certificate surface.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The constructor in the finite-record interface theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, reads only the
finite tuple \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\).  Here \(K\) is the claim-kind
set assigned by the dispatch table, \(\ell\) is the declared evidence level,
\(E\) is the submitted evidence surface, \(H\) is the human-promotion field,
\(R\) is the finite list of recorded pass rows, \(D\) is the pinned
discovery-interface field when the claim has a discovery component, and \(B\) is
the evidence boundary.  If another implementation supplies the same values for
these fields, the same finite schema verifier receives the same input record and
therefore gives the same certificate-construction conclusion by
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier} and
the schema-relative finite-record exactness theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}.  No step of the proof inspected an
unsubmitted daemon trace, reran a proof assistant, reran a finite-witness
artifact, or queried a venue form after the recorded venue check; those facts are
not coordinates of \(\mathcal C(c)\).

Now suppose the manuscript asserted one of the stronger implementation claims
without adding a new accepted record.  External workflow correctness and current
execution of unrecorded gates require pass data not present in \(R\).  Lean
correctness requires a formal-source certificate rather than the bounded
contextual rows allowed by Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation}.
Artifact semantic validity requires a stronger artifact row than the bounded
manifest records of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface}.
Venue acceptance requires a venue decision rather than the submission-pack
readiness row of Proposition~\ref{audit:venue-submission-pack-gate}.  In each
case, either the needed finite field is missing or the row is read at a stronger
evidence level than its certificate permits.  The obstruction is therefore a
finite subrecord of the kind classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:evidence-level-overclaim-obstruction}.\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-input projection-extension criterion]
\label{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}
Fix the dispatch table $\Gamma$ and the finite certificate schema of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}.  A reading of a
load-bearing package claim as a finite-input implementation-projection claim is
accepted by the same publication-safety interface if and only if the submitted
finite record surface is enlarged by an implementation-projection extension
record
\[
\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)=(K^{\mathrm{impl}},E^{\mathrm{impl}},R^{\mathrm{impl}},B^{\mathrm{impl}})
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K^{\mathrm{impl}}$ contains the additional finite-input implementation
projection claim kind or claim-kind component being asserted, rather than merely
reusing the original finite-record claim kind of $c$.
\item $E^{\mathrm{impl}}$ is a submitted finite evidence surface naming the
implementation object and projection being certified: for example the relevant
source path, version or commit, configuration, executable verifier, parsed-input
surface, declared finite predicate, and implementation-log surface.
\item $R^{\mathrm{impl}}$ contains a pass record, with evidence pointer inside
$E^{\mathrm{impl}}$, for every gate assigned by $\Gamma$ to the enlarged claim
kind $K\cup K^{\mathrm{impl}}$.
\item $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$ declares the evidence level of the implementation
projection claim and contains the command-run tuple whenever that finite-input
projection is asserted at command-run strength.
\end{enumerate}
When such an extension record is present, the finite certificate constructor of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} accepts the enlarged claim exactly
at the evidence level declared by $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$.  When it is absent, every
finite-input implementation-projection reading of the same row has a finite
obstruction of one of the five kinds in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.  No conclusion of
whole-program implementation soundness, semantic adequacy, or runtime soundness
outside the submitted projection follows from this criterion.
The current package supplies no record of the displayed form
$\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)$ for the package verifiers or gates.  Thus the theorem is
a future-facing exact criterion rather than an implementation-soundness result
for this submission: it says precisely what finite projection record must be
added before a later package may make that stronger claim.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First suppose the extension record is present.  Replace the original row for
$c$ by the enlarged row whose claim-kind coordinate is $K\cup K^{\mathrm{impl}}$,
whose evidence surface is $E\cup E^{\mathrm{impl}}$, whose pass-record field is
$R\cup R^{\mathrm{impl}}$, and whose boundary field is the original boundary
together with $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$.  The first condition makes the stronger
reading visible to the dispatch table rather than hiding it in prose.  The second
condition supplies a finite submitted surface for the implementation object and
the finite projection being asserted.  The
third condition supplies every gate record required by $\Gamma$ for the enlarged
claim-kind set, and the fourth condition prevents a path-verified implementation
record from being read as a command-run implementation certificate without the
command, source-state, environment, exit-code, and log-path fields.  Therefore
the tuple has exactly the fields checked by
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}.  Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} to the enlarged row constructs an
accepted finite certificate for the finite-input implementation-projection
reading, and the
accepted strength is precisely the declared evidence level because the schema
reads no unsubmitted evidence-level coordinate.

Conversely, suppose a manuscript row is read as a finite-input
implementation-projection claim
but no extension record with the four displayed properties is submitted.  If the
additional implementation-projection claim kind is not present in the claim-kind coordinate,
then the stronger reading has no assigned implementation gate and is an
unsupported escalation of the original row.  If the kind is present but
$E^{\mathrm{impl}}$ is absent, the claim lacks a submitted evidence surface for
the implementation object and finite projection, giving obstruction type~1 of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.  If the evidence
surface is present but some gate assigned by $\Gamma$ has no corresponding pass
record in $R^{\mathrm{impl}}$, the bad subrecord is type~2.  If the
implementation-projection reading crosses an intake, source, route, or venue boundary with
no required promotion or decision field, the bad subrecord is type~3.  If the
implementation-projection reading is also a discovery or classifier-shift reading without
the pinned discovery-interface rows, the bad subrecord is type~4.  Finally, if
the row asserts command-run implementation-projection strength without the command-run tuple
inside $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$, the bad subrecord is type~5.  These cases exhaust the
finite schema fields by the obstruction-skeleton theorem, so absence of the
extension record is exactly absence of finite support for the stronger reading.
Inspecting Table~\ref{tab:current-certificate-ledger} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:machine-readable-certificate-records}, the current package
records path-verified certificate rows $a_1,\ldots,a_7$ and command-boundary
inventory rows for bounded verifier invocations, but it does not add a new
implementation-projection claim kind, implementation-projection evidence surface, implementation gate
pass family, and implementation boundary tuple as a single
$\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)$ extension record.  Therefore this theorem is not instantiated
as an implementation-soundness theorem here; it remains an exact finite-record
extension test for a later package.

\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current-package projection-only implementation boundary]
\label{thm:current-package-implementation-upgrade-absence}
Fix the current submitted support surface, ledger, and dispatch table.  For every
load-bearing claim accepted by the finite-record publication-safety interface, the
largest implementation-related consequence available in the current package is
one of the named finite-input projection contracts explicitly covered by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}.  In
particular, the current package does not instantiate
\(\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)\) for any package verifier, gate program, daemon, Python
runtime, artifact checker, or end-to-end automath/newmath workflow.  Therefore
any reading that asserts whole-program implementation soundness, runtime
semantic adequacy, or correctness outside the submitted finite projection is
rejected by the finite-record interface with an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord;
conjoining finite-script projection rows, assigned-gate pass rows, source-path
rows, inventory rows, and historical case rows does not create the missing
implementation-upgrade coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The positive part is exactly the finite projection theorem for the four named
scripts.  Its hypotheses require source path, invocation command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path, and its conclusion is restricted to the
finite input projection parsed by the script and to the finite predicate printed
by that script.  The theorem explicitly excludes theorem truth, Lean/BEDC
correctness, artifact semantics, venue status, archive status, broad verifier
implementation soundness, and Python operational semantics.  Hence the current
package supplies finite-input projection-contract support only at those named
predicates.

Now fix any accepted load-bearing claim \(c\) and suppose that it is read as a
stronger implementation claim.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, acceptance of
that stronger reading is equivalent to the presence of an extension record
\(\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)=(K^{\mathrm{impl}},E^{\mathrm{impl}},R^{\mathrm{impl}},B^{\mathrm{impl}})\)
with an implementation claim kind, an implementation evidence surface, all
assigned implementation pass rows, and the corresponding boundary or command-run
tuple.  The proof of that theorem inspects the current package ledger and shows
that these four families are not present as a single extension record for the
package verifiers or gates.  Thus no current accepted row is upgraded to an
implementation-projection claim by the publication-safety constructor.

For a whole-program, runtime-semantic, daemon-level, or end-to-end workflow
soundness reading the obstruction is stronger still.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:gate-implementation-soundness-upgrade-obstruction}, even a
finite-input implementation projection would have to name the audited source,
command or invocation, finite input/output/log projection, submitted-byte binding,
finite implementation predicate, and proof-obligation link to the abstract gate
predicate.  A whole-program reading distinguishes states that agree on all those
submitted finite rows but differ outside the named predicate; therefore it
requires a separate semantic or program-verification coordinate.  Since that
coordinate is not present, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}
identifies the first absent coordinate, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} returns it as an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.

Finally, no conjunction of the other bounded rows repairs the absence.  Assigned
gate rows prove only the record-gate predicate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary}; source-path and
inventory rows prove only their finite equality or coverage predicates; and the
case rows remain historical/path-verified witnesses.  None contains an
implementation claim kind, implementation evidence surface, implementation pass
family, and implementation boundary tuple for the same claim.  The no-free-upgrade
results, in particular Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, forbid
gluing bounded coordinates from different channels into a missing upgrade
coordinate.  Hence the absence of implementation soundness in the current package
is a theorem-level boundary, not merely a terminological convention.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Submitted gate-implementation contract dichotomy]
\label{cor:submitted-gate-implementation-contract-dichotomy}
Fix the package ledger $L$, support surface $S$, and dispatch table $\Gamma$ of
the publication-safety interface.  A claim that the actual gate-producing
daemons or human workflow of the package satisfy record-gate soundness is
accepted by the theorem chain of this paper only in the following submitted-form
case: the package includes a finite implementation contract
\[
\mathsf{GateImpl}(P)=(I,E_I,R_I,B_I)
\]
where $I$ names the gate-producing implementations and human boundary
procedures, $E_I\subseteq S$ names their source, configuration, replay inputs,
and produced-row surfaces, $R_I$ contains a submitted pass record for every
implementation or human-boundary gate assigned by $\Gamma$ to that stronger
claim, and $B_I$ contains the command-run tuple whenever the contract is read at
command-run strength.  If no such finite tuple is submitted, then every system
soundness reading of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} is rejected:
the theorem remains strictly conditional on the submitted gate-passage records
in $L$ and asserts no independent soundness of the daemons, scripts, or human
workflow that produced those rows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The claim that the actual daemons, scripts, or human workflow satisfy
record-gate soundness is an implementation-soundness reading of the finite
record row.  Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}
with $K^{\mathrm{impl}}$ equal to the additional implementation component,
$E^{\mathrm{impl}}=E_I$, $R^{\mathrm{impl}}=R_I$, and
$B^{\mathrm{impl}}=B_I$.  If the displayed contract is present, the enlarged row
has an explicit implementation kind, a submitted evidence surface for the
implementation objects and human boundary procedures, all assigned pass rows,
and the declared evidence-level boundary.  The finite certificate constructor
therefore accepts exactly that enlarged finite-record claim and no stronger one.

Conversely, suppose the manuscript is read as asserting such implementation
soundness while no tuple $\mathsf{GateImpl}(P)$ is submitted.  If $I$ or the
corresponding implementation claim kind is missing, the stronger reading is
invisible to $\Gamma$; if $E_I$ is missing, there is no submitted implementation
surface; if $R_I$ is missing, some assigned implementation or human-boundary gate
has no submitted pass row; and if $B_I$ is missing at command-run strength, the
evidence-level boundary is incomplete.  These are exactly the finite obstruction
cases classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}
and by Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}.  Hence,
without the displayed tuple, the only remaining hypothesis available to
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} is the conditional finite
predicate $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ over the submitted gate-passage records;
no independent implementation-level soundness follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[External-interface projection and no-free-implementation upgrade]
\label{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade}
Fix a package $P$, submitted surface $S$, acceptance ledger $L$, and dispatch
table $\Gamma$.  The finite schema for this theorem is exactly the six-predicate
acceptance relation \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}\) of
Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table}.  Its preorder is the
stronger-reading preorder \(\preceq_{\Gamma}\): a reading is stronger only by
adding a finite claim-kind, evidence-level, implementation, command, semantic,
venue, or support coordinate assigned by \(\Gamma\).  Minimality always means
inclusion-minimality among submitted finite fields after unrelated rows are
deleted, and exhaustiveness is relative to the coordinates named by this schema,
not to hidden implementation or semantic states.  Let $\pi(P,S,L,\Gamma)$ be the
finite record projection that retains only the fields read by the certificate
schema: claim kinds, evidence levels, submitted evidence pointers,
human-promotion fields, assigned passing gate rows, discovery-interface rows, and
command-boundary tuples.  Then the following are equivalent for the
finite-record publication-safety conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem constructs the accepted publication certificates for the
load-bearing rows of $L$.
\item The projected finite record $\pi(P,S,L,\Gamma)$ satisfies
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ and the remaining finite hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently any two gate-producing implementations, daemon histories, or human
workflows with the same projection $\pi(P,S,L,\Gamma)$ are indistinguishable by
the theorem: they yield the same accepted certificates and the same finite bad
subrecords.  A stronger reading asserting independent soundness of the gates,
scripts, daemons, or human workflow is accepted if and only if the projection is
strictly enlarged by an implementation-soundness extension record of the form
specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}; in
particular, when a command-run implementation reading is asserted, that extension
must include command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path.  Without
that enlargement the stronger implementation reading is rejected while the
finite-record interface certificate, if otherwise valid, remains accepted at its
declared finite evidence level.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The verifier predicates $P_1,\ldots,P_6$ in the certificate schema read exactly
the fields retained by $\pi$: the claim-kind coordinate, the evidence-level and
evidence-surface coordinates, the assigned gate rows, the human-promotion field,
the discovery-interface field, and the command-boundary field.  Therefore
replacing $(P,S,L,\Gamma)$ by another package with the same projection gives the
same input to Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}.  The
schema-relative exactness theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness},
then gives the same acceptance value and the same rejected bad subrecord for each
load-bearing row.  Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}
identifies this projected record condition with the finite predicate
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.  Thus the theorem's certificate
construction depends on the package only through $\pi$ and the explicitly stated
finite hypotheses, proving the equivalence and the indistinguishability claim.

It remains to characterize stronger implementation readings.  Such a reading
adds an implementation claim-kind component or raises the evidence level of an
existing gate row beyond the submitted row-and-pointer record.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, acceptance of
that stronger reading is equivalent to adding the four implementation extension
coordinates $K^{\mathrm{impl}}$, $E^{\mathrm{impl}}$, $R^{\mathrm{impl}}$, and
$B^{\mathrm{impl}}$; at command-run strength the fourth coordinate contains the
command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path.  If the extension is
present, the enlarged projection is checked by the same schema and the stronger
finite-record claim is accepted at its declared evidence level.  If the extension
is absent, one of the finite coordinates required by the schema is missing, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} supplies the finite bad
subrecord.  The original finite-record certificate is unaffected because its
projection has not changed.
\end{proof}

$a_5$ & path-verified & phase-D hard-lint path, theorem inventory or artifact inventory surface, and source-interface rows & marker that no separate publication route is promoted by the rejected extension & theorem-content delta record plus discovery-gate record rejecting statement-only, code-only, mechanical, or compression-only growth & present: rows for certificate/ledger, demotion, lineage, pipeline safety, and main pipeline theorem in Table~\ref{tab:source-interface-record} & no claim that compilation or file churn is theorem growth \\
$a_6$ & path-verified & Rule110 status file, collision and exhaustiveness ledgers, paper-data reference, and review-bundle manifest & marker that the artifact row does not create a new route boundary & artifact status and limitation-ledger records & absent & no fresh \path{make test-collision-audit} or dynamic artifact rerun asserted \\
