\begin{theorem}[Workspace-to-final-package reconciliation]
\label{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation}
Let $D_0$ be the digest manifest
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, and let $H_i$ denote the source
state printed in verifier log $i$.  The source-state claim made in Audit
record~\ref{prop:final-immutable-package-state-certificate} is the finite package
claim consisting of these recorded pairs $(H_i,D_0)$, not a claim that every
later reviewer checkout, editor workspace, or post-packaging working tree has Git
\path{HEAD} equal to a single historical commit.  If a current workspace reports
a different Git \path{HEAD} from one of the historical rows, then the verifier-log and
bundle-backed claims of this supplement remain admissible exactly in the
following two reconciled cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the submitted support surface is exact inclusion of \path{review_bundle/}, or
an archive equivalent to it, whose finite certificate files match the SHA-256
rows of $D_0$; or
\item the package is deliberately advanced to the current workspace state by
rerunning the three verifier commands and replacing the displayed source-state
record, the verifier logs, and the digest manifest by new matching
source-state--manifest certificates.
\end{enumerate}
In all other cases a mismatch between a later workspace \path{HEAD} and a
recorded historical row does not certify a new package state and does not
invalidate the historical finite package claim $(H_i,D_0)$; it only shows that
the later workspace is
outside the submitted support surface.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The accepted command-result coordinates are finite.  By
Audit record~\ref{prop:final-immutable-package-state-certificate}, the three log
paths, the recorded source-state fields $H_i$, and the manifest $D_0$ form the
source-state record for the verifier runs.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}, those log claims are part of the
accepted support surface only when the exact bundle is submitted or when an
archive supplies the same finite file list, digests, and relative path semantics.
Thus case (1) fixes the bytes of the certificate files directly: the reviewer's
ambient checkout may have any Git \path{HEAD}, but the submitted certificate
surface is still the byte-identified finite package $(H_i,D_0)$.

Suppose instead that the authors want the later workspace itself to be the
package state.  Then at least one source-state coordinate has changed, namely
the Git \path{HEAD} coordinate.  The verification rule in the scope contract
requires every command-result claim to record its exact command, source commit,
environment, exit code, and log path.  Therefore a new workspace state cannot be
accepted by merely observing the new \path{HEAD}; the three verifier runs must be
rerun against that state, and their logs and digest manifest must be replaced by
consistent source-state--manifest records.  This is case (2).

If neither case holds, the later workspace contributes no finite coordinate to
the submitted certificate.  It is not named in $D_0$, it is not an
archive-equivalent representative under Table~\ref{tab:review-bundle-archive-equivalence},
and it is not accompanied by fresh verifier logs satisfying the command-result
record rule.  The finite-coordinate determination boundary of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} then forbids silently
using that workspace either to certify a new package or to refute the old
byte-identified package.  The only certified statement left is the historical
finite package claim $(H_i,D_0)$, conditional on the exact support-surface branch
already proved above.\end{proof}

\begin{auditrecord}[Mutable-checkout observations are non-certifying]
\label{prop:mutable-checkout-observation-boundary}
This audit record retains the legacy cross-reference label
\path{prop:mutable-checkout-observation-boundary} for compatibility with earlier
acceptance-ledger entries; its environment category is \path{auditrecord}, not
\path{proposition}.
Let $W$ be a review-time working tree whose Git \path{HEAD} is not one of the
source-state rows recorded in the verifier logs named in
Theorem~\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation}.  The observation of $W$
is not a certificate coordinate for any verifier-log claim in this package unless
$W$ is promoted by the second branch of that theorem, namely by rerunning the
three verifier commands and replacing the source-state, log, and digest records
by new matching finite package certificates.  Consequently, a reviewer who sees
$W$ with a different \path{HEAD} has exactly one source-level reconciliation
test for the existing package: inspect the exact-bundle or archive-equivalent
surface whose certificate-file bytes match \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
\medskip
\noindent\emph{Verification.} The finite package certificate records three kinds of coordinates relevant here:
the logged source-state rows, the verifier logs, and the per-file digest manifest.  A
bare working-tree observation supplies none of the last two coordinates and, when
its \path{HEAD} differs from a recorded row, supplies a different first coordinate.  By the
command-result rule used in
Audit record~\ref{prop:final-immutable-package-state-certificate}, changing a
source-state coordinate requires fresh logs with their command, environment, exit
code, and log path; this is precisely the promotion branch in
Theorem~\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation}.  If that branch is not
performed, the observation of $W$ remains outside the finite package.  The only
remaining reconciliation route is therefore the branch that checks the already
selected support surface: the exact included \path{review_bundle/} directory, or
an archive equivalent under Table~\ref{tab:review-bundle-archive-equivalence},
with certificate bytes fixed by the final digest manifest.
\end{auditrecord}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record support invariant: bundle-backed normal form]
\label{thm:support-surface-normal-form}
For the current presentation package, every accepted use of a bundle-backed
certificate coordinate is in exactly one of the following normal forms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Exact inclusion}: an external upload or submission receipt records
that the submitted support surface contains the exact \path{review_bundle/}
directory whose certificate-file bytes match
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
\item \emph{Archive-equivalent inclusion}: a replacement archive satisfies every
row of Table~\ref{tab:review-bundle-archive-equivalence}, including manifest
identity, bundle-version identity, finite file-list identity, SHA-256 content
identity, and relative path semantics.
\item \emph{Promoted rerun}: the package is advanced to a new source state by
rerunning the verifier commands and replacing the displayed source-state record,
verifier logs, and digest manifest by one common finite commit--manifest
certificate.
\end{enumerate}
If none of these three normal forms is present, the attempted bundle-backed
reading has a finite obstruction subrecord: either the external exact-inclusion
receipt is absent, the archive-equivalence table has a failed row, or the rerun
branch lacks the command, source-state, environment, exit-code, log-path, and
digest coordinates required by the command-boundary rule.  Thus the late
support-surface chain is a finite audit-interface classification for this
package, not a theorem about general archive infrastructure, venue upload, or
semantic correctness of the bundled artifacts.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The candidate support surface for a bundle-backed coordinate can differ from the
source-level package in only three record-visible ways.  First, it can supply an
external receipt for the same directory selected by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-inclusion-support-surface-realization} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} prove that this exact directory,
with the final digest manifest, is the local byte surface that must be supplied;
the additional receipt is what turns that local selection into submitted support.
This is normal form~(1).

Second, the candidate can replace the directory by an archive.  The manuscript
does not accept arbitrary archive availability as a certificate coordinate:
Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence} gives the finite
hash-and-manifest test, and every failed row of
Table~\ref{tab:review-bundle-archive-equivalence} is a finite bad subrecord.  If
all rows pass, the replacement denotes the same certificate bytes under the same
relative paths and is normal form~(2); if any row fails, the archive cannot carry
the bundle-backed claim.

Third, the candidate can point to a later or different workspace state.
Theorem~\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation} proves that such a state
is not the old finite package unless it is deliberately promoted by fresh verifier
runs and by a replacement commit--manifest certificate.
Audit record~\ref{prop:mutable-checkout-observation-boundary} then shows that a
bare mutable-checkout observation is non-certifying.  Therefore a different
workspace is accepted only in normal form~(3), and otherwise has the finite
command-boundary obstruction stated in the theorem.

The three cases are mutually exclusive as record modes for a fixed submitted
claim: the first uses the selected directory, the second uses a byte-identical
archive representative, and the third replaces the package state and digest
record by a new common certificate.  If a proposed support reading is in none of
the modes, it contributes no coordinate read by the verifier.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} and the obstruction
skeleton of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, the missing
coordinate is an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord rather than a semantic
fact about the underlying artifacts.\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record support invariant compression]
\label{thm:support-surface-invariant-compression}
Let $\mathcal S$ be the family of support-surface and post-inventory claims in
Theorems~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure},
\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation},
\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}, and
\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple}.  For the current package,
every member of $\mathcal S$ is a projection of the same finite support tuple
\[
\Sigma=(F,M,D,R,Q),
\]
where $F$ is the selected relative file list, $M$ is the review-bundle manifest,
$D$ is the final digest table, $R$ is the retained extractor and verifier log
family, and $Q$ is the post-inventory ordering relation saying that the inventory
bytes precede the retained log bytes and that the digest table is regenerated
after them.  More precisely, each theorem in $\mathcal S$ is obtained from
$\Sigma$ by forgetting all but one of the following projections:
\begin{enumerate}
\item byte closure of the selected support surface $(F,M,D)$;
\item reconciliation of a later workspace through replacement logs $(R,D)$;
\item the three accepted external-support modes of
Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}; or
\item the post-inventory replay order $(Q,R,D)$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence a presentation version may state this family as one finite-record support
invariant and cite the inventory file, theorem-environment extractor log, finite
record-verifier logs, and final digest table for full label coverage.  Such a
compression loses no mathematical content for the CICM presentation route,
because none of the separated labels in $\mathcal S$ carries an independent
semantic claim beyond these finite projections.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each cited result reads only the named finite files, manifests, logs, digests, and
their ordering.  The final support-surface closure theorem reads the selected
file list, manifest rows, and digest rows, so it is the projection $(F,M,D)$.
The workspace reconciliation theorem compares later workspace observations with
the retained source-state and verifier-log records; it therefore reads only the
log family and digest certificate, namely $(R,D)$, together with the rule that a
replacement workspace must supply fresh records of the same form.  The support
surface normal-form theorem classifies the same selected bytes into exact
inclusion, archive-equivalent inclusion, or promoted rerun; this is a case split
on the external-support projection of $(F,M,D,R)$.  The post-inventory fixed
point and its stable replay corollary add no new support object; they add the
ordering projection $Q$ saying which inventory, extractor, verifier, and digest
bytes were produced after which earlier bytes.

Because these projections are all functions of the one tuple $\Sigma$, a reader
who is given $\Sigma$ can reconstruct the truth value and bad-subrecord witness
of every label in $\mathcal S$ by applying the corresponding projection and then
the already proved finite-coordinate determination theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  Conversely, any
accepted support claim among the cited labels must pass one of the displayed
projection checks: otherwise the normal-form theorem or the post-inventory fixed
point supplies the missing finite coordinate as a bad subrecord.  Thus the labels
are useful finite-record support entries but not independent semantic theorems about Lean,
artifact behavior, archive infrastructure, venue upload, or journal acceptance.
For a presentation article, replacing the separated labels by the single tuple
statement and pointing to \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log}, the retained finite
record-verifier logs, and \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} preserves
exactly the same finite-record content.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record upload-boundary invariant]
\label{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}
Before the bundle-backed claims of this supplement are treated as part of a
completed venue submission, the external submission record must instantiate one
support-surface branch selected by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention} and
Theorems~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} and
\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}.  Either it must record that
\path{review_bundle/} was uploaded exactly with digest manifest $D_0$ and with
the root \path{theorem_inventory.json} coordinate named by the manifest and
ledger, or it must record an archive-equivalent locator satisfying
Theorem~\ref{thm:public-branch-archive-equivalent-realization}.  The TeX source
and the local digest manifest select those admissible branches but do not
constitute a venue upload receipt or a public byte-equality locator.  In the
present source package no exact-upload receipt and no final-state public
byte-equality locator is recorded; consequently all bundle-backed claims are
proved only as local/path-verified support claims until one of the two external
instantiation records is supplied.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} prove that the bundle-backed
claims for this package are admissible in either the exact-directory branch or
the public branch/path archive-equivalent branch, subject in both cases to the
same final digest rows.  Audit record~\ref{prop:exact-review-bundle-upload-witness}
and Audit record~\ref{prop:final-immutable-package-state-certificate} give the
same support tuple and explicitly exclude a DOI, venue-upload receipt, and
final-state public byte-equality record.  Those source records determine what
must be submitted or publicly located, but they are produced before the venue's
upload action.  Hence a completed submission needs one additional external
instantiation record: either the venue or packager records the exact supplemental
directory upload with the final digest manifest, or the public branch/path
coordinate is checked at a pinned commit or refreshed branch head and contains
the matching digest-identified tuple.
Without one of those records, the statements proved above remain conditional
source-level support claims rather than a proof that an external support action
has occurred.  Therefore
treating the bundle-backed claims as externally instantiated would add a
coordinate not present in the finite support surface, contradicting the finite
coordinate determination boundary of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Upload-or-archive instantiation record]
\label{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
The bundle-backed support claims of the current package may be used only under
the external-record condition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}.  In particular,
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is a local byte-level packaging
manifest and not, by itself, an upload receipt, DOI, or proof that the public
branch/path locator already contains the matching bytes.  Thus the current
package has a conditional local-support reading unless a later exact-upload
receipt or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator is added to the finite
support surface.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the record-level specialization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary} to the current digest
manifest.  The added sentence is the contrapositive of the same boundary: when
neither admissible external record is present, the finite support tuple lacks the
coordinate that would certify completed upload or archive-equivalent byte
equality, and Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} forbids
supplying that coordinate by prose.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[No external instantiation from local bundle records]
\label{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}
In the current source package, the rows of
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, the manifest fields of
\path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}, and the support-boundary notes
in this supplement instantiate only a local exact-inclusion
support mode and name the public branch/path archive-equivalent coordinate.
They do not by themselves instantiate either admissible external-support branch
of Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  Consequently any
claim depending on a file under \path{review_bundle/} or on the root theorem
ledger \path{theorem_inventory.json} remains a conditional local package-support
claim unless a finite update supplies an exact venue-upload receipt or the public
automath branch/path archive-equivalent locator with matching bytes recorded in
the manuscript, manifest, bibliography, and digest surfaces.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The admissible external-support branches are exactly the two branches isolated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}: an exact uploaded
\path{review_bundle/} directory with matching final digests, or an
archive-equivalent replacement satisfying the same manifest, file-list, digest,
and relative-path tests.  The present package supplies the local byte manifest
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} and manifest text selecting exact
supplemental inclusion, but these are source-package coordinates.  By the same
corollary, a local byte manifest is not an upload receipt, DOI, public archive
identifier, or archive locator.  The source-level support-boundary records assert no such upload receipt or DOI.  The archive-equivalent branch is
instantiated only when the public automath branch/path coordinate contains bytes
matching the final digest rows.  Hence the local source package alone does not
instantiate either external branch.

If a bundle-backed claim were nevertheless read as externally supported, its
finite support tuple would contain an upload-or-archive coordinate absent from
the local package.  This is exactly the obstruction excluded by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  Therefore the only
current reading is conditional local package support.  The final sentence is the
contrapositive update condition: leaving this normal form requires adding one of
the missing external coordinates to the common manuscript, manifest,
bibliography, and digest surfaces so that all finite records name the same
submitted support surface.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Upload-or-archive instantiation update protocol]
\label{prop:upload-or-archive-instantiation-update-protocol}
Suppose a later venue upload receipt or archive-equivalent locator is to be used
to replace the current no-receipt boundary of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} by an externally
instantiated submitted-support claim.  Then the replacement is accepted by the
finite-record interface if and only if one of the two following finite update
protocols is performed.  The manuscript surfaces in the statement are precisely
\path{submission_abstract.tex} and \path{main.tex}; the manifest surface is
\path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}; the bibliography surface is
\path{references.bib}; and the digest surface is
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} or a replacing digest manifest named
by both manuscript sources and by the manifest.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Exact-upload update.}  \path{submission_abstract.tex} and
\path{main.tex} record the receipt or venue
submission identifier for the exact support surface selected in
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention}; the manifest field
\path{public_interface.distribution_mode} is changed from conditional exact
supplemental upload to completed exact supplemental upload; the manifest field
\path{public_interface.preferred_submission_form} or an adjacent receipt field
names the uploaded \path{submission_abstract.pdf}, \path{main.pdf} or
\path{main.tex}, root \path{theorem_inventory.json}, and \path{review_bundle/};
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} still contains matching digest rows
for the submitted bundle files; and a support-boundary sentence in the source is changed from no completed upload
to the same receipt-bound support statement.
\item \emph{Archive-equivalent update.}  \path{submission_abstract.tex} and
\path{main.tex} record the archive
locator; the manifest field \path{public_interface.current_public_archive} and the
support-boundary sentence in the source names that same locator; the manifest keeps or replaces \path{public_interface.archival_update_rule}
with the byte-equivalence rule actually satisfied; and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, or a replacing digest manifest named
by both the manuscript and the manifest, records the file list and SHA--256 rows
against which the archive is checked, including the coordinates for
\path{review_bundle/}, \path{theorem_inventory.json}, and the manifest itself.
\end{enumerate}
In either protocol, if any digest row, manifest public-interface field,
manuscript support statement, bibliography note, or receipt/locator coordinate is
changed, all four surfaces must name the same support mode and the same finite
receipt-or-locator record.  Without this finite common update, the current
no-receipt normal form of
Proposition~\ref{prop:submission-support-instantiation-field-normal-form} remains
the only accepted submitted-support status.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The current package has only the source-level exact-inclusion branch by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}.  Thus an external
instantiation can add exactly one new positive coordinate: either a receipt for
that exact upload or a locator for an archive-equivalent representative.  The
finite-coordinate determination boundary,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, forbids the verifier
from reading any coordinate not present on the submitted support surface.  Hence
the new coordinate must be visible wherever the package declares public support
status: in the manuscript statement that changes the boundary, in the manifest
public-interface fields that describe distribution mode and archive status, in
the digest manifest that identifies the bytes being supplied, and in the
source-level support-boundary sentence that tells a reviewer whether the bundle
is an external support surface or merely a local note.

For the exact-upload branch, the receipt is meaningful for this package only if
it refers to the support surface selected by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention}: the primary presentation
artifact, the technical supplement, the root theorem inventory, and the exact
\path{review_bundle/} directory with matching final digests.  Updating the
manuscript, the manifest distribution fields, the digest record, and the
bibliography note with the same receipt is therefore sufficient for the finite
record checker to read the external-upload coordinate; if one of those records is
missing or names a different support mode, the checker sees a bad subrecord of
the kind classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}.

For the archive-equivalent branch, Table~\ref{tab:review-bundle-archive-equivalence}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form} require the archive to preserve
the same file list, digest rows, manifest semantics, and relative-path meanings.
The stated archive update records exactly those finite data: the common locator,
the byte-equivalence rule, and the digest manifest identifying the archive bytes.
Again, if the manuscript, manifest, bibliography, and digest surface do not name a
single common locator and byte-equivalence certificate, the proposed archive is
not a finite coordinate accepted by the verifier.

The two branches are exhaustive because
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} allows only an exact
upload receipt or an archive-equivalent replacement to instantiate the support
surface.  Therefore a future support claim is accepted exactly after one of the
two finite common updates above, and otherwise the no-receipt normal form remains
the accepted status.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current package missing-coordinate classifier]
\label{thm:current-package-missing-coordinate-classifier}
For the current presentation package, the following five proposed upgrades are
rejected by the finite-record interface unless the named coordinate is added to
the submitted support surface:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a current-byte theorem-inventory or support-surface closure claim requires
post-inventory extractor and verifier logs followed by a regenerated final digest
manifest containing the resulting \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes;
\item an externally instantiated supplemental-support claim requires either an
exact venue-upload receipt for the selected supplemental surface or an
archive-equivalent locator whose bytes match the final digest rows;
\item a fresh Lean/BEDC formal-source claim requires an accepted formal-source
row with build-gate and axiom-purity-gate pass records, and, for any fresh
execution reading, the command, source commit or package digest manifest,
environment, exit code, and log path;
\item a dynamic Rule110/GroundCompiler or finite-witness artifact-semantic claim
requires a separate artifact-validation row containing the evaluator contract,
rerun command, source or artifact digest coordinates, exit code, and log path;
and
\item an upload-time venue or completed-submission compliance claim requires a
finite submission record naming the upload command or interface action,
timestamp, submitted source state, included support files, and receipt or
archive-equivalent locator, together with the fresh or unchanged-rule venue
record required by
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}.
\end{enumerate}
With the support records currently printed and bundled, none of these five
coordinates is present except as a conditional future-update protocol.  Therefore
the accepted reading of the package is exactly local/path-verified finite-record
support, bounded source-interface evidence, and historical manifest-bounded
artifact evidence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each item is a direct finite-coordinate specialization of the preceding support
spine, and the five items exhaust the missing-coordinate upgrades named in the
current package boundary.  For item~1, the post-inventory support theorems treat
inventory bytes as part of the support tuple, not as invariant background.  If
\path{theorem_inventory.json} or \path{theorem_inventory.md} is rewritten, an old
extractor log or final digest row is a record about an earlier byte string.  The
finite-coordinate determination theorem therefore accepts a current-byte closure
claim only after the new inventory bytes, the post-inventory extractor/verifier
logs, and the final digest manifest occur in that order and the final manifest
contains the new SHA--256 rows.

For item~2, Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary},
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records} show
that a local digest table and manifest identify the support surface but do not
record the external upload or archive event.  An externally instantiated reading
therefore adds a coordinate not present in the current source package unless the
receipt or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator is supplied.

For item~3, Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction} identify the formal-source
dispatch gates as build and axiom-purity, with command-run fields added for any
fresh-execution sentence.  The current six-row ledger contains no accepted
formal-source row of that kind, so a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-existence
audit, or axiom-purity audit is not a coordinate of the package.

For item~4, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} restrict the Rule110,
GroundCompiler, and finite-witness case material to the manifest-bounded
historical rows and snapshots.  A semantic-validity or dynamic-rerun assertion
would require a new artifact-validation coordinate with the evaluator contract
and command-result fields listed in the statement; absent that row, the finite
schema verifier returns the missing-coordinate bad subrecord.

For item~5,
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} show that a
dated venue/bibliography readiness row lacks the upload action, timestamp,
receipt or form state, submitted source state, included support-file list, and
unchanged-rule bridge needed for upload-time compliance.  A completed-submission
claim is also an external-support claim, so
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} requires either the
exact supplemental-upload receipt or the archive-equivalent locator of item~2.
Thus the item~5 coordinate is not obtained by combining the dated readiness log
with the local digest manifest; it is a separate upload-time finite record.

Thus each proposed upgrade fails for the same reason: it asks the package to
read a coordinate outside the finite tuple actually supplied.  The accepted
reading is consequently the intersection of the five bounded interfaces already
proved: current local support only after regenerated inventory/digest records,
conditional external support only after upload or archive instantiation, bounded
source-interface context rather than fresh formal-source execution, and
historical manifest-bounded artifact evidence rather than dynamic semantic
validation, plus dated local-readiness evidence rather than upload-time venue or
completed-submission compliance.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-coordinate local support closure]
\label{thm:four-coordinate-local-support-closure}
Let \(\Sigma\) be the current finite support surface of the presentation package,
consisting of the submitted source paths, the two theorem-inventory files,
\path{source_interface_record.json}, the manifest rows in \path{review_bundle/},
the retained verifier logs, the final SHA--256 digest manifest, and the dated
venue/bibliography readiness logs.  Then the five coordinates below are
independent finite coordinates of \(\Sigma\):
\begin{enumerate}
\item the post-inventory local byte-closure coordinate;
\item the external submitted-support coordinate, instantiated only by an exact
supplemental-upload receipt or an archive-equivalent byte-equality locator;
\item the fresh formal-source coordinate, instantiated only by accepted build and
axiom-purity rows with the command-result fields of the formal-source gate;
\item the dynamic artifact-semantic coordinate, instantiated only by an accepted
artifact-validation row with evaluator contract, artifact digests, semantic
predicate, command result, exit code, and log path; and
\item the upload-time venue/completed-submission coordinate, instantiated only by
an upload command or interface-action record with timestamp, submitted source
state, included support files, receipt or archive-equivalent locator, and the
fresh or unchanged-rule venue bridge.
\end{enumerate}
After the two inventory files are accepted, rerunning the theorem-environment
extractor, the certificate-record verifier, the source-interface verifier, the
primary-claim verifier, and then regenerating
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} supplies exactly the first
coordinate for the current local bytes.  It supplies none of the last four
coordinates.  Consequently the accepted reading of the current package is:
local/path-verified support for the current inventory bytes; no externally
instantiated support surface absent an upload receipt or archive-equivalence
byte-equality record; bounded source-interface evidence rather than a fresh
Lean/BEDC rebuild or complete source audit; and finite-witness or historical
artifact evidence rather than dynamic artifact-semantic validation; and dated
local-readiness evidence rather than upload-time venue or completed-submission
compliance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The five listed coordinates are fields in different projections of the finite
record interface.  The first projection reads only local source bytes,
inventory bytes, command-log bytes, and digest rows.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}, when the inventory bytes are fixed
before the extractor and verifier runs and the final digest is generated after
the logs, the ordered tuple consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, \(R_{\mathrm{A2}}\), and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is a positive local fixed point
for current-byte theorem-inventory support.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-missing-coordinate-classifier}, if any member of
that ordered tuple is absent or stale, the first absent or stale member is the
finite bad subrecord for a current-byte closure claim.  Thus the specified rerun
sequence is necessary and sufficient for the first coordinate.

The remaining coordinates are not read by the same projection.  The external
support projection is classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary},
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}:
it requires either an exact supplemental-upload receipt or a byte-equality record
for an archive-equivalent locator.  Local path names, local manifests, verifier
logs, and digest rows can identify the bytes to be submitted, but none of them is
the external receipt or public byte-equality event.  Therefore the post-inventory
rerun tuple cannot instantiate the submitted-support coordinate.

The formal-source projection is classified by
Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation},
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}.  Those
results require build-gate and axiom-purity-gate rows, with command, source
commit or digest state, environment, exit code, and log path for any fresh-run
reading.  The current source-interface files and logs verify bounded extraction,
range, label, manifest, and non-escalation data; they do not contain a Lean or
BEDC rebuild command row and do not audit all source axioms.  Hence they cannot
be reinterpreted as the third coordinate.

The artifact projection is classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  A dynamic semantic
artifact claim adds evaluator-source, artifact-byte, semantic-predicate,
environment, command-result, exit-code, and log-path fields.  The case-study and
manifest rows available in \(\Sigma\) are finite-witness or historical
path-verified records; they contain no accepted row of that artifact-validation
form.  Hence the fourth coordinate is absent unless such a row is later added.

The upload-time venue/completed-submission projection is classified by
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  It reads an upload
or interface action, timestamp, submitted source state, included support files,
receipt or archive-equivalent locator, and the fresh or unchanged-rule venue
bridge.  The dated venue/bibliography logs in \(\Sigma\) record only a local
readiness observation on their observation dates.  The inventory rerun tuple and
the digest manifest do not add an upload action, receipt, form state, or
unchanged-rule bridge.  Hence the fifth coordinate is absent unless that finite
submission record is later added.

Finally, finite-coordinate determination,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, forbids recovering a
missing coordinate from another projection.  Since the post-inventory rerun and
digest sequence changes only the first projection, it closes exactly the local
current-byte support claim and leaves the external-support, fresh formal-source,
dynamic artifact-semantic, and upload-time venue/completed-submission upgrades
uninstantiated.  This proves the stated normal form for the current package.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current no-receipt support-surface non-escalation]
\label{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}
In the current source package the records
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md},
\path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json},
\path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}, and
\path{theorem_inventory.json} contain no venue upload receipt, public DOI, or
institutional archive identifier for \path{review_bundle/}.  They do record the
public automath branch/path coordinate as an archive-equivalent locator, but only
under matching file-list, digest, manifest, and path-semantics tests.  Hence every
claim whose evidence surface is a bundle-local path is accepted only as a
conditional exact-supplemental-inclusion or matching archive-equivalent claim.
Such a claim becomes an externally instantiated submitted-support claim only
after one of the two finite records below is present on the submitted support
surface:
\begin{enumerate}
\item an upload receipt naming the exact \path{review_bundle/} directory and the
final digest manifest; or
\item an archive-equivalent locator satisfying the file-list, digest, manifest,
and path-semantics tests of
Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence}.
\end{enumerate}
Until then, the theorem inventory, verifier logs, case snapshots, source
snapshot, and primary-claim inventory remain local/path-verified review-bundle
coordinates rather than unconditional public or venue-submitted coordinates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The four named files are the only finite records in the present source package
that select the support branch for \path{review_bundle/}: the digest manifest
gives the byte-level package identity, the review-bundle manifest gives the
submission strategy, the pass-record ledger exposes the accepted finite gates,
and \path{theorem_inventory.json} is the theorem-ledger coordinate.  Their
recorded branch is exact supplemental inclusion and their archive fields state
that no archive replacement or locator is claimed.  Therefore they determine the
bytes and paths that must be supplied, but they do not determine that a venue
upload, DOI minting event, institutional archiving event, or archive-equivalent
publication event has occurred.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}, an externally
instantiated bundle-backed claim needs exactly the missing external coordinate:
either an upload record for the exact directory and final digest manifest, or a
replacement archive record passing
Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence}.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, the digest manifest
alone is not such a coordinate.  If neither finite record is present, promoting a
bundle-local path to an unconditional submitted-support coordinate would add an
evidence coordinate not contained in the support surface, contrary to
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  The stated
conditional boundary follows for every bundle-backed surface named in the
corollary.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fresh inventory digest instance for this source state]
\label{cor:fresh-inventory-digest-instance-this-source-state}
In the present source state, the regenerated files
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} are closed as local
exact-inclusion coordinates only after their SHA-256 rows in
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} are recomputed from the bytes of
those two files and the finite command-boundary table names that refreshed
manifest state.  This corollary supplies no upload receipt, archive locator,
extractor-completeness certificate, or semantic proof check; it supplies only the
local byte-coordinate instance required by
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-theorem-inventory-digest-instance}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
There are two relevant file coordinates, namely
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  For each
coordinate the SHA-256 computation is a deterministic function of the finite byte
string stored at that relative path.  Replacing the rows in
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} by the values computed after the
inventory regeneration therefore makes the digest manifest name the regenerated
bytes rather than a prior or anticipated inventory state.  The command-boundary
table is the only place in the manuscript where command-run and freshness claims
are promoted beyond path names, so updating that table to the same refreshed
state prevents a stale 2026-06-05 package description from being read as the
current digest instance.  The argument uses only byte equality at the two named
paths and the finite-record boundary of
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}; it does not add an extractor
run, external support-surface instantiation, upload event, archive event, or
semantic validation.  Hence exactly the local digest-closure claim stated above
is obtained.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record digest-refresh invariant for final package claims]
\label{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}
For the current presentation package, any claim that a submitted support surface
has exact final digests is accepted only for a closed finite state $D$ satisfying
all of the following conditions.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The digest manifest \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} contains
SHA-256 rows for \path{main.tex}, \path{submission_abstract.tex},
\path{references.bib}, \path{source_interface_record.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md}, and every file in
the selected \path{review_bundle/} support directory.
\item The digest rows are computed after the accepted versions of
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json}, and every verifier log named
by a command-run claim have been written.
\item If \path{submission_abstract.tex} is edited after the primary-claim
inventory was checked, then
\path{review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py} is rerun and its fresh
log replaces the old primary-inventory freshness coordinate before the final
digest rows are recomputed.
\item If an upload-time venue-compliance claim, rather than a dated local
readiness observation, is made, the venue and bibliography check is rerun at the
upload rule state and the fresh venue record is included before the final digest
rows are recomputed.
\end{enumerate}
If any one of these conditions fails, the package still has the local
path-verified records printed in the manuscript, but it does not have an exact
final-digest certificate for the regenerated inventory, primary-claim, or
upload-time venue component that failed the condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The support-surface certificate is byte-level: by
Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}, exact inclusion and
archive-equivalent inclusion both read the finite file list, relative paths, and
SHA-256 content rows rather than prose descriptions of those files.  Therefore a
file written after the digest manifest was computed cannot be covered by that
manifest; its byte string was not one of the inputs to the listed hash values.
This proves the necessity of recomputing the digest rows after regenerating the
theorem inventory, primary-claim inventory, and command logs named by the final
package.

The primary-claim inventory is line-span dependent.  Its verifier reads the
current \path{submission_abstract.tex}, checks the row-id set and line ranges,
and prints a finite freshness log.  If the primary source is changed after that
run, at least the source line-span premise of the old log is no longer the
current primary source checked by the verifier.  A fresh verifier run before the
digest pass restores a finite coordinate for the new primary state; omitting it
leaves only the old path-verified inventory observation.

Venue compliance is external-state dependent by
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}.  A dated venue log can
witness local readiness at its observation time, but upload-time compliance
requires a record of the rule state at upload or an included replacement record.
Thus a package that claims upload-time venue compliance must write that fresh
record before the digest closure step; otherwise the digest manifest can cover
only the dated local-readiness file, not the missing upload-time premise.

Combining these observations gives a finite fixed-point condition: first write
the accepted inventory files and freshness logs, then compute the manifest over
those bytes, and finally submit either the exact directory or an
archive-equivalent replacement.  If a later edit or upload-time claim changes one
of the inputs, the fixed point is broken precisely at that finite subrecord.  The
remaining local rows remain available at their declared evidence levels, but the
stronger exact final-digest claim is not accepted for the changed component.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Finite-record submission-support refresh invariant]
\label{thm:submission-support-refresh-rigidity}
Let $S$ be a source package for this presentation route, and suppose $S$ changes
one of the following four support coordinates after the last accepted digest
manifest was written:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the theorem-obligation inventory bytes in \path{theorem_inventory.json} or
\path{theorem_inventory.md};
\item a verifier or extractor log used to support a command-result claim;
\item the primary-source line-span coordinate checked by
\path{review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}; or
\item the asserted venue-status coordinate, upgraded from dated local readiness to
upload-time venue compliance.
\end{enumerate}
Then the strongest certificate available from the old manifest is obtained by
deleting the changed coordinate from the claimed support tuple.  The changed
coordinate re-enters the publication-safety chain only after the corresponding
post-change extractor, verifier, or venue-rule record is written and the digest
manifest is regenerated over those new bytes.  In particular, a post-inventory
edit cannot be certified by a pre-inventory digest row, a dated local-readiness
venue log cannot certify upload-time compliance, and a local bundle manifest
cannot certify external upload or archive equivalence without the separate
external coordinate of Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All four listed coordinates are finite byte or rule-state fields in the support
surface.  For item~1, the theorem-obligation ledger is exactly the ordered pair
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md}, together with the
extractor coverage row that reads those files.  If either inventory file is
edited after the digest manifest was computed, the old SHA--256 row is a hash of
a different byte string.  Since SHA--256 rows in this paper are used only as
content-addressed finite records, not as semantic proof obligations, the old row
cannot denote the new inventory bytes.  The coordinate is therefore absent until
the extractor is rerun on the new inventory and the digest table is recomputed
after that new log exists.

For item~2, Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} make every command-result claim
depend on the finite tuple consisting of command, source state, environment,
exit code, and log path.  A changed extractor or verifier log changes the log
byte string selected by that tuple.  The old manifest can still witness the old
run as historical local evidence, but it cannot be a digest certificate for the
new run because the new log was not an input to the old hash table.

For item~3, the primary-claim verifier reads the current
\path{submission_abstract.tex} and records row and line-span facts.  If the
primary source changes after that verifier run, the line-span coordinate checked
by the old log is no longer the current primary-source coordinate.  The only
finite repair is to rerun the primary-claim verifier and then include the fresh
log in the regenerated digest manifest.

For item~4, venue compliance is a time- and rule-state-dependent coordinate by
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}.  A dated local-readiness
record states what was observed at its logged date.  Upload-time compliance is a
different finite field: it requires the rule state and submission state at the
upload event.  Therefore an old local-readiness log cannot be reinterpreted as
that upload-time field; a fresh venue-rule record must be written before digest
closure if the stronger claim is made.

Finally, external upload or archive equivalence is independent of the local
inventory and digest coordinates.  Theorems~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} require either an
exact supplemental-upload record or a byte-equality archive locator.  None of the
four local refresh steps supplies such an external coordinate.  Thus the old
manifest proves the package only after projecting away the changed or missing
field, and the full support tuple is restored exactly by writing the required
post-change finite records and regenerating the manifest over them.
\end{proof}


\begin{proposition}[Primary architectural fallback without external support]
\label{prop:primary-architectural-fallback-without-external-support}
Assume the current source package is used without an upload receipt for the exact
\path{review_bundle/} directory and without an archive-equivalent replacement
satisfying Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence}.  Then the
primary presentation article may assert only the source-level architecture and
path-verified local-package claims whose evidence surfaces are visible outside the
missing bundle.  In particular, the theorem-ledger claim of
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary}, the case-snapshot claims,
the verifier-log claims, and any claim whose certificate coordinate is
\path{theorem_inventory.json} or a file under \path{review_bundle/} cannot be
read as externally submitted evidence.  If either accepted external instantiation
record is later supplied, the same claims re-enter exactly at the finite evidence
level stated in their certificate rows and not at any stronger semantic or venue
acceptance level.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation} identifies
the only two records that can externally instantiate a bundle-backed support
claim: an exact upload receipt for \path{review_bundle/} with the final digest
manifest, or an archive-equivalent locator passing the finite file-list, digest,
manifest, and path-semantics tests.  Under the present hypothesis neither record
is available.  Hence every bundle-local path is absent from the externally
submitted finite support surface.

The affected claims are precisely those whose certificate coordinate names such a
path.  Table~\ref{tab:submitted-theorem-obligation-ledger} places the manual
theorem inventory at \path{theorem_inventory.json} and exposes it through
\path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}; the case-snapshot and
verifier-log statements similarly name files under \path{review_bundle/}.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a claim cannot acquire
an evidence coordinate that is absent from the finite support surface.  Therefore
those claims cannot be read as externally submitted evidence while both accepted
instantiation records are missing.

Removing that external reading does not remove the primary article's independent
architectural assertion.  The primary text describes the compiler's typed record
interface and cites the pinned public source surface; those claims do not require
the missing bundle-local coordinate.  If a valid exact-upload or
archive-equivalent record is later supplied, Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} put the
bundle-backed claims back into the finite support surface.  The reinstatement is
only at the recorded evidence levels, because the same corollaries and
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary} exclude stronger
readings such as semantic proof checking, fresh dynamic validation, venue
compliance, or acceptance.\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic theorem-environment extractor boundary]
\label{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}
Let the theorem-like environment domain $\mathcal E$ for this package consist
of the five environment names \path{definition}, \path{lemma},
\path{proposition}, \path{theorem}, and \path{corollary}.  The command
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} run on
\path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json} is a deterministic
syntactic extractor for the following finite claim only: every labelled
environment in \path{main.tex} whose environment name belongs to $\mathcal E$ is
listed by label in \path{theorem_inventory.json}; every such environment is
labelled; and no such label is duplicated.  When the refreshed run log
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log} records exit code
\path{0}, the package has a deterministic theorem-environment coverage
certificate at this syntactic label level.  The certificate does not assert that
the inventory is a semantic proof checker, that the printed proofs are correct,
that external Lean or BEDC semantics were rebuilt, or that theorem-like material
outside $\mathcal E$ is covered.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The extractor is a finite program whose inputs are exactly the two byte strings
at \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}.  It scans the source lines
for beginnings of the five displayed environment names, records the first
\path{\textbackslash label\{...\}} before the matching end of the same
environment, and forms the finite set $T$ of recorded labels together with line
numbers, titles, and environment names.  It also reads the inventory JSON and
forms the finite set $I$ of labels appearing in inventory label fields with one
of the package theorem-label prefixes.  These operations are deterministic
functions of the two input byte strings.

The script exits with code \path{0} exactly when three finite tests pass: there
is no element of $\mathcal E$ without a label, no duplicate label in $T$, and
$T\subseteq I$.  Therefore a refreshed exit-code-zero log proves precisely the
syntactic coverage assertion: every labelled theorem-like environment in the
chosen domain has a corresponding inventory label and the source labels are
well-formed for this comparison.  If any test fails, the printed missing-label,
duplicate-label, or omitted-from-inventory list is the finite bad subrecord.

No step of this computation parses mathematical statements, checks proofs,
invokes Lean, consults the publication daemon, or validates external artifacts.
Thus the certificate is stronger than the earlier manual ledger at the single
point needed by the scope contract---deterministic environment-label coverage---
and no stronger than that.  The semantic and implementation boundaries remain
those of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-record-gate-soundness-boundary}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Extractor-domain exactness and non-gluing]
\label{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}
For the submitted theorem-inventory surface, the command
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} is exact for one
domain and impossible to glue beyond that domain without an added finite
coordinate.  Its exact domain is the syntactic label-coverage predicate on
\[
\mathcal E=\{\texttt{definition},\texttt{lemma},\texttt{proposition},
\texttt{theorem},\texttt{corollary}\}.
\]
An exit-code-zero run proves precisely that the source has no unlabelled
environment in $\mathcal E$, no duplicate label among those environments, and no
labelled environment in $\mathcal E$ omitted from \path{theorem_inventory.json}.
It proves no audit-record coverage, statement-semantics coverage,
proof-correctness coverage, Lean/BEDC rebuild, artifact validation, daemon run,
or venue-state fact.  Any manuscript reading that adds one of those conclusions
is a properly stronger reading of the theorem-inventory coordinate and is
accepted only after the submitted surface adds the corresponding parser domain,
semantic checker, proof checker, build log, artifact log, daemon log, or venue
record with assigned pass rows.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The script definition fixes the domain: its \path{THEOREM_ENVS} tuple contains
exactly the five displayed names, and its begin-pattern is built from that tuple.
The extraction loop records only occurrences of those begins in \path{main.tex},
then searches within the matched environment for the first \path{\label{...}}
token.  The inventory side reads only label strings from
\path{theorem_inventory.json}.  Thus the finite predicate computed by the script
has exactly three positive clauses: every detected environment in $\mathcal E$
has a label, the detected labels are not duplicated, and the detected label set
is contained in the inventory label set.  Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}
therefore gives exactness on this syntactic domain.

Each proposed extension reads a coordinate absent from that computation.  Audit
records use a different LaTeX environment counter and are not in $\mathcal E$;
statement semantics would require a parser and meaning relation for theorem
bodies; proof correctness would require a proof checker or a formal build;
Lean/BEDC rebuilding, artifact validation, daemon execution, and venue state each
require their own command, source state, environment, exit code, and log or
external record.  Two package states can agree on \path{main.tex} labels in
$\mathcal E$ and on \path{theorem_inventory.json} while differing in any of
those absent coordinates.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary},
the extractor's accepted finite record cannot determine such a stronger fact.

Finally, in the stronger-reading preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}, adding any of the excluded
conclusions enlarges the claim-kind, evidence-surface, command-boundary, or
assigned-gate coordinate.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}
then supplies the positive direction: once the enlarged parser domain, semantic
checker, proof checker, build log, artifact log, daemon log, or venue record and
its pass rows are included, that stronger coordinate may be checked by the
finite interface.  Without those additions,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} returns the missing
coordinate as a finite bad subrecord.  Hence the extractor is exact and maximal
for syntactic label coverage over $\mathcal E$, and it cannot be glued into any
semantic, auditrecord, implementation, artifact, daemon, or venue certificate by
prose alone.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Final-byte extractor inventory inclusion]
\label{thm:final-byte-extractor-inventory-inclusion}
Fix a manuscript source byte string $M$, an inventory byte string $J$, and the
extractor byte string
\path{review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py}.  Let $T(M)$ be the finite
set of labels obtained by running that extractor on the five-environment domain
$\mathcal E$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
and let $I(J)$ be the finite set of inventory labels read from $J$ with the
accepted theorem-label prefixes.  For the final bytes of this package, a
zero-exit extractor run is equivalent to the following three finite conditions:
\[
  T(M)\subseteq I(J),
  \qquad \text{no element of }\mathcal E\text{ in }M\text{ is unlabelled},
  \qquad \text{and }T(M)\text{ has no duplicate source label}.
\]
Consequently, after any edit to \path{main.tex} or \path{theorem_inventory.json},
the exact theorem-obligation ledger coordinate used by
Theorems~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary} and
\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} is available only from a fresh
zero-exit run on those final bytes.  This inclusion criterion is the complete
bad-example obstruction for missing in-domain labels: an omitted labelled
environment, an unlabelled in-domain environment, or a duplicate in-domain label
is witnessed by a finite failing row printed by the extractor, and no prose
inventory statement can remove that row without changing $M$, $J$, or the
extractor coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first two input byte strings determine the two finite sets.  The extractor
constructs $T(M)$ by a line scan for begins of the five names in $\mathcal E$,
searches each matched environment body for its first label token, and records the
label together with its line and title fields.  It constructs $I(J)$ by reading
the inventory JSON and collecting the finite label fields with the accepted
prefixes.  Since these operations use only fixed regular expressions and JSON
parsing on finite byte strings, $T(M)$, the unlabelled-environment list, the
duplicate-label list, and $I(J)$ are deterministic functions of the final bytes.

The extractor's acceptance test is exactly the conjunction of the three displayed
conditions.  If an in-domain environment has no label, the unlabelled list is
nonempty and the command exits nonzero.  If two in-domain environments have the
same label, the duplicate list is nonempty and the command exits nonzero.  If a
recorded source label is absent from the inventory, then the set difference
$T(M)\setminus I(J)$ is nonempty and the command exits nonzero.  Conversely, when
all three lists are empty and $T(M)\subseteq I(J)$, the extractor has no failing
row for its declared predicate and exits with code zero.  This proves the stated
equivalence.

It remains to connect the equivalence to the paper's support-coordinate chain.
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary} uses the inventory only as a
finite theorem-obligation ledger plus the syntactic extractor coordinate, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} requires that the inventory,
extractor run, verifier logs, and final digest be ordered after the final source
bytes are selected.  Editing either $M$ or $J$ changes one of the deterministic
inputs just described.  The exact ledger coordinate for the edited package
therefore requires the fresh zero-exit run on those edited bytes; otherwise the
package has at most the weaker path-verified or stale-coordinate reading already
classified in Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-support-coordinate-dichotomy}.

The bad-example statement follows from the same finite disjunction.  Each failure
mode is represented by an explicit finite row: an unlabelled environment, a
duplicate label, or a member of $T(M)\setminus I(J)$.  Because
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} allows the submitted
claim to depend only on recorded finite coordinates, prose cannot erase such a
row.  Only changing the source bytes, the inventory bytes, or the extractor
coordinate can change the computed obstruction.  Thus the theorem gives the
final-byte inclusion gate required for the post-inventory theorem chain and no
semantic proof-checking, Lean/BEDC rebuild, artifact, daemon, upload, or venue
claim beyond that syntactic gate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem-inventory proof-checker obstruction]
\label{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction}
Let $\mathcal E$ be the five-environment domain
\{\path{definition}, \path{lemma}, \path{proposition}, \path{theorem},
\path{corollary}\} in \path{main.tex}.  The finite theorem-inventory support
surface consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
and the output of \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py}
classifies exactly labelled-environment coverage in $\mathcal E$: every labelled
environment in $\mathcal E$ is present in the inventory, no such label is missing
or duplicated, and no inventory conclusion glues to material outside that domain.
It is not a proof checker.  Any stronger reading that validates proof semantics,
checks theorem statements against Lean or BEDC, covers other TeX environments,
covers \path{submission_abstract.tex}, validates remarks or audit records, or
certifies artifact or venue facts is accepted by this calculus if and only if the
support surface is extended by a nonempty finite checker coordinate for that
additional domain and by an assigned pass row.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} identifies
the extractor domain as the five classes in $\mathcal E$ and records that the
script reads \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}.  Theorem~\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}
then proves non-gluing: the successful extractor run eliminates exactly the bad
example of a labelled environment in $\mathcal E$ missing from the inventory or a
duplicate label in that same syntactic domain, and it says nothing about other
files, environments, proof semantics, or external artifacts.

To see that no proof-checking conclusion follows, fix two TeX states with the
same sequence of labelled $\mathcal E$ environments and the same inventory rows,
but with different proof bodies for one theorem.  For example, replace a proof
body by another body while leaving the surrounding \path{\textbackslash begin}
line, label, environment kind, and inventory row unchanged.  The extractor reads
only the syntactic environment record and the inventory labels, so it returns the
same coverage result on both states.  A semantic proof checker could distinguish
the states, but that checker output is not part of the finite projection.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a semantic theorem
validation claim is therefore not determined by the inventory support surface.

The same argument applies to every listed stronger domain: each requires reading
at least one new file, environment class, proof-assistant state, artifact log, or
venue record that is absent from the extractor projection.  Hence each stronger
reading has a finite bad subrecord unless a new checker coordinate and assigned
pass row are submitted.  Conversely, once that coordinate is submitted, the claim
is no longer a gluing inference from the old inventory; it is a separate finite
extension governed by Theorem~\ref{thm:record-interface-rigidity}.  This proves
both exact syntactic coverage and the proof-checker obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem-inventory boundary]
\label{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary}
This theorem retains the legacy cross-reference label
\path{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} for compatibility with earlier
acceptance-ledger entries; its environment category is \path{theorem}, not
\path{proposition}.
The file \path{theorem_inventory.json} is a theorem-obligation inventory record whose
current support has two finite parts.  First, it is an obligation ledger selected
by finite-record review and connected to the manifest and acceptance ledger.  Second,
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} supplies a
deterministic syntactic comparison between the labelled theorem-like environments
in the five-environment domain $\mathcal E$ and the labels appearing in the
inventory.  The inventory indexes obligations; the evidence for those obligations
is supplied by the corresponding TeX statements and proofs in this source,
together with external records only where a statement explicitly cites them.  It
is not a semantic proof checker and it is not an executable completeness
certificate for theorem-like material outside $\mathcal E$.  Consequently any
claim that the ledger itself semantically checks the printed proofs, reruns Lean
or BEDC, validates artifacts, or certifies an external venue state is rejected by
the current finite-record interface, while the bounded obligation-ledger and
syntactic environment-label coverage claims are accepted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The support records named in Table~\ref{tab:submitted-theorem-obligation-ledger}
are finite manifest and ledger records.  The root manifest exposes the path
\path{theorem_inventory.json}; acceptance-ledger entry \path{a7} records the
inventory, marker-existence, theorem-environment extraction, and submission-pack
gates for the bounded theorem-ledger claim; and the certificate verifier checks
only record shape, gate coverage, evidence pointers, and file availability.  The
new extractor coordinates add a command, source state, environment, exit code,
and log path for syntactic label coverage in the domain $\mathcal E$.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}, those
coordinates prove only that all labelled environments in the chosen domain are
represented by labels in the inventory and that no source label is missing or
duplicated.

The remaining boundary is semantic, not syntactic.  A finite inventory can still
be useful because it fixes the Stage-A obligation surface that the submission
chooses to expose and lets the certificate ledger prevent hidden prose-only
references to that surface.  The extractor strengthens this by eliminating one
bad example: an environment in $\mathcal E$ whose label exists in \path{main.tex}
but is absent from the inventory.  Once the extractor log has exit code
\path{0}, that bad example cannot occur.  Finite-coordinate determination is
still exact, however.  The accepted records are manifest, ledger, table, and
syntactic extractor coordinates; they cannot imply a nonrecorded semantic
theorem checker, nonrecorded Lean rebuild, nonrecorded daemon run, or nonrecorded
artifact validation.  Hence the finite interface accepts the obligation ledger
together with deterministic syntactic environment-label coverage and rejects
every stronger proof-checking or implementation-soundness reading.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Regenerated theorem-inventory digest closure]
\label{prop:regenerated-theorem-inventory-digest-closure}
Suppose a theorem-inventory pass regenerates either \path{theorem_inventory.json} or
\path{theorem_inventory.md} after the package has selected the exact-inclusion
support branch.  Then the final support-surface claims of
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}, the submitted theorem-ledger
claim of Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary}, and the command
boundary of Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory} remain closed
only under the fixed-point conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}: the package refreshes the
corresponding SHA-256 rows in \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md},
reruns the finite record verifiers and the theorem-environment extractor whose
records name that digest manifest or inventory coordinate, and does not promote
primary-claim or venue-compliance rows beyond the fresh records actually
included.  Once those rows and logs are refreshed, the regeneration creates no
new mathematical, Lean, daemon, or artifact claim: it only changes the
byte-coordinate of the theorem-obligation ledger and its syntactic label-coverage
certificate inside the already selected finite support surface.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The selected support branch is byte-level exact inclusion.  In that branch,
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} identifies the submitted support
surface by relative paths together with the digest rows in
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  The theorem inventory is one of
those paths: Table~\ref{tab:submitted-theorem-obligation-ledger} exposes
\path{theorem_inventory.json} through the root manifest and acceptance-ledger
entry \path{a7}, while the final digest record also lists the human-readable
companion \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Therefore regenerating either file after
the digest record was written changes a finite coordinate used by the exact
support-surface relation.  Until the SHA-256 rows are recomputed, the digest
record denotes the old bytes, and the regenerated inventory is not the same
finite certificate file as the one named by the final packaging record.

The required reruns are exactly the finite record verifiers and extractor at the
package boundary.  The certificate-record verifier checks that the
manifest-required paths, including the theorem-inventory coordinate, are present
and covered by the accepted gate records; the source-interface and primary-claim
verifiers record their command boundary against the same final digest manifest;
and the theorem-environment extractor compares labelled environments in
$\mathcal E$ with the inventory labels.  Rerunning those commands after the
digest refresh supplies fresh source state, environment, exit code, and log-path
coordinates for the command-boundary table.  No verifier in this list proves
theorem semantics.  Hence the refreshed state is closed precisely as a finite
record-and-digest package with deterministic syntactic label coverage, and by
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} it remains a
non-semantic theorem-obligation ledger rather than a proof-checking certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current theorem-inventory digest instance]
\label{cor:current-theorem-inventory-digest-instance}
For the present local support package, after \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} have been regenerated, the submitted
theorem-obligation ledger may be cited in
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary} only through the refreshed
digest rows for those two files in \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}
and through fresh finite-record verifier logs produced after the regenerated
inventory files are present.  If either the two digest rows or the
post-regeneration verifier logs are absent, the
inventory remains a local index but is not closed as an exact-inclusion
support coordinate for the bundle-backed theorem-ledger claim.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:regenerated-theorem-inventory-digest-closure} to the
two regenerated inventory files in this package.  The support branch selected by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention} is exact inclusion, so the
identity of each submitted support file is read from the corresponding
relative-path and SHA-256 row in \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary} uses
\path{theorem_inventory.json} as the theorem-ledger coordinate and uses
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} only for
syntactic label coverage.  Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary}
excludes every stronger semantic-proof reading.  Therefore the only new fact
needed after regeneration is byte-coordinate and command-coordinate closure: the
digest rows must name the new bytes, and the finite verifiers and extractor whose
records mention the digest or inventory coordinate must be rerun against the
package state in which the regenerated inventory files exist.  Without those rows
and logs, the ledger is still a local file, but the exact-inclusion support
relation points either to stale bytes or to an unverifiable command-boundary
state.  With them, no additional mathematical, Lean, daemon, or artifact claim is
introduced; the refreshed package supplies exactly the finite support coordinate
used by the submitted theorem-obligation ledger.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Inventory-synchronized support certificate]
\label{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}
In the present package state, the two regenerated theorem-inventory files are
accepted by the exact-inclusion theorem-ledger chain only at the following
finite fixed point: the rows of
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} name

Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary}.  If any one of the two
inventory digest rows or four refreshed command-log rows is replaced by a
