\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The statement is a finite-coordinate instance of
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}.  The first named coordinate
is \path{theorem_inventory.json}, and the second is
\path{theorem_inventory.md}; after regeneration, each coordinate is identified
inside the exact-inclusion surface only by the SHA-256 row attached to its
current byte string in \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  The four
command-run coordinates are exactly the finite verifier and extractor logs listed
in Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}: the certificate-record verifier,
the source-interface record verifier, the primary-claim inventory verifier, and
the theorem-environment extractor.  The same table records command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path, and its boundary column states that these
are record or syntactic label-coverage checks rather than Lean, daemon, Rule110,
upload, or semantic validation runs.

If the five rows are current, the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:regenerated-theorem-inventory-digest-closure} are met for
the regenerated inventory files and for the verifier and extractor records whose
logs name the digest or inventory boundary.
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-theorem-inventory-digest-instance} then supplies
exactly the local fixed-point instance needed by the theorem-obligation ledger in

one of the two inventory digest rows is stale.  Then the digest manifest denotes

four command-log rows is stale.  Then the command-boundary table promotes a
fresh verifier invocation while the digest surface still names an earlier log
file, so the command-run coordinate is not closed in the selected byte surface.
In either case the bad subrecord is finite: it is the stale row together with

Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} still permits the

\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record post-inventory realization invariant]
\label{thm:post-inventory-finite-record-realization}
Suppose the following finite records are present in the current source package and
read by the declared theorem-ledger support schema:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md};
\item a zero-exit log for
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} computed after those
two files were written;
\item zero-exit logs for
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py} computed against the
same post-inventory package state; and
\item a regenerated \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} whose rows name
the two inventory files and the four log files just listed; and
\item either no external-support claim is made, or an exact supplemental-upload
receipt or archive-equivalence byte-equality locator is supplied separately for
this same support surface.
\end{enumerate}
Then the first coordinate in
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} is instantiated as
a local exact-inclusion theorem-ledger support coordinate, and as an external
support coordinate only in the second branch of item~5.  The instantiated
coordinate is exactly syntactic inventory coverage plus finite-record verifier
closure: it is not a semantic proof check, a Lean rebuild, a daemon run, an
artifact rerun, a venue upload receipt, or an archive-equivalent locator.  If one
of the first four listed conditions is absent, the theorem-inventory files remain
at most local historical indices and cannot support the exact-inclusion
theorem-ledger claim; if item~5 is in its no-external-support branch, the same
coordinate remains local/path-verified only.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof is by finite-coordinate determination.  The first condition supplies
the two byte strings that are to be accepted as the theorem-ledger inventory.
The second condition supplies the only syntactic coverage test used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}: the
extractor reads \path{main.tex}, extracts theorem-like labels, and compares them
with labels present in \path{theorem_inventory.json}.  The third condition
supplies the companion finite-record checks for the certificate ledger, the
source-interface record, and the primary-claim inventory.  The fourth condition
places the resulting bytes and logs into the selected exact-inclusion digest
surface.  The fifth condition fixes the support-surface status of that coordinate:
either it is read only as local/path-verified support, or the package separately
supplies the upload receipt or archive-equivalence byte-equality locator required
by Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.

Under all four conditions, every finite coordinate named in
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} is present:
the inventory-file coordinates are identified by SHA-256 rows, and the extractor
and verifier coordinates are identified by their zero-exit command logs and
digest rows.  Therefore
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-theorem-inventory-digest-instance} applies, giving the
local exact-inclusion support coordinate used in the first clause of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.  The fifth
condition prevents this local coordinate from being re-read as external support
unless the separate external-support finite field is present.  The boundary of
the coordinate is the intersection of the boundaries of its inputs: the
extractor is syntactic label coverage only, the three verifiers are finite-record
checks only, and the digest manifest is a byte-coordinate manifest only.  None of
these records contains a proof-assistant rebuild, publication-daemon run,
artifact validation rerun, external upload receipt, or archive locator, so no
such stronger coordinate can be inferred.

Conversely, omit any one condition.  If the inventory files are absent, there is
no byte string for the theorem-ledger row.  If the extractor log is absent or
pre-inventory, syntactic coverage is not recorded for the current inventory
bytes.  If any finite-record verifier log is absent or pre-inventory, the
corresponding support record is not closed against the same package state.  If
the digest manifest is not regenerated over the inventory files and logs, the
exact-inclusion surface names stale or missing byte coordinates.  If the fifth
condition is the no-external-support branch, any external-support reading is
missing the upload-or-archive coordinate named by
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  In each case
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} rejects the stronger
reading and leaves only whatever local historical or local/path-verified index was
actually recorded.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Seven-row submitted theorem-obligation ledger integration]
\label{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary}
Let $P^{+}_{7}$ be the seven-row support state obtained from $P^{+}_{6}$
by the conservative finite-record extension of
Theorem~\ref{thm:nested-package-states}, namely by adding exactly the submitted theorem-ledger coordinate \path{a7}.  In
$P^{+}_{7}$, the theorem-obligation ledger is no longer a detached review-only
artifact: the submitted finite support surface contains
\path{theorem_inventory.json} through the manifest field \path{theorem_inventory}
and through acceptance-ledger entry \path{a7}.  The earlier six-row state
$P^{+}_{6}$ of Theorems~\ref{thm:nested-package-states}
and~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} remains
the row-frozen certificate state for \path{a1}--\path{a6}; the present theorem
adds exactly the theorem-ledger coordinate \path{a7}.  Consequently the
package may make
the following bounded theorem-ledger claim: every theorem-obligation assertion
made by the submission is supported only through the finite coordinates in
Table~\ref{tab:submitted-theorem-obligation-ledger}, namely the integrated
theorem inventory, the primary-claim inventory, the certificate ledger, and the
manifest exposure records.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:manual-ledger-dependence-boundary}, this is a theorem-obligation ledger claim with deterministic syntactic
theorem-environment label coverage, not a semantic proof-checking or
implementation-soundness claim.  The claim does not assert that
\path{theorem_inventory.json} proves the mathematical semantics of each theorem,
does not replace the proofs printed in this source, and does not certify a Lean
rebuild, publication-daemon run, Rule110 artifact rerun, semantic extractor
completeness beyond $\mathcal E$, or external upload.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The support surface is finite and can be inspected coordinate by coordinate.
The root manifest now contains the key \path{theorem_inventory} with value
\path{theorem_inventory.json}.  The certificate schema includes the same key in
its required manifest-file map.  Therefore a certificate-record verification of
the enlarged package must check that the manifest exposes this root-level
inventory path and that the file is present.  This removes the previous
possibility of silently citing a root-level theorem-inventory artifact outside the support
surface.

The acceptance ledger contains the additional entry \path{a7}.  Its accepted
claim is exactly the bounded submitted theorem-obligation ledger claim; its
claim kinds are \path{traceability} and \path{submission}.  Under the schema's
gate dispatch, those kinds require the inventory, marker-existence, and
submission-pack gates; the theorem-extractor check is an additional command
boundary attached to the marker-existence gate.  Entry \path{a7} supplies the
required pass records: the inventory gate points to \path{theorem_inventory.json},
the marker-existence gate points to
Table~\ref{tab:submitted-theorem-obligation-ledger} and the extractor log, and
the submission-pack gate points to \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}.  Thus the
ledger supplies a finite route from the theorem-inventory file to the submitted
certificate records rather than a prose-only reference.

It remains to identify the boundary.  The schema-level verifier checks finite
record shape, required manifest paths, gate coverage, evidence pointers, and
evidence levels.  None of those checks is a semantic proof of the theorem-like
environments in this source, and none reruns Lean, the publication daemon, or the
Rule110/GroundCompiler artifacts.  The independent theorem-environment extractor
only supplies the syntactic coverage certificate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}.
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:manual-ledger-dependence-boundary} supply the remaining
classification: the inventory is an accepted Stage-A ledger with syntactic label
coverage and not an executable semantic completeness certificate.  The theorem-ledger claim is
therefore admissible only at the path-verified evidence level stated in
\path{a7}.  The mathematical content of the article remains carried by the
printed definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs, and external
records carry only the finite evidence claims that cite them.  The integrated
inventory gives the submitted finite obligation surface against which those
theorem-like claims are enumerated; it indexes the obligations and does not prove
them.  This is exactly the bounded claim stated in the theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Post-inventory support-tuple extraction certificate]
\label{prop:post-inventory-support-tuple-extraction-certificate}
For the current source package, the theorem-ledger support tuple is accepted only
in the post-inventory form consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  In that form the extraction log must be generated after the two inventory files
exist, the pass-record ledger must contain the theorem-ledger certificate entry,
and the digest manifest must be regenerated after those three records are in
place.  A digest manifest whose inventory rows predate any member of this tuple
does not certify the current theorem-ledger support coordinate; it certifies only
the earlier local byte state named by its rows.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The tuple has five finite coordinates.  The first two are the regenerated manual
inventory files.  The third is the syntactic extractor output: by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}, the
extractor reads \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json} and records
only labelled theorem-like environment coverage.  The fourth is the finite
certificate ledger entry for the theorem-obligation surface described in
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary}.  The fifth is the digest
manifest used by Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure} to identify the
bytes available under exact supplemental inclusion.

If the five coordinates are produced in the stated order, every support claim
about the regenerated theorem ledger is a function of byte strings already fixed
before the digest pass: the inventory bytes are read by the extractor, the
theorem-ledger certificate entry records the finite support route, and the digest
manifest hashes the resulting files and log.  The support tuple is therefore a
finite coordinate of the package.  If, however, the digest rows for
\path{theorem_inventory.json} or \path{theorem_inventory.md} are older than the
accepted inventory, or if the extractor or pass-record ledger is written after
the digest manifest, then one of the bytes used by the theorem-ledger claim is
not among the bytes hashed by the manifest.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, the stronger current
support claim cannot be inferred from a finite record that omits that coordinate.
Thus the old digest remains evidence only for the earlier local byte state and
not for the post-inventory support tuple stated here.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current local-support normal form]
\label{cor:current-local-support-normal-form}
For the current presentation package, the finite support state has exactly the
following normal form.  The theorem-inventory coordinate is accepted only through
the post-regeneration digest-and-verifier fixed point of
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}; the
review-bundle coordinate is externally instantiated only under exact upload or
matching public branch/path bytes, because

records no upload receipt and makes the archive-equivalent locator
byte-conditioned; and the venue and
bibliography coordinate is only the dated local-readiness record of
Proposition~\ref{prop:dated-venue-record-instantiation}, not an upload-time
venue-compliance certificate.  Consequently every bundle-backed theorem-ledger,
case-evidence, verifier-log, source-interface, and primary-claim-inventory claim
in this package is a local/path-verified exact-inclusion claim unless a later
submitted support surface adds both an accepted upload-or-archive instantiation
record and, for venue compliance, an upload-time or unchanged-rule venue record.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The three named coordinates are disjoint finite fields of the support record.
For the theorem-inventory field,
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} gives the
necessary and sufficient local fixed point after the regenerated inventory files:
the current byte rows for \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, together with the three current finite-record

ledger.  Replacing any of those rows by a pre-regeneration row leaves only the
manual local index and fails the exact-inclusion theorem-ledger claim.

For the submission-instantiation field,
Proposition~\ref{prop:submission-support-instantiation-field-normal-form} lists
the complete current values: conditional exact supplemental inclusion, absent
upload receipt, a digest-conditioned public branch/path locator, and external
support status only when exact upload or matching branch bytes are present.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}, no
bundle-local path can therefore be promoted to an unconditional public or
venue-submitted coordinate in this package.  For the venue field,
Proposition~\ref{prop:dated-venue-record-instantiation} supplies only the
dated 2026-06-13 live route and bibliography check and explicitly excludes
venue upload, acceptance, proceedings status, archive minting, Lean rebuilds,
and artifact reruns.  Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}
then prevents that dated record from being read as upload-time compliance unless

The finite-coordinate determination theorem applies to the product of these
fields.  A support reading that adds external submission support without the
receipt-or-locator field, or adds upload-time venue compliance without the
required venue field, introduces a coordinate absent from the current record.
Thus the only current normal form is the local/path-verified exact-inclusion one

\medskip

the schema-relative finite-record exactness theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, the same certificate cannot accept
that stronger assertion: its boundary field $B$ records no command-run assertion,
and the missing command tuple is a finite bad subrecord.  Thus the snapshots are

added.

\begin{theorem}[Qualitative finite-row closure of case evidence]
\label{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}
Let $C$ be the finite set of four case-study rows in
Table~\ref{tab:case-witnesses}.  Under
Propositions~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} and
\ref{prop:review-bundle-case-snapshot-coverage}, the publication-safety interface
accepts the case-study contribution exactly as the image of $C$ under the
skeleton map of Theorem~\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity}.  The image has
four possible values only: promotion, route/submission blocking, theorem-content
non-growth, and artifact-limitation disclosure.  For each row, the accepted
claim is finite-record evidence for the corresponding software-workflow lesson;
it is a qualitative illustration using historical/path-snapshot evidence, not empirical validation
of current system behaviour and not evidence that the historical daemon, overlap
checker, fake-extension pipeline, Rule110 artifact system, or GroundCompiler
evaluator has been rerun or semantically validated.  A proposed upgrade of any
row to such a rerun, empirical current-behaviour, or semantic-validation claim is
accepted if and only if it adds the positive
extension coordinates required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}, including command, source
state, environment, exit code, and log path whenever fresh execution is asserted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} gives, for every row in $C$,
the gate name, observed issue, safe lesson, and cited path surface.  Proposition~\ref{prop:review-bundle-case-snapshot-coverage}
places those cited path surfaces inside the reviewable snapshot boundary and
records that the boundary is historical or path-verified.  Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity} therefore maps each row to one
of the four skeleton values listed in the statement, and no fifth skeleton is
available because the table contains only those four gate/lesson forms.

The finite-record interface theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
then accepts only the certificate tuple carried by the row: its claim kind, path
surface, assigned pass rows, and boundary field.  By
Proposition~\ref{audit:case-snapshot-non-rerun-boundary}, that boundary field has
no command-run tuple for a fresh daemon execution, full-source rebuild,
theorem-content rerun, Rule110 rerun, or GroundCompiler semantic rerun.  Hence the
accepted image of $C$ is exactly finite-row evidence for the four safe workflow
lessons and not a live-system measurement, empirical rerun, benchmark, or full
artifact-validation claim.

Conversely, suppose a stronger reading of a case row is accepted.  It changes at
least one finite coordinate: the claim-kind coordinate for a semantic or artifact
validation assertion, the evidence-surface coordinate for a new run or semantic
property, the assigned-gate coordinate for the enlarged gate set, or the boundary
coordinate for command-run strength.  The finite extension-budget normal form,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}, says that exactly these
positive coordinates must be added, and clause A6 of
Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table} supplies the command,
source-state, environment, exit-code, and log-path requirement for fresh
execution.  If any required coordinate is absent, the schema exactness theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, returns a finite bad subrecord
instead of accepting the upgrade.  This proves both finite-row closure and the
upgrade criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current case-behaviour evidence criterion]
\label{cor:current-case-behaviour-evidence-criterion}
The four case-study rows support current-behaviour claims only for the finite
record-verifier commands that are explicitly listed in
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}.  They do not support current daemon,
overlap-checker, fake-extension-pipeline, Rule110, GroundCompiler, or full
artifact-suite behaviour unless the row is enlarged by a fresh command tuple for
that system.  For each such current-behaviour upgrade, the required tuple is
nonempty and contains at least command, source state, environment, exit code, log
path, and the assigned pass row binding the run to the submitted support surface.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} identifies the accepted case
image as the finite skeleton of four historical lessons and proves the exact
upgrade criterion for rerun or semantic-validation readings.  The only command
rows available before the case rows are the finite verifier rows displayed in
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}: certificate-record verification,
source-interface comparison, primary-claim inventory verification,
theorem-environment extraction, digest generation, and dated venue/bibliography
reachability.  None of these rows names a daemon execution, overlap-checker run,
fake-extension-pipeline rerun, Rule110 rerun, GroundCompiler rerun, or full
artifact-suite validation.

Therefore a proposed current-behaviour reading for any of those systems changes
the command-boundary coordinate of the case row.  Clause A6 of
Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table} requires the five
command-run fields whenever such a command-result assertion is made, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} requires the corresponding
positive extension coordinate and pass row.  If that tuple is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} returns it as the
finite bad subrecord.  If it is present and assigned, the upgraded current-run
claim is accepted exactly at the evidence level of that fresh row.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Command-run boundary}

\begin{proposition}[Command-run boundary inventory]
\label{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}

is complete for the command-boundary claims used by

\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}, and

\medskip

The evidence-level definition in

\path{current local automath checkout plus review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md},

\begin{theorem}[Post-edit rerun metadata gate]
\label{thm:post-edit-rerun-metadata-gate}
Let $I$ be the pair consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, let $L$ be the tuple of retained extractor and
finite-record verifier logs named in Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory},
and let $D$ be \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  After any edit to
\path{main.tex}, $I$, or a retained support record, a claim that the package has
a post-inventory fixed point for the new bytes is accepted only if the submitted
surface also contains, for each newly claimed rerun, its command, source commit
or source-state description, environment, exit code, and log path, and if $D$ is
regenerated after those logs exist.  If those metadata rows are absent, the same
source text has only the conditional reading of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: the fixed point is the
finite coordinate that would be obtained by the ordered rerun, not a current-byte
execution certificate for the edited package.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The operational evidence interface,
Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}, makes command-run status
a finite coordinate: the command, source state, environment, exit code, and log
path are part of the accepted record.  The digest-closure refresh criterion,
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}, makes the byte digest another
finite coordinate: after an inventory or support-record byte changes, the old
digest row names the old byte string and cannot identify the edited state.

The tuple $(I,L,D)$ is therefore ordered data, not a self-updating invariant.  If
the edited package includes fresh rows for the extractor, the retained
finite-record verifiers, any retained dated venue check, and the final digest
generator, then Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} applies to
those rows and supplies the fixed point.  If one of the metadata fields or the
post-log digest regeneration is missing, two packages can agree on the manuscript
prose while differing on the command actually run, the source state used, the
environment, the exit status, the log bytes, or the final digest bytes.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, the stronger
current-byte rerun claim is then not determined by the submitted surface; the
missing command or digest field is the finite bad subrecord.  What remains is
only the conditional finite-record statement, namely that such a fixed point is
available once the ordered rerun metadata and final digest coordinate are
supplied.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record support-state reconciliation invariant]
\label{thm:final-local-support-state-reconciliation}
For the source package after the present manuscript edits, the finite support
state used by the publication-safety theorem chain is the following reconciled
local state and no stronger one.  First, the files
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} are accepted as a
post-inventory fixed point only under the ordered metadata condition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-edit-rerun-metadata-gate}; absent such post-edit rows, the
fixed-point statements are conditional rerun criteria rather than current-byte
execution certificates.  Second, each command-run source state is the state
recorded in the corresponding log row of Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory};
historical rows are not claims that every later editor checkout has the same Git
\path{HEAD} or digest bytes.  Third, because the source package records neither
an upload receipt nor an archive-equivalent locator, bundle-backed support
remains conditional on the external instantiation record of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.

Moreover the same finite state is maximal simultaneously for the four boundary
interfaces on which the presentation route depends:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the imported BEDC/newmath discovery-gate source interface is exactly the
bounded path, commit, line-range, label, and summary interface of
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}; a full source-verification
reading requires fresh Lean or BEDC build records, axiom-purity records, and
source-marker or labelled-statement existence logs;
\item the publication-safety and current-package claims are exactly the
finite-record certificates of Theorems~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
and~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} under the explicitly supplied
record-gate soundness interface, not implementation soundness of the gates; the
current-package certificate is schema-relative and row-frozen to the declared
verifier schema and the six current command rows, so semantic truth of package claims,
post-edit freshness, and external venue status require the semantic
non-escalation, command-boundary, and post-edit rerun coordinates named below;
\item the four case-study rows are exactly the path-complete historical snapshot
lessons classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity} and closed
by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}; current operational
reproducibility of any daemon, overlap checker, Rule110 system, GroundCompiler
evaluator, or artifact suite requires the corresponding rerun log; and
\item the theorem-obligation inventory is exactly the syntactic labelled
environment coordinate on \path{main.tex} proved by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}; non-main \TeX{} files,
snapshot excerpts, and auxiliary tables are supporting or background material
unless separately brought into the extractor domain, and the coordinate is not a
proof-correctness, semantic-theorem-completeness, Lean/BEDC, daemon, artifact, or
venue certificate.
\end{enumerate}
Any stronger reading of one of these four interfaces is accepted by the
publication-safety theorem chain if and only if the submitted support state adds
the positive finite coordinates named in the relevant item and the assigned pass
records required by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}; if a
required coordinate is absent, the attempted upgrade has an inclusion-minimal
finite bad subrecord in the sense of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is exactly the fixed-point criterion specialized in
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} and
realized by Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-finite-record-realization}: the two
inventory paths and the verifier-log paths are finite byte coordinates of the
selected exact-inclusion support surface.  If any of those rows is stale,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} rejects the stronger
exact-inclusion claim and leaves only the local index reading.

For the second assertion, Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}
classifies the command-boundary table.  A row with command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path is accepted only at the evidence level
stated in that row.  Hence a historical source-state field certifies the logged
finite command result, not an equality between the final editor workspace and the
historical commit.  This is the reconciliation theorem
Theorem~\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation} applied to the refreshed
log rows.

For the third assertion,
Proposition~\ref{prop:submission-support-instantiation-field-normal-form} lists
the upload receipt and archive-equivalent locator fields as absent in the current
package.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}
therefore forbids promoting a bundle-local path into an unconditional venue or
public support coordinate.  Combining the three finite fields gives precisely
the local reconciled support state stated above, and no additional source-state,
upload, archive, Lean, daemon, or artifact-rerun coordinate is introduced.

It remains to prove simultaneous maximality for the four interfaces.  For the
source interface, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} fixes
the manual record fields, Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}
separates those fields from stronger formal-source evidence levels, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} proves maximality for the
submitted source surface.  A fresh Lean or BEDC rebuild, axiom-purity assertion,
or source-marker existence assertion reads a command, formal-build, axiom-audit,
or marker-coordinate not present in the bounded line-range interface.  Hence the
finite-coordinate theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, forbids deriving it
from the submitted fields alone, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} gives the positive
direction after the missing records and pass rows are added.

For the safety interface, Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}
fix record-gate soundness as an external finite input/output promise.  The finite
publication theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, and the
current package theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness},
use that promise only to construct and identify finite publication certificates.
Theorems~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade} and
\ref{thm:current-package-extension-coordinate-rigidity} classify an
implementation-soundness reading as a proper extension requiring gate-source,
command, environment, exit-code, and log coordinates.  Thus the stated finite
safety chain is not demoted: it remains the maximal accepted theorem chain at the
record level, and the stronger software-verification theorem is accepted exactly
when its additional executable gate records are supplied.

For the case rows, Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} provides
the finite path-complete row surface, Theorem~\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity}
classifies each row into one of the four skeleton lessons, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} proves closure under the
finite-record interface.  A current operational reproduction claim changes the
command-boundary coordinate: it asks for a fresh daemon, overlap-checker,
Rule110, GroundCompiler, or artifact-suite run rather than for the historical
snapshot lesson.  Proposition~\ref{audit:case-snapshot-non-rerun-boundary} shows
that the required command tuple is absent, so the obstruction skeleton returns
that missing tuple as a finite bad subrecord unless the rerun log and assigned
pass rows are added.

For the theorem-inventory coordinate,
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} proves the
deterministic labelled-environment extraction predicate, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing} proves that the domain is
exactly the five displayed theorem-like environments in \path{main.tex}.  The
manual boundary proposition,
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary}, separately identifies
non-main \TeX{} material as manual supporting or background material.  Therefore
semantic theorem completeness, proof correctness, non-main-file coverage, Lean or
BEDC rebuilding, daemon execution, artifact validation, and venue facts all read
coordinates outside the extractor predicate.  The same finite-coordinate and
extension-budget theorems then give non-escalation when those coordinates are
absent and acceptance when they are explicitly added with assigned pass rows.

In all four cases the stronger reading preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder} is strict exactly when the reading
adds one of the named coordinates.  If the coordinate is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} supplies an
inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord; if it is present with the required pass
rows, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} supplies the upgraded
finite certificate.  This proves the advertised simultaneous maximality and the
``if and only if'' upgrade criterion.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Support-coordinate discharge for the local evidence surface]
\label{cor:local-support-coordinate-discharge}
In the current presentation-route package the three support-coordinate repairs
are exhausted by the finite-record state of
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-local-support-state-reconciliation}.  Namely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the theorem-obligation inventory contributes only the ordered
post-inventory tuple consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, the theorem-environment extractor log, the retained
finite-record verifier logs, and the final digest table, and this tuple is a
current-byte fixed point only after those logs and the digest table are freshly
regenerated in that order;
\item the review bundle, technical supplement, and theorem-obligation inventory
are local/path-verified support unless a later exact upload receipt or
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator is added to the finite support
surface; and
\item the imported BEDC/newmath labels remain bounded source-interface rows, not
fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-correctness, semantic source-theory, or
axiom-purity evidence, unless the corresponding formal-source command row is
added.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the publication-safety theorem chain uses the inventory, bundle,
and imported-source coordinates exactly at these three bounded levels.  Any
reading that treats them as a post-edit fixed point without fresh logs, as
external support without an upload-or-archive coordinate, or as formal-source
evidence without a rebuild or axiom-audit command row has an inclusion-minimal
bad subrecord in the sense of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-local-support-state-reconciliation} is a simultaneous
maximality statement for the local support state.  Its first clause, together
with Theorem~\ref{thm:post-edit-rerun-metadata-gate}, gives item~1: after edits
to the inventory or support records, the accepted fixed-point coordinate is the
ordered tuple whose extractor/verifier logs and final digest table record the
new bytes, while absent or stale rows leave only the conditional rerun criterion.

Its third clause, together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}, gives
item~2.  Local manifests and digest rows identify the package bytes, but they do
not contain either of the two fields that would witness external support: an
exact venue-upload receipt or an archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator.

The first boundary interface in the maximality part of
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-local-support-state-reconciliation}, together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}, gives
item~3.  The imported rows are finite path, commit, label, line-range, and
bounded-summary coordinates.  A Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-correctness,
source-theory semantic validation, or axiom-purity reading adds a distinct
formal-source command coordinate, so it is accepted only when that coordinate is
present.

Each of the three stronger readings therefore differs from the current support
state by exactly one missing finite coordinate.  Removing the stronger-reading
tag returns to the accepted bounded reading, while adding the corresponding
fresh-log, upload-or-archive, or formal-source row supplies the missing field.
This is precisely the minimal-bad-subrecord normal form of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, and no additional
semantic, venue, or proof-assistant claim is introduced.
\end{proof}
\begin{theorem}[Supplement-level presentation-route five-interface sharpness]
\label{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness}
For the CICM presentation-only package whose primary source is
\path{submission_abstract.tex}, whose supplement is this file, and whose selected
support directory is \path{review_bundle/}, the maximal claim certified by the
present theorem chain is exactly the conjunction of the following five bounded
interfaces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Conditional finite-record publication safety.}  The publication claim is a
finite-record certificate under the externally supplied record-gate soundness
predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), not a proof that the gate
implementations satisfy their specifications.
\item \emph{Schema-relative package exactness.}  The executable verifier and the
current-package certificate identify the finite rows accepted by the declared
schema and dispatch table; they do not check proof semantics, theorem adequacy,
or mathematical truth of all prose in the package.
\item \emph{Bounded source-interface import.}  The imported newmath discovery-gate
material is the pinned path/commit/label/line-range/bounded-summary interface of
Table~\ref{tab:source-interface-record}, strengthened only by the finite
table/JSON/snapshot comparison where that comparison is invoked.  It is not an
exact reproof, exact source-statement import, public-source semantic-completeness
result, Lean rebuild, BEDC rebuild, or axiom-purity certificate.
\item \emph{Manifest-bounded case evidence.}  The Rule110 and GroundCompiler
finite-witness claims are historical manifest rows with reviewable snapshots,
status records, and stated limitation boundaries.  They are not fresh dynamic
artifact validations, evaluator-correctness proofs, or semantic-exhaustiveness
theorems for the artifacts.
\item \emph{Operational support-surface condition.}  Bundle-backed claims are
submitted-support claims only if the exact \path{review_bundle/} directory with
the final digest manifest is uploaded, or if a single archive-equivalent byte
locator supplies the same file list, manifest identity, SHA-256 digest rows, and
relative path semantics.  In the current source package, absent such an external
receipt or archive-equivalent record, the same claims remain conditional
exact-inclusion or matching-archive claims.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, by the finite-record certificate calculus spine of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine}, these five interfaces
form a sharp bad-record skeleton.  Let
\(c^{+}\) be any stronger reading of a load-bearing presentation-route claim that
adds content on a nonempty set \(J\) of the five axes above.  Then \(c^{+}\) is
accepted by the same finite-record publication chain if and only if, for every
axis in \(J\), the submitted support surface adds the corresponding positive
coordinate and the assigned pass record:
\begin{enumerate}
\item gate identity, gate specification, source state or version, and an
implementation-soundness pass row or command-run tuple for axis~1;
\item a semantic proof-checking, theorem-adequacy, exact-proof, Lean/BEDC rebuild,
or out-of-schema verifier coordinate for axis~2;
\item exact source-statement text, formal-source rebuild, axiom-purity record,
public-source equality log, or semantic source-validation coordinate for axis~3;
\item evaluator contract, artifact-semantic pass row, or fresh evaluator command
run tied by manifest row to the submitted Rule110/GroundCompiler artifact for
axis~4; and
\item exact upload receipt for \path{review_bundle/} and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, or one archive-equivalent locator
passing the file-list, digest, manifest-identity, and path-semantics tests, for
axis~5.
\end{enumerate}
If at least one required positive coordinate is absent, then \(c^{+}\) has an
inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord supported on one unpaid axis.  Consequently
no mixture of the existing source-interface rows, verifier rows, theorem-inventory
rows, historical case snapshots, or local bundle paths can glue together into an
operational compiler-correctness, semantic theorem-correctness, dynamic
artifact-validation, or unconditional submitted-support theorem.  Conversely,
after all coordinates in the displayed union are added and pass their assigned
gates, the same finite-extension normal form accepts precisely that upgraded
finite-record reading.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We prove both maximality and sharpness axis by axis, and then take the finite
union.  For axis~1, Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness} make
record-gate soundness an external input/output predicate, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} constructs finite publication
certificates only under that predicate.  Theorems~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade}
and~\ref{thm:current-package-extension-coordinate-rigidity} identify an
implementation-soundness reading as a strict extension requiring gate identity,
specification, source-state or version, and implementation-soundness pass or
command-run coordinates.  Thus the conditional finite-record reading is maximal
until those coordinates are supplied, and the positive direction is exactly the
extension criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}
together with Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}.

For axis~2, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} proves exactness only
for the declared schema predicate and the executable record verifier's projection,
and Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} specializes that
schema-relative result to the current package.  The theorem-inventory side is
bounded by Theorems~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}, and
\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction}: they provide syntactic
labelled-environment coverage in the declared domain, not proof semantics or
mathematical correctness.  Hence any semantic or adequacy reading reads a
coordinate absent from the accepted schema projection unless it is added as a new
proof-checking, exact-proof, formal-rebuild, or theorem-adequacy coordinate.

The finite union is governed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine}: each axis is a
projection of the same certificate tuple, and every upgrade is a positive
extension budget rather than an informal combination of support rows.

For axis~3, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} fixes the
manual source-interface fields, Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}
proves maximality of those bounded fields even after the finite comparison record
is used, and Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
shows that semantic source completeness is not determined by that projection.
Therefore exact source import requires exact source text and byte equality,
public-source equality requires a public fetch-and-compare log, formal rebuilds
require Lean/BEDC command records, and semantic source-theory claims require a
semantic-validation record; none is supplied by the bounded line-range interface.

For axis~4, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface} identifies
the complete manifest-bounded coordinate set for the finite-witness evidence, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} plus
Audit record~\ref{audit:case-snapshot-non-rerun-boundary} isolate the missing
dynamic evaluator, artifact-semantic, and fresh-rerun fields.  Thus the accepted
case evidence is historical and manifest-bounded, while dynamic Rule110 or
GroundCompiler validation is accepted only after the evaluator contract, semantic
pass row, or command-run tuple is added.

For axis~5, Proposition~\ref{prop:primary-supplement-interface-map} maps primary
claims to supplemental theorem, table, and manifest support; Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-inclusion-support-surface-realization}
proves that this support is realized by exact inclusion of \path{review_bundle/}
with matching final digests or by an archive-equivalent replacement satisfying the
finite byte and path tests; and Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}
records that the present source package has no upload receipt, DOI, or
institutional archive identifier.  Consequently the current support-surface claim
is conditional until one of those operational finite records is present.

Now let \(c^{+}\) add content on the nonempty set \(J\) of axes.  Each added
content item is a strict stronger reading in the preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder} exactly when its corresponding
positive coordinate is not already one of the accepted finite fields just listed.
If every positive coordinate for every axis in \(J\) is present and passes its
assigned gate, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} constructs
the upgraded finite certificate.  If some required coordinate is absent, choose an
unpaid axis and then an inclusion-minimal missing finite field in the budget for
that axis.  The finite-coordinate theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, shows that two review
states can agree on all submitted coordinates and differ on that missing field;
therefore the stronger reading is not determined by the current certificate.
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} turns the missing field
into an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord.  Adding records on any other axis
does not change that projection, so mixed-interface gluing is impossible unless
all unpaid axes are paid.  This proves the sharp skeleton, the lower bound, and
the converse finite-extension acceptance statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Supplement-level presentation-route stronger-reading classifier]
\label{thm:presentation-route-stronger-reading-classifier}
For the present CICM presentation-only package, every attempted stronger reading
of the five flagged interface families is classified by the five-axis skeleton of
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness}, and the classifier
is exact in the following sense.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A stronger reading of the finite publication-safety interface, the
certificate-calculus spine, publication-safety maximality, or the current-package
publication-safety instance is accepted exactly when it adds an axis~1
implementation-soundness coordinate for record gates and, if the reading mentions
proof truth, artifacts, submitted support, or venue outcome, the corresponding
axis~2, axis~4, or axis~5 coordinates.
\item A stronger reading of the four finite scripts, the finite-script RGS
instantiation, or the assigned-gate soundness audit boundary is accepted exactly
when it adds either the named finite projection coordinate already proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}, or a separate
axis~1/axis~2 implementation-soundness coordinate containing the verifier
specification, source state, command-run tuple, log path, and assigned pass row
for the stronger implementation claim.
\item A stronger reading of the current-package acceptance ledger, certificate
exactness theorem, or row-frozen invariance corollary is accepted exactly when it
adds the missing axis~2 schema or semantic-proof coordinate, or the extra row,
fresh command-run, artifact-semantic, upload, archive, or venue coordinate read by
that stronger claim.
\item A stronger reading of the imported source interface, source-record-file
consistency, bounded source-interface maximality, or source-interface semantic
completeness obstruction is accepted exactly when it adds the missing axis~3
coordinate: exact source-statement text, byte-equality or public-reachability log,
formal Lean/BEDC rebuild record, axiom-purity record, or semantic source-validation
record, together with the assigned pass row for that coordinate.
\item A stronger reading of the theorem-environment extractor boundary,
extractor-domain exactness, or theorem-inventory proof-checker obstruction is
accepted exactly when it adds the missing theorem-inventory coordinate for the
claimed extension: a declared parser domain beyond
\{\path{definition}, \path{lemma}, \path{proposition}, \path{theorem},
\path{corollary}\}, a proof or semantic checker, a Lean/BEDC rebuild record, an
artifact/daemon/venue log, or an inventory field that textually classifies audit
records, constructions, proof-interface prose, and other out-of-domain material,
together with the assigned pass row for that coordinate.
\end{enumerate}
If a proposed stronger reading in any of these five families lacks at least one
coordinate listed above, then it has an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord on
an unpaid axis.  Conversely, if all coordinates required by its listed axes are
submitted and pass their assigned gates, the finite-record certificate calculus
accepts precisely that upgraded finite-record reading.  Hence the theorem chain
is maximal for the conditional, row-frozen, schema-relative, bounded-source,
finite-projection claims stated in this paper and no mixed use of existing rows
can silently upgrade them to implementation soundness, semantic truth, public
source completeness, artifact validity, support upload, or venue acceptance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each of the five families is a load-bearing presentation-route claim and is
therefore first projected to the seven-coordinate certificate tuple
\((K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine}.  A proposed stronger
reading is strict precisely when it changes a coordinate not determined by that
projection, by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  The
five-axis theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness},
then identifies the unique axis on which the changed coordinate lives and lists
the positive finite coordinates that must be paid for acceptance.

For the first family, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} assumes
record-gate soundness and constructs only finite publication certificates;
Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-maximality} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:publication-safety-current-package-instance} inherit exactly
that conditional interface.  Therefore an implementation-soundness reading changes
axis~1 by adding gate specification, source-state, command-run, and pass-row
coordinates.  If the same reading also asserts proof truth, artifact semantics,
support upload, or venue acceptance, those phrases change axes~2, 4, or~5 exactly
as listed in Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness}.

For the second family,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} proves only the
printed finite predicate on the parsed finite projection of each named script;
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-script-rgs-instantiation-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary} use those rows only as
finite command-run coordinates.  A claim about broad verifier correctness or gate
semantics reads a verifier specification, source state, execution environment,
runtime semantics, log, and assigned pass row not contained in the projection.
Thus it is an axis~1 or axis~2 extension, while the already proved projection
claim is exactly the finite coordinate supplied by the command-run record.

For the third family,
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-package-acceptance-certificate-ledger},
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:row-frozen-current-package-invariance} read only the displayed
six rows, their certificate fields, the submitted support surface, and the
recorded verifier log.  A semantic truth certificate, a seven-row or modified-row
state, a fresh execution, an artifact-validity statement, an upload or archive
claim, or a venue decision changes a finite coordinate outside that six-row
projection.  Those are respectively axis~2, axis~4, or axis~5 extension
coordinates, or a row-set extension governed by the same budget normal form.

For the fourth family,
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency},
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} determine
only the pinned path, commit, label, line range, extraction date, bounded summary,
local JSON/table/snapshot comparison, and declared evidence level.  Exact
source-statement import, public reachability, byte equality against a public
checkout, formal rebuilds, axiom-purity checks, and semantic source-validation
require new axis~3 coordinates and assigned pass rows.

For the fifth family,
Theorems~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}, and
\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction} determine only syntactic
label coverage for the five displayed theorem-like environments in
\path{main.tex}.  Audit records, constructions, proof-interface prose, remarks,
submission abstracts, semantic statement checking, proof correctness, Lean/BEDC
rebuilding, artifact validation, daemon behavior, and venue state are absent from
that finite computation.  A reading that covers any such material therefore
changes the theorem-inventory coordinate or another presentation-route axis and
requires the corresponding positive finite row and assigned pass record.

If all coordinates required by the axes touched by the stronger reading are
present and pass their assigned gates, the extension-budget normal form,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}, constructs the enlarged
certificate and Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} accepts it at the
declared evidence level.  If any required coordinate is absent, choose one unpaid
axis and one missing finite field on that axis.  The finite-coordinate theorem
gives two review states agreeing on every submitted coordinate and differing on
that missing field, so the stronger reading is not determined by the current
certificate.  The obstruction skeleton,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, reduces the failure to
an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  Since the five axes are projections of the
same certificate tuple, adding rows on a different axis cannot alter the unpaid
projection.  This proves exact classification, maximality, and the no-gluing
boundary for all five flagged families.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[End-to-end upgrade decomposition obstruction]
\label{thm:end-to-end-upgrade-decomposition-obstruction}
For the present CICM presentation-only package, an end-to-end workflow-correctness
reading of the publication-safety theorem chain is accepted by the finite-record
calculus if and only if it decomposes into the finite positive-coordinate budgets
of Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness} and every touched
budget is supplied with its assigned pass record.  More explicitly, any reading
asserting correctness of the actual gate implementations, fresh source or Lean
rebuilds, semantic truth of the package claims, dynamic Rule110 or
GroundCompiler artifact validity, current post-edit execution, uploaded
supplemental support, or venue outcome touches respectively one or more of the
gate-implementation, schema/proof, source-interface, artifact-semantic,
command-boundary, support-surface, and venue coordinates listed in the
five-interface skeleton.  If one of those coordinates is absent, the stronger
end-to-end reading has an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord and no mixture
of the existing finite source rows, pass rows, theorem-inventory rows, historical
case snapshots, or local bundle paths can certify it.  Conversely, after exactly
the missing coordinates and assigned pass records are added, the finite-extension
normal form certifies only the corresponding upgraded finite-record reading, not
any further semantic or venue fact.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let \(e\) be an attempted end-to-end reading of the theorem chain.  Project \(e\)
to the seven certificate fields \((K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine}.  If \(e\) says no more
than the finite publication certificates, row-frozen current-package exactness,
bounded source import, manifest-bounded case evidence, and conditional support
surface already listed in Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness},
then it is the existing finite-record theorem chain.

Otherwise \(e\) is a strict stronger reading in the preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}.  The stronger-reading classifier,
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-stronger-reading-classifier}, sends each
changed assertion to one of the five axes of
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness}.  The concrete
phrases in the statement are precisely those axes: gate implementation correctness
uses axis~1; semantic proof truth, schema escape, and theorem adequacy use
axis~2; fresh source or Lean/BEDC rebuild and source semantic completeness use
axis~3; dynamic Rule110 or GroundCompiler artifact semantics use axis~4; uploaded
supplemental support, archive replacement, and venue outcome use axis~5, with
fresh post-edit execution also reading the command-boundary coordinate required by
the relevant axis.  Hence the end-to-end reading decomposes into the finite union
of the touched positive-coordinate budgets.

If every coordinate in that union is present and every assigned gate row passes,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} constructs the enlarged
certificate, and Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} accepts it exactly
at the declared evidence level.  This proves the positive direction, including
the final caveat: a finite extension certifies only the finite fields it adds.

If some coordinate in the union is absent, choose an unpaid touched axis and an
inclusion-minimal missing field on that axis.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, two review states may
agree on all submitted coordinates and differ on that missing field, so the
end-to-end assertion is not determined by the current package.  The obstruction
skeleton, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, identifies
the missing field as an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord.  Because the five
axes are projections of the same certificate tuple, adding or reusing rows on a
different axis leaves this unpaid projection unchanged.  Thus existing finite
source rows, pass rows, theorem-inventory rows, historical case snapshots, and
local bundle paths cannot glue into end-to-end workflow correctness.  This proves
the obstruction and the converse lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Presentation-summary non-escalation]
\label{cor:presentation-summary-non-escalation}
Let \(s\) be a load-bearing sentence in the primary presentation source
\path{submission_abstract.tex} or in an accompanying presentation abstract that
summarizes Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness},
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure},
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-stronger-reading-classifier}, or
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness}.  If \(s\) is
accepted by the same finite-record publication chain without adding new support
coordinates, then its strongest accepted normal form is the following bounded
reading: under the externally supplied record-gate-soundness predicate, the
visible finite records determine the schema-relative certificate rows and their
finite bad-subrecord obstructions.  In particular, the accepted presentation
summary is finite-record only and does not assert gate implementation soundness,
end-to-end compiler correctness, proof-assistant correctness, dynamic artifact
validity, upload or archive availability, venue compliance, or venue acceptance.
Conversely, a presentation summary that explicitly keeps the phrases
``under record-gate soundness'' and ``finite-record only'' for this theorem chain,
and that makes no additional implementation, semantic, artifact, upload, archive,
or venue claim, is accepted at the same finite-record level as the corresponding
certificate rows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Treat the summary sentence \(s\) as a presentation-route claim whose evidence
surface is the primary source and the supporting theorem chain in this
supplement.  Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} constructs only the
certificate tuple \((K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) from the submitted finite surface, ledger,
dispatch table, and record-gate-soundness input.  Its conclusion already excludes
implementation soundness, proof-assistant correctness, artifact semantics,
daemon behavior, upload, archive availability, venue compliance, and venue
acceptance unless the corresponding finite extension coordinates are added.
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} specialize this same tuple to
the current schema rows and refreshed command-result rows, so they add no new
semantic or operational coordinate.

Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness} classifies the five
presentation-route axes and proves the exact extension budget for every stronger
reading on any nonempty set of those axes.  Therefore a summary sentence accepted
without additional coordinates can project only to the conditional
record-gate-sound, finite-record certificate reading.  If the sentence is read as
gate implementation soundness, end-to-end compiler correctness, proof-assistant
correctness, dynamic artifact validity, upload or archive availability, venue
compliance, or venue acceptance, it has added content on at least one of the five
axes.  The five-interface theorem then supplies an inclusion-minimal missing
coordinate as a finite bad subrecord unless that coordinate and its assigned pass
row have been supplied.  This proves the non-escalation part.

For the converse, the displayed bounded wording asserts exactly the positive
coordinates already present in the publication-safety certificate and current
package rows: the record-gate-soundness premise, the finite support surface, the
schema-relative verifier projection, and the finite bad-subrecord boundary.  It
does not add any coordinate from the five extension budgets.  The schema-relative
exactness theorem and the five-interface sharpness theorem therefore accept the
summary at precisely the same finite-record level as the underlying certificate
rows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record support-coordinate synchronization normal form]
\label{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}
For the current source package, the support state for the three externalized
claims in the publication-safety theorem chain is exactly the following finite
normal form.  This is a finite-record support lemma for the machine-checkable
support coordinates used by the bounded audit interface: it records when byte
strings, logs, and digest rows are mutually current, and it is not an
independent semantic invariant of the paper, the artifacts, or the venue process.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-inventory coordinate is accepted only after
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} have been written,
the theorem-environment extractor and finite-record verifiers have been rerun on
that post-inventory state, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} has been regenerated over those
bytes and logs.
\item Bundle-backed support is local/path-verified only unless the exact
\path{review_bundle/} directory is uploaded with matching final digests or an
archive-equivalent locator satisfying
Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence} is supplied.
\item Venue/page-limit compliance is only a dated local-readiness observation
unless a near-submission upload-time venue record, or an included unchanged-rule
statement tying the upload to the latest dated venue record, is supplied.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently no theorem-ledger, bundle-availability, or upload-time venue claim
may be read in the stronger submitted-support sense unless the corresponding
finite coordinate in this normal form is present.  The only mathematical role of
this theorem in the article is to close the support-coordinate input required by
Theorems~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and
\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}; later corollaries in this
subsection are projections of this same finite byte-level closure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the theorem-inventory coordinate, the digest table is a function of finite
bytes.  If \path{theorem_inventory.json} or \path{theorem_inventory.md} is
created or changed after that table is computed, its byte string is not an input
to the recorded hash row.  The fixed-point closure theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}, the post-inventory certificate
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}, and the
realization theorem
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-finite-record-realization}, therefore accept the
inventory coordinate exactly after the inventory files and their verifier logs
precede the final digest pass.  This proves the first clause and prevents stale
digest rows from supporting the exact-inclusion theorem-ledger claim.

For bundle-backed support,
Proposition~\ref{prop:submission-support-instantiation-field-normal-form}
records no current upload receipt and records the archive-equivalent locator only
as a digest-conditioned public branch/path coordinate.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation} and
Proposition~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition}, a local path under
\path{review_bundle/} is therefore not an external reviewer-available coordinate
unless the exact-upload record is present or the public coordinate contains the
matching digest-identified bytes.  This proves the second clause.

For venue compliance, the venue facts are external facts rather than internal
source definitions.  Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} classify the
current venue logs as dated readiness records and require either a later
upload-time tuple or an unchanged-rule statement before the stronger upload-time
claim is available.  This proves the third clause.  The three fields are
independent coordinates of the finite package state, so adding a stronger
reading in any one field without its named coordinate is exactly the prohibited
coordinate extension ruled out by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  Hence the displayed
normal form is exact.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record post-inventory support-coordinate dichotomy]
\label{thm:post-inventory-support-coordinate-dichotomy}
For the current presentation package there are exactly two possible support
readings for any claim whose evidence surface names \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, or a file under \path{review_bundle/}.  If the
ordered post-inventory pass of Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}
has been run and the exact resulting surface is externally instantiated by the
upload-or-archive record of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, then the claim is a
submitted bundle-backed support claim at the finite-record evidence level stated
in its certificate.  In every other case it is only a local/path-verified or
dated-readiness claim, with the further fallback of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} if the
post-inventory pass is not closed.  No intermediate reading is available in
which refreshed local digests alone supply an external support coordinate, or in
which an upload-or-archive locator alone supplies post-inventory verifier and
digest closure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $c$ be a claim whose evidence surface names one of the stated paths.  The
finite-coordinate determination boundary,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, allows $c$ to be
read only from finite fields present in the accepted package state.  The first
field is the post-inventory closure field.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, that field is present
exactly when the inventory files are written, the theorem-environment extractor
and finite-record verifiers are rerun on that post-inventory state, any retained
dated route-readiness log is fixed, and the final SHA--256 manifest is generated
after those bytes exist.  If this field is absent, the first clause of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} permits only the
local index or dated-readiness fallback and forbids the exact theorem-ledger
support reading.

The second field is external instantiation of the selected support surface.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Proposition~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition}, this field is
present only when either the exact supplemental directory with the matching final
digest manifest is uploaded, or an archive-equivalent replacement satisfying
Audit record~\ref{audit:review-bundle-archive-equivalence} is supplied.  If this
field is absent, Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}
keeps every bundle-backed support claim local/path-verified and prevents it from
becoming an unconditional public or venue-submitted support coordinate.

Thus the support state is the product of two independent finite fields: local
post-inventory closure and external support instantiation.  When both are
present, the submitted bundle-backed reading follows from the exact support
surface closure theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}.  If the
first field is missing, the verifier/digest fixed point is not closed; if the
second is missing, the closed local surface has not been externally instantiated.
In either missing-field case, promoting $c$ to a submitted bundle-backed claim
would add a finite coordinate not contained in the package.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}
rejects that promotion, and the only remaining readings are precisely the
local/path-verified or dated-readiness readings already classified above.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Final refreshed-coordinate instantiation]
\label{prop:final-refreshed-coordinate-instantiation}
For the current dated local-readiness package, the local theorem-ledger
coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} is instantiated by
the finite tuple consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, \path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},

\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, provided these files exist on the

upload receipt, DOI, venue acceptance record, upload-time venue-compliance record,
fresh Lean rebuild, daemon run, or artifact rerun; any archive-equivalent locator
requires the separate public byte-equality coordinate of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The tuple is finite, and each named component is one of the coordinates already
classified by Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate},
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-finite-record-realization},
Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.  The two theorem
inventory files are the post-inventory byte coordinates.  The theorem-environment
log is the syntactic coverage coordinate for those files.  The two finite-record
verifier logs and the primary-claim verifier log are the schema-relative,
source-interface, and primary-surface coordinates.  The
venue/bibliography log is the dated external-route locator coordinate.  The
digest manifest is the finite hash table selecting the bytes of the preceding
coordinates.

If the local package files have the printed hashes, then equality of SHA-256 rows
is exactly the package-state equality relation used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:workspace-final-package-reconciliation}; hence the first normal
form coordinate is present.  If any named file is omitted, changed after the
digest pass, or replaced by a file with a different row, then the finite tuple no
longer equals the selected coordinate and the post-inventory claim falls back to
the weaker local or historical reading described in
Proposition~\ref{prop:regenerated-theorem-inventory-digest-closure}.  The final
sentence follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}: none of
the listed files is an upload receipt, DOI, venue acceptance, Lean rebuild,
daemon execution, or artifact-rerun record; the branch/path locator is already
classified separately by the support-surface normal form.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted inventory coverage criterion]
\label{thm:accepted-inventory-coverage-criterion}
Let $E$ be the finite set of labelled theorem-like environments in the current
\path{main.tex}, where theorem-like means one of definition, lemma,
proposition, theorem, or corollary, and let $I$ be the finite label set recorded
in \path{theorem_inventory.json}.  Let $s$ be a source state of \path{main.tex}
and the accepted inventory files.  If the post-inventory extractor run
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} is run on $s$, has
exit code zero, and reports no unlabelled theorem-like environments, no duplicate
labels, and no labels omitted from \path{theorem_inventory.json}, then the
accepted inventory pair \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} is an exact syntactic coverage coordinate for the
manuscript's theorem-like environment surface at $s$.  Moreover this condition is
the unique inventory-coverage input to the fixed point of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: any later edit to
\path{main.tex} or to either inventory file changes the source state from $s$ and
removes the exact current-byte inventory coordinate until the extractor is rerun
on the new state and its log is included in the final digest pass.  Conversely,
if a theorem-like environment in \path{main.tex} has no label, has a duplicate
label, has a label outside $I$, or is introduced after the last extractor log
named by the digest surface, then the exact coverage coordinate is absent until
the source or inventory is updated and the extractor is rerun on the same state
that is later digested.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The extractor's domain is the finite list of lines of \path{main.tex}.  It scans
that list for the five displayed environment names, assigns to each occurrence
its first label, and compares the resulting finite label set $E$ with the finite
set $I$ parsed from \path{theorem_inventory.json}.  Exit code zero with the three
stated zero counters says precisely that every extracted environment has a
label, no two extracted environments share a label, and $E\subseteq I$.  Since
the coordinate is only a syntactic coverage coordinate, extra explanatory rows
in the inventory do not add theorem-like environments; the needed equality is
therefore equality on the extracted manuscript surface, namely every member of
$E$ is represented by an inventory label.  The pair
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} then selects the
same finite labelled surface named by the extractor log, so it is an exact
finite coverage coordinate for the manuscript at $s$.

It remains to prove the fixed-point clause.  The support-coordinate fixed point
