uses current bytes, not path names in isolation.  Thus the relevant object is the
triple consisting of the manuscript bytes, the accepted inventory bytes, and the
extractor log produced from those same bytes.  On this triple the extractor
predicate is deterministic: changing none of the three bytes preserves the
reported finite set $E$ and the comparison with $I$, while changing
\path{main.tex} can add, delete, relabel, or move a theorem-like environment, and
changing \path{theorem_inventory.json} can add or remove an inventory label.  In
either changed case the old log is no longer a log for the new triple.  The exact
inventory coordinate therefore descends to the fixed point of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} only when the log was
computed after the accepted source and inventory bytes were fixed and before the
final digest manifest was regenerated.  This is precisely the inventory-coverage
input used later by Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}:
the digest surface records the accepted inventory files and the extractor log as
one finite current-byte tuple rather than as independent historical artifacts.
No second inventory-coverage coordinate is available, because any purported
coverage claim over the same surface must be a claim about the same finite set of
displayed theorem-like environments and the same finite inventory label set; by
determinism it is identical to the extractor predicate above when the bytes
agree, and stale when the bytes do not agree.

For the converse, an unlabelled environment supplies no element by which the
inventory can select that environment, a duplicate label makes the selection
non-injective on the manuscript surface, and a label outside $I$ is a member of
$E$ not represented by the accepted inventory.  A theorem-like environment added
after the last extractor run is the same obstruction at the level of source
states: it belongs to the new extracted set but cannot belong to the old logged
set, since the old log was computed from earlier bytes.  Each case removes one
of the finite coordinates required in the first paragraph.  Updating the source
or the inventory and rerunning the extractor on the same state that will be
digested is therefore necessary before exact coverage can again be asserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record post-inventory support-coordinate fixed point]
\label{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}
Let $P$ be the current local package state consisting of the manuscript source,
\path{submission_abstract.tex}, \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, and \path{review_bundle/}.  Suppose that the following
finite sequence is executed in the displayed order:
\begin{enumerate}
\item write the theorem-inventory files for the manuscript source state;
\item rerun \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py};
\item rerun the finite-record verifiers named in
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory};
\item rerun the dated venue/bibliography locator check, if a dated route-readiness
claim is retained; and
\item write \path{review_bundle/final_digest_generation_run.log} as the command
metadata for the hash pass and regenerate
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} from the resulting bytes of the
inventory files, verifier logs, dated venue log, and selected review-bundle files
other than the digest manifest and this generation log.
\end{enumerate}
Then, at the same finite-record support level as
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}, the support coordinate selected by
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-refreshed-coordinate-instantiation} is a fixed point
of the finite post-inventory verifier/digest pass: every file used to justify the
theorem-ledger, finite-verifier, and dated-readiness claims is an input to the
final digest manifest, the digest-generation command has its own acyclic command,
source-state, environment, exit-code, and log-path row in
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}, and the manifest is produced after
those support inputs exist.
Conversely, if any one of the five ordered steps is omitted or performed after the
digest regeneration, the stronger exact-inclusion theorem-ledger claim is not
available; the manuscript retains only the local path-verified or dated-readiness
reading classified in
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.  In either case the
fixed point supplies no external upload receipt, archive-equivalent locator,
upload-time venue-compliance record, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-resolution
audit, axiom-purity audit, daemon run, or artifact-semantic rerun.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The package state $P$ is finite because it is a finite list of relative paths and
finite byte strings.  The extractor in the second step reads
\path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}; its stated boundary is
syntactic theorem-like environment extraction and inventory-label coverage only.
The finite-record verifiers in the third step read the schema, pass-record,
primary-claim, submission-interface, source-interface, manifest, and source
snapshot records named in Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}.  The dated
venue/bibliography check, when retained, reads external route and locator pages
and writes a dated log with the explicit boundary that it is not acceptance,
upload, archive minting, Lean rebuild, daemon execution, or artifact rerun
evidence.  The final digest pass records the command, source state, environment,
exit code, generated manifest, and log path in
\path{review_bundle/final_digest_generation_run.log}, and computes the SHA--256
table from the already-existing support inputs.  The table deliberately excludes
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} and
\path{review_bundle/final_digest_generation_run.log} as hashed inputs, avoiding a
self-digest recursion; those two files are instead the manifest and the command
metadata for producing it.

For the forward implication, Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coverage-criterion}
converts the post-inventory extractor counters into the exact syntactic coverage
coordinate for the accepted inventory pair.  The ordering then makes every
load-bearing finite record that supports the theorem-ledger coordinate an
already-existing byte string before the digest table is computed.  Hence the
digest rows name the same inventory, extractor-log, verifier-log,
dated-venue-log, and selected bundle bytes that are cited in
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-refreshed-coordinate-instantiation}.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}, exact finite support is precisely
equality of the selected paths and their final digest rows.  The digest-generator
row in Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory} supplies the command-result
ledger required for the final hash pass itself without requiring the log to be a
hashed input to its own output, so the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} is closed under the
post-inventory verifier/digest pass without borrowing a pre-inventory or
unlogged command result.

For the converse, suppose a step is omitted or run after digest regeneration.  If
the inventory files are missing or stale, the extractor and inventory coverage
claim has no post-inventory input.  If the extractor or verifier logs are missing
or stale, the package has no command-result record with command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path for the relevant finite comparison.  If a
dated venue-readiness claim is retained but the dated locator check is missing or
stale, the venue statement has no current dated-readiness coordinate.  If the
digest manifest is produced before any of these inputs exists or after they later
change, at least one cited byte string is not the byte string selected by its
final SHA--256 row.  In every case the stronger exact-inclusion coordinate would
require adding a finite record not selected by the manifest, which is forbidden by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  The fallbacks are
exactly the local/path-verified and dated-readiness readings stated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.

Finally, none of the five steps contains the finite fields required for the other
evidence axes.  Upload and archive support require the records of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}; upload-time venue
compliance requires the tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}; and fresh
formal-source, daemon, and artifact-semantic claims require the command/source,
environment, exit-code, and log coordinates isolated in
Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}.  Since those coordinates
are not created by the post-inventory fixed-point pass, no such stronger claim is
proved.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current post-inventory realization]
\label{cor:current-post-inventory-realization}
Assume that the present source state contains the two submitted
inventory files \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}.
If, after those two files exist, the theorem-environment extractor, the retained
finite-record verifiers, the retained dated venue/bibliography check, and the
final SHA--256 manifest are run in the order displayed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, then the theorem-ledger
row $a_7$ of Table~\ref{tab:current-acceptance-ledger} is instantiated at exactly
the finite support level of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.  In particular the
instantiated row certifies only syntactic inventory coverage, finite-record
schema acceptance, retained dated-readiness logging, and byte-level digest
closure; it does not certify theorem semantics, upload, archive replacement,
venue acceptance, fresh source-theory rebuilds, or dynamic artifact validation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first hypothesis supplies the missing finite coordinates selected in
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-package-shape-convention} and in the added row
$a_7$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:nested-package-states}.  The ordered post-write command
sequence is precisely the sequence required in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Applying that theorem
therefore makes the resulting digest table a fixed point over the inventory
bytes and the verifier/log bytes that are used by the theorem-ledger claim.

It remains to identify the strength of the instantiated support row.  The
normal-form theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form},
classifies the post-inventory coordinate as a finite local support coordinate:
inventory coverage is syntactic, verifier acceptance is schema-relative, dated
venue evidence is local-readiness evidence only, and digest closure is a
byte-string equality surface.  The exclusions listed in the last sentence are
exactly the non-escalation exclusions in that theorem and in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Hence the current
inventory row is realized, but only at the stated finite support level.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record current inventory support-coordinate realization]
\label{thm:current-inventory-artifact-realization}
For the present accepted source state, after the final theorem-inventory bytes
for this manuscript have been accepted, suppose that the files
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} are present as
finite package coordinates.  Let $L$ be the retained finite-record log family
consisting of the syntactic theorem-environment extraction log
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log}, the finite
certificate verifier log \path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
the source-interface verifier log
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}, the primary-claim
inventory freshness log
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_freshness_2026-06-09.log}, and any
retained dated venue/bibliography check log used only at its stated historical or
local-readiness level.  If every log in $L$ that is cited as a current
command-result coordinate is regenerated after the two inventory files exist and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those log bytes
exist, then the two missing support-coordinate obligations labelled
\path{post-inventory-artifact-realization} and
\path{fresh-post-inventory-verifier-and-digest-logs} are discharged exactly at
the support level of Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: the
inventory files are selected finite coordinates, the extractor and finite-record
verifiers are post-inventory command records, and the digest table names the
resulting inventory and log bytes.  Conversely, if either root inventory file is
absent when a cited current extractor or finite-record verifier log is produced,
or if the final digest table is not regenerated after those cited log bytes
exist, the same support claim is stale for the current inventory bytes and is
rejected as a current fixed-point coordinate.
This realization is only a finite byte/log/digest realization and does not assert extractor semantic completeness, theorem-proof
correctness, venue acceptance, upload, archive replacement, fresh Lean/BEDC
rebuilds, daemon execution, or dynamic artifact validation.
If the inventory files are changed after the extractor or digest pass, the same
statement is no longer current; it reverts to the conditional/historical reading
until the displayed rerun sequence is repeated against the changed bytes.
In the source state used for this presentation package, the displayed rerun sequence
is instantiated by exit-code-zero records at
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_freshness_2026-06-09.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/final_digest_generation_run.log}, with the regenerated
manifest at \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  This current-instance
sentence is a finite command-result claim only and inherits the same
non-escalation boundary as the theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first hypothesis supplies the two finite byte coordinates that were absent
from the pre-run support surface.  The theorem-environment extractor then reads
\path{main.tex} together with \path{theorem_inventory.json}; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}, an
exit-code-zero refreshed log proves precisely syntactic label coverage in the
five-environment domain and proves no semantic theorem property.  The certificate
and source-interface verifiers are finite programs of the kind isolated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} and
Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}.  Rerunning each cited
current verifier after the inventory bytes exist is therefore exactly the
finite-order condition that makes its command, source-state, environment,
exit-code, and log-path record a post-inventory record rather than a stale
pre-inventory record.  The retained dated venue/bibliography check, if used,
contributes only the dated readiness coordinate classified in
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.

Finally, regenerating \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after those
files and logs exist makes the digest table a deterministic SHA--256 function of
the same finite byte strings used by the inventory and verifier claims.  This is
exactly the ordered fixed-point construction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, so the two named issue
obligations are realized as local finite-record support coordinates.  The
current-instance sentence is obtained by reading the named post-inventory logs:
each finite verifier log has exit code zero, and the digest-generation log records
exit code zero for regenerating the final SHA--256 manifest after those logs
exist.  The negative part follows from the same fixed-point theorem and from
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}: none of the listed
finite rows contains the fields required for semantic proof checking, external
publication, source-theory rebuilds, daemon runs, or artifact-semantic reruns.
If an inventory byte changes later, the extractor log and final digest table no
longer name the changed byte string.  The fixed-point theorem then applies only
to the earlier byte tuple, so the current claim is recovered only by rerunning
the sequence and regenerating the digest rows.

The converse is the same finite-coordinate argument read backwards.  If either
inventory file was absent when a cited current extractor or verifier log was
produced, then that log has no finite input coordinate equal to the present
inventory byte string.  If the digest table predates one of the cited log bytes,
then the digest table cannot select that log byte as part of the same tuple.  In
either case the candidate support surface lacks one of the displayed finite
coordinates.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} supplies
that missing coordinate as the bad subrecord, so a pre-inventory or pre-digest
record cannot discharge the current fixed-point obligation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record current command-result closure]
\label{thm:current-command-result-closure}
Assume the current source package contains the accepted inventory files
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  After those
bytes exist, suppose that every command-result sentence retained for the
submission state cites one of the command-boundary rows in
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}, that the corresponding command log is
rerun from the source state named in that log with exit code zero, and that
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after all such logs
exist.  Then the command-result claims of the submission state are closed exactly
at their recorded finite level: each accepted claim has command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path, and every stronger reading not represented
by such a row remains only historical, conditional, path-verified, or absent as
specified by the row boundary.  In particular, the closed command-result surface
does not imply external upload, archive replacement, venue acceptance, Lean/BEDC
rebuild success, daemon execution, theorem-proof semantics, or dynamic artifact
validation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}, the command-result
sentences used by the current package are exhausted by the rows of
Table~\ref{tab:command-boundary-inventory}.  Each such row is a finite record
whose positive coordinates are the command, the named source state, the
environment, the exit code, and the log path, while its negative boundary states
which stronger assertions are not supplied.  The hypothesis that the retained
logs are rerun after the accepted inventory bytes exist makes those rows
post-inventory command records rather than pre-inventory or stale prose records.

The final digest regeneration adds the remaining byte coordinate.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, the inventory files, the
rerun command logs, and the regenerated digest manifest form the finite local
support fixed point for the edited package.  Therefore every accepted
command-result claim factors through an explicit row containing the five command
metadata fields required by Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}.
If a proposed reading asserts upload, archival replacement, venue acceptance,
source-theory rebuild success, daemon execution, theorem semantics, or dynamic
artifact validation, then it changes the evidence level or adds a semantic
coordinate not present in the row.  The finite-coordinate determination theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, then identifies the
missing coordinate as a finite bad subrecord, so the stronger reading is not
accepted.  The only surviving readings are precisely the historical,
conditional, path-verified, or finite command-result readings declared in the
row boundaries.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Current post-inventory support tuple instantiation]
\label{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
In the current source package, after \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} have been written and while the theorem-ledger support
schema reads only the declared extractor, verifier-log, and digest rows, the
ordered tuple consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_freshness_2026-06-09.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} instantiates the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} exactly when the
extractor and finite-record verifiers are rerun after the inventory files exist
and the final digest table is regenerated after those logs exist.  The resulting
coordinate is a finite local support tuple only unless the package also supplies
the external-upload receipt or archive-equivalence byte-equality locator of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}; it is not theorem
semantics, venue submission, archive replacement, Lean/BEDC rebuild evidence,
daemon evidence, or dynamic artifact-validation evidence.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The two inventory files are the finite byte coordinates whose absence blocks the
post-inventory fixed-point claim.  Once they exist, the theorem-environment
extractor reads \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}, and the
certificate and source-interface verifiers read the finite records specified in
their scripts and in Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}.
Running these commands after the inventory write therefore produces command-log
bytes whose input side includes the inventory state rather than a pre-inventory
state.

If \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is then regenerated after those
logs exist, each support input displayed before the digest manifest is selected
by a post-inventory byte row, and the digest manifest itself is the generated
finite selector for those rows.  Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} says precisely
that this ordered acyclic construction closes the first coordinate of the normal form in
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-refreshed-coordinate-instantiation} identifies the
same paths as the refreshed finite support tuple.  Hence the tuple instantiates
the current theorem-ledger support coordinate.

Conversely, if the inventory write, either verifier rerun, or digest
regeneration is missing or out of order, at least one tuple component is not a
post-inventory byte selected by the final digest manifest.  The exact-inclusion
coordinate would then require an unstated finite row, which is excluded by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  The final sentence
is the non-escalation boundary already proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Verifier and support-coordinate realization for the local evidence surface]
\label{prop:current-verifier-support-realization}
For the current local source state, the local theorem-ledger
coordinate is instantiated by the finite tuple consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_freshness_2026-06-09.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, provided these files are included
with the exact bytes selected by the final digest manifest.  In this source
state the root file \path{primary_claim_inventory.json} is only a byte-for-byte
alias for \path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json}; the canonical
support path remains the prefixed review-bundle path.  The same finite tuple does
not instantiate the external support coordinate: an external-review reading of a
bundle-backed claim additionally requires either an exact supplemental-upload
receipt for the selected support surface or an archive-equivalent public locator
with matching file list, relative-path semantics, manifest identity, digest rows,
and byte-equality evidence.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is precisely the ordered construction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}.  The two
inventory files are present before the retained extractor and verifier logs are
read as current command records.  The extractor log names
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py}, reads
\path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}, records zero omitted theorem
labels, and has exit code zero.  The retained certificate, source-interface, and
primary-claim verifier logs likewise have exit code zero and name their finite
input records.  Regenerating \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after
those log bytes exist selects the inventory files and logs as byte-level inputs
to the final local support surface.  Hence the tuple is the current local
theorem-ledger coordinate under
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.

For the alias claim, the root alias file adds no new evidence coordinate: it is
accepted only as a duplicate of the canonical bundle file.  Every load-bearing
primary-claim row in the manuscript is stated against
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json} and its freshness log.  If the
two files ever differ, byte equality fails and the alias sentence is no longer an
accepted support row; the canonical prefixed path remains the verifier input.

For the external-boundary claim, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  That corollary
lists the positive coordinates needed for external support: either the exact
supplemental-upload receipt or the archive-equivalent locator together with the
matching byte-equality fields.  The local tuple displayed above contains file
paths, command logs, exit codes, and digest rows, but it contains neither an
upload receipt nor the public byte-equality record required for an archive
replacement.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
therefore blocks any escalation from local/path-verified support to external
review support.  The current package may be supplied to reviewers by adding one
of those external coordinates, but until such a coordinate is present, no
bundle-backed claim in the theorem chain relies on external availability.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Byte-level stable replay criterion for the post-inventory tuple]
\label{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple}
Let $S$ be a source state of the present presentation package in which
the final accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}
exist.  Suppose
that the theorem-environment extractor, certificate-record verifier,
source-interface verifier, and retained primary-claim verifier are run from $S$,
that their logs have exit code zero, and that
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those logs are
written.  Then every later support claim for the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} factors through the
finite tuple of Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}:
the claim is valid for $S$ exactly as a byte-level replay of that tuple, and any
stronger claim must add a new command-result coordinate of the kind listed in
Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}.  If either inventory file
is later rewritten, this replay criterion applies only historically to the old
tuple until the extractor/verifier/digest sequence is run again from the new
source state.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The hypotheses reproduce the ordered construction required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Since the inventory files
exist before the four retained commands are run, the resulting logs are
post-inventory command records.  Since the digest table is regenerated after the
logs are written, the same finite byte strings are also selected by the final
SHA--256 surface.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
therefore identifies exactly the support coordinate available in $S$.

Now consider any later claim that cites the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} without adding new
records.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a local
support claim is determined only by its displayed finite coordinates.  The only
displayed coordinates under the hypotheses are the two inventory files, the four
post-inventory logs, and the regenerated digest table that selects those inputs.
Hence the later claim
can use no support surface beyond the tuple just identified.  To assert theorem
semantics, upload, archive replacement, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuilding, daemon
execution, or dynamic artifact validation would require additional command,
source, environment, exit-code, and log data; those are precisely the missing
coordinates isolated in Proposition~\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}.
Thus the replay criterion is stable and non-escalating.
A later inventory rewrite changes one of the support-input byte strings in the tuple.  Since
the regenerated digest table selects hashes of the old support inputs, the later
state has a different finite coordinate.  The criterion is
therefore stable under byte-level replay of the recorded tuple, but it is not an
automatic certificate for a changed inventory state.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Post-inventory freshness obstruction]
\label{prop:post-inventory-freshness-obstruction}
Let $S$ and $S'$ be two source states of the present package which differ in at
least one byte of \path{theorem_inventory.json} or \path{theorem_inventory.md}.
Suppose the theorem-environment extractor, certificate-record verifier,
source-interface verifier, retained primary-claim verifier, and final digest
generator were run from $S$ in the order required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Then those logs and digest
rows do not instantiate the theorem-inventory coordinate of $S'$.  The coordinate
for $S'$ is available exactly after the same extractor/verifier/digest sequence is
rerun from $S'$ and the digest manifest is regenerated after the new log bytes
exist.  Consequently the two source-support obligations consisting of the root
theorem-obligation ledger and the fresh verifier/digest support tuple cannot be
closed by a pre-inventory or stale-inventory command record.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} is a finite byte
tuple, not an isomorphism class of prose descriptions.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple}, a support claim based on
the post-inventory pass factors through the exact byte strings of the two
inventory files, the four retained command logs, and the digest table that was
generated after those logs.  If $S$ and $S'$ differ in either inventory file, then
the input byte tuple for $S'$ is not the input tuple selected by the digest rows
computed from $S$.  Equality of the finite support coordinate therefore fails.

The ordered construction in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} is also sufficient.  Rerunning
the extractor and the three finite-record verifiers from $S'$ makes their command
records post-inventory records for the $S'$ byte strings; regenerating
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after those logs exist selects the
new inventory and log bytes in the same finite tuple.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
then identifies that tuple as the current theorem-inventory coordinate, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} rejects any stronger
reading that omits one of these finite coordinates.  Thus stale logs prove only a
historical coordinate for $S$, and the current issue obligations close only by the
fresh sequence just described.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Accepted-inventory rerun realization]
\label{prop:stage-a2-accepted-inventory-rerun-realization}
For the accepted presentation-package state, the root inventory pair
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} is accepted as a
newly produced local theorem-obligation ledger only in the finite state in which
the following ordered tuple is present:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the accepted inventory bytes and the corresponding \path{main.tex} bytes;
\item a post-inventory run of
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py};
\item post-inventory retained runs of
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}; and
\item a regenerated \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} computed only
after the inventory, manuscript, and log bytes above exist.
\end{enumerate}
If this tuple is produced after the inventory files are written, then the two
issue coordinates named ``accepted-current \path{theorem_inventory.json}/\path{theorem_inventory.md}
pair'' and ``post-inventory rerun-and-digest tuple for newly accepted inventory
bytes'' are discharged exactly at local finite-record support level.  If any
member of the tuple is absent or predates the accepted inventory bytes, the same
issue coordinates remain open for current-byte support claims.  In neither case
does the tuple assert proof truth, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, artifact-semantic
validity, upload/archive support, venue compliance, or acceptance.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first item fixes the byte state to which the inventory ledger belongs.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coverage-criterion}, an extractor log is
an exact syntactic coverage coordinate only for the manuscript and inventory
bytes on which it was run; a pre-inventory log is therefore a historical row for
an earlier state and not a current-byte row for the newly accepted pair.  The
second item supplies this unique coverage coordinate for the newly written
inventory bytes.

The third item supplies the retained command-result coordinates classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  Each verifier contributes only
its finite input/output predicate, command, source state or hashes, environment,
exit code, and log path.  These rows do not depend on the semantic truth of the
manuscript's proofs and do not create any coordinate outside their printed
finite-record predicates.  The fourth item is then exactly the digest-ordering
requirement of Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}: the
digest surface must be generated after the bytes it selects, otherwise it is not
a digest for the accepted post-inventory state.

Combining the four items gives precisely the ordered tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}, hence a
local theorem-inventory support coordinate for the accepted presentation-package state.  If
one item is missing or stale, Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-freshness-obstruction}
identifies the first absent or stale byte/log/digest field as the obstruction to
current-byte closure.  Finally, the non-upgrade clause follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}: the tuple contains
only inventory paths, command logs, source-state/hash fields, exit codes, and
digest rows, while proof truth, fresh source rebuild, artifact semantics,
upload/archive support, venue compliance, and acceptance require independent
coordinates not present in the tuple.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Three-coordinate submission-support closure]
\label{prop:three-coordinate-submission-support-closure}
In the present presentation-only package, the three source-support obligations
consisting of the post-inventory theorem-obligation ledger, the dated
venue/bibliography verification record, and the external support surface admit
the following exact normal form.  The theorem-obligation coordinate is closed
precisely by the ordered tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}: the two
root inventory files exist, the theorem-environment extractor and retained
finite-record verifiers are rerun after those files exist, and the final digest
manifest is regenerated after the resulting log bytes exist.  The
venue/bibliography coordinate is either a dated local-readiness record with
command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path, or else all
venue-readiness language remains conditional or historical.  The external
support coordinate is either exact supplemental upload of the selected support
surface with matching final digests, or an archive-equivalent locator satisfying
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}; if neither field is
present, all bundle-backed support claims remain local/path-verified only.  No
finite record in one coordinate supplies either of the other two coordinates.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The theorem-obligation coordinate is a finite byte/log/digest field.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-freshness-obstruction}, any inventory write
changes the source state for that field and invalidates pre-inventory or
stale-inventory command records as current support.  Conversely,
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation} proves
that, after the two inventory files exist, rerunning the extractor and retained
finite-record verifiers and then regenerating the digest manifest produces
exactly the finite local support tuple for the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form}.  This proves the
first clause and also shows that no weaker pre-inventory row closes the current
theorem-obligation ledger.

The venue/bibliography field reads live external route and locator facts, not
the manuscript's theorem inventory.  Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} require a
dated record for any current route-readiness assertion and prevent that record
from becoming venue acceptance or an upload receipt.  Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}
is the command-result interface for such a row: the command, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path are the finite fields that make the row
auditable.  Hence, when such a row is retained, the manuscript may use it only
as dated local-readiness evidence; without such a row the only honest readings
are conditional or historical.

The external support field is separate again.  Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
classifies the finite records that instantiate external support: either the
selected support surface is actually uploaded with matching final digests, or a
public archive-equivalent locator supplies the required byte-equality fields.
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-no-receipt-support-surface-non-escalation} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-support-coordinate-dichotomy} rule out the
intermediate reading in which local digest rows, support-boundary text, or a
candidate branch path are treated as a completed upload or archive replacement.

The three fields have different finite domains: inventory and verifier bytes,
dated venue/bibliography locator metadata, and upload-or-archive byte-equality
metadata.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a
stronger submitted-support reading that omits any one of these finite fields has
a missing bad subrecord.  Therefore a post-inventory digest tuple proves no
venue compliance or external upload, a dated venue/bibliography row proves no
theorem-ledger fixed point or upload, and an upload-or-archive locator proves no
post-inventory rerun or live venue check unless the corresponding rows are also
present.  This is the claimed exact normal form.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local fixed point and external-support boundary]
\label{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary}
Assume that the current source state contains
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}, that the
theorem-environment extractor and the three retained finite-record verifiers are
rerun after those inventory files exist, and that
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after the resulting
logs are written.  Then the support tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation} is a
closed local fixed point for the theorem-inventory coordinate of the present
package.  This fixed point does not instantiate external support unless one of
the two external coordinates of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} is also supplied:
either exact supplemental upload with matching final digests, or an
archive-equivalent public locator with matching file list, path semantics,
manifest identity, SHA--256 rows, and pinned-commit or same-state branch-head
byte equality.  In the absence of such an upload receipt, DOI, completed
supplemental upload, or byte-equality locator, all bundle-backed and
theorem-inventory-backed claims remain local/path-verified only.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first three hypotheses are exactly the ordered construction required in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: the inventory files are
present before the extractor and finite-record verifiers run, their logs are
therefore post-inventory command records, and the final digest table is computed
only after those log bytes exist.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
then identifies the resulting tuple of inventory files, extractor log, verifier
logs, and digest manifest as the current finite support coordinate.  The replay
criterion of Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple} shows that
later uses of this coordinate factor through the same byte tuple unless a new
inventory write or a new command-result coordinate is added.  Hence the tuple is
closed as a local fixed point for the theorem-inventory coordinate.

The remaining assertion is the external-support separation.  The local tuple
contains byte paths, zero-exit command logs, and SHA--256 rows, but none of the
finite fields that Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
requires for external instantiation.  Exact upload requires the selected
supplemental surface to be supplied to the venue with matching final digests.
Archive replacement requires the public locator test of
Theorem~\ref{thm:public-branch-archive-equivalent-realization}: same finite file
list, same relative paths, same manifest identity, same digest rows, and an
immutable or same-state branch-head byte-equality record.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}, those
external coordinates cannot be inferred from the local bundle, bibliography row,
or digest table alone.  Therefore, unless one of the two external coordinates is
actually supplied, the closed fixed point remains local/path-verified and proves
no upload, DOI, archive replacement, venue acceptance, Lean/BEDC rebuild, daemon
rerun, or dynamic artifact-validation claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Current absence of external support-surface instantiation]
\label{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
For the present source package, the local post-inventory support coordinate of
Corollary~\ref{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary} and the digest manifest
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} do not instantiate the external
support coordinate of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  Hence every claim
whose support uses \path{review_bundle/} has only local/path-verified status in
this package unless a further finite record supplies one of the following two
positive coordinates:
\begin{enumerate}
\item an exact supplemental-upload receipt for the selected support surface with
matching final SHA--256 rows; or
\item a public archive-equivalent locator with the same file list, relative-path
semantics, manifest identity, digest rows, and pinned-commit or same-state
branch-head byte-equality record.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, a local digest row, support-boundary text, a candidate branch/path
locator, or a zero-exit local verifier log is never by itself an upload receipt,
DOI, completed supplemental upload, or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The local coordinate supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary} consists of the theorem
inventory bytes, the post-inventory extractor and finite-record verifier logs,
and the regenerated digest manifest.  Those fields are exactly the fields used
by Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} to close the local
theorem-inventory fixed point: path names, command metadata, exit codes, logs,
and SHA--256 rows.  None of these fields records a venue transaction, upload
receipt, DOI minting event, public archive locator, or public byte-equality
comparison.

Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} gives the exhaustive
normal form for external support in this paper.  Its first case requires the
selected supplemental surface to be uploaded with matching final digests, which
adds a finite upload coordinate absent from the local fixed point.  Its second
case requires a public locator together with file-list, path-semantics,
manifest-identity, digest-row, and pinned-commit or same-state branch-head
byte-equality fields; these fields are likewise absent from the local fixed
point.  The two cases are disjoint from mere local hashing because two ambient
states can have identical local digest rows and local verifier logs while
differing on whether a venue upload occurred or whether a public archive locator
has been byte-compared.

The finite-coordinate determination boundary,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, therefore prevents
any verifier or reader using only the local coordinate from inferring either
external coordinate.  Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-fixed-point-normal-form} already classify
the same missing fields as bad subrecords for stronger support readings.  Thus,
until one of the two positive external coordinates is actually supplied, every
\path{review_bundle/}-backed assertion remains local/path-verified and no listed
local record can be read as an upload receipt, DOI, completed supplemental upload,
or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Final support-coordinate refresh closure]
\label{prop:final-support-coordinate-refresh-closure}
Fix the selected 2026--06--13 venue/bibliography coordinate
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log}.
Suppose that, after the accepted bytes of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} exist, the commands \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py} are rerun under
Python 3.10.11 on Windows 10 with exit code \path{0} and with respective logs
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_verification_run.log}, and that
\path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json} names the same 2026--06--13
venue/bibliography log while
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those logs and
manifest bytes exist.  Then the current support state has exactly the following
closed local coordinates: the post-inventory theorem-obligation tuple, the
source-interface verifier tuple, the primary-claim verifier tuple, the selected
2026--06--13 venue/bibliography tuple, and the final digest tuple.  These
coordinates close the local support surface used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}; they do not add
the external-support coordinate unless an exact supplemental-upload receipt or an
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator is also supplied.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first hypothesis places the two inventory files before every command-log
coordinate that reads them.  The theorem-environment extractor therefore reads
the accepted inventory bytes rather than a pre-inventory ledger, and the three
finite-record verifiers produce command-result rows tied to the same source
state.  By Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple}, those ordered rows
are precisely the local post-inventory theorem-obligation coordinate.

The selected venue/bibliography coordinate is independent of that theorem-ledger
coordinate: its finite content is the dated 2026--06--13 check log and its
manifest pointer, not theorem semantics or external availability.  Requiring
\path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json} to name
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log} prevents the
current support surface from mixing an old manifest date with a new log date.
Regenerating \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after the verifier
logs and manifest bytes exist then selects the same finite byte strings in one
digest tuple.  Hence the listed local coordinates are mutually current at the
byte-record level and close the local support surface used in the
four-coordinate skeleton.

The final assertion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.
The ordered reruns, manifest pointer, dated venue check, and final digest rows
record local bytes and local command results only.  They contain neither a venue
upload receipt nor the file-list, path-semantics, manifest-identity, digest-row,
and pinned or same-state branch-head byte-equality fields required for an
archive-equivalent public locator.  Thus the refresh closes the local coordinate
and supplies no external-support instantiation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Manifest-required theorem-inventory fixed point]
\label{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}
Assume that \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json} names
\path{theorem_inventory.json} as the theorem-inventory coordinate and that the
accepted package contains both \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Suppose further that, after those two files are
written, the command
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} is run on the same
\path{main.tex} and exits with a log whose omitted-label count is zero, and that
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is then regenerated over the
accepted source, inventory, and review-bundle bytes.  Then the local support
surface has a closed theorem-inventory coordinate: every labelled
theorem-like environment in the extractor domain is represented in the accepted
JSON inventory, the Markdown inventory is a human-readable companion to the
same support coordinate, and the digest manifest is a post-inventory digest
rather than a pre-inventory placeholder.  No semantic proof-checking,
external upload, archive-equivalent public locator, or venue-acceptance
coordinate follows from this fixed point alone.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The manifest hypothesis first makes the JSON inventory a required finite file
coordinate rather than an optional reviewer note.  Because both inventory files
are present before the extractor is run, the extractor compares the current
label set from \path{main.tex} with the accepted JSON inventory bytes, not with
a missing or anticipated inventory.  The zero omitted-label count is therefore
exactly the syntactic coverage assertion isolated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}: it
covers the listed definition, lemma, proposition, theorem, and corollary
environments by label and asserts no truth of their statements.

Regenerating \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after the source,
inventory files, and refreshed log are present applies
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion} to the same finite byte
strings.  Hence the digest rows for the JSON inventory, Markdown inventory,
and theorem-environment extraction log are post-inventory rows.  The Markdown
file contributes only a readable mirror of the inventory coordinate; the
coverage property used by the extractor remains the JSON-label comparison.

Finally, the conclusion is local because every premise is a local path, local
command result, or local hash row.  The external-support alternatives remain
exactly those classified in Corollary~\ref{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary}:
an exact supplemental-upload receipt or an archive-equivalent byte-equality
locator must be supplied separately.  The same reasoning excludes semantic
proof-checking and venue acceptance, neither of which is one of the finite
coordinates supplied in the hypotheses.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record four-coordinate submission-support skeleton]
\label{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}
For the current presentation-only package, every support reading used by the
publication-safety theorem chain factors through the certificate-calculus spine of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine} and then through
exactly the following four finite coordinates, with no gluing between them unless
the missing coordinate is explicitly supplied.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-obligation coordinate is the post-inventory byte tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}, obtained
only when \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} exist
before the extractor and retained finite-record verifiers are rerun and before
the final digest manifest is regenerated.
\item The external-support coordinate is either exact supplemental upload or the
archive-equivalent public locator of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}; local digest rows,
local manifests, and bibliography notes alone do not instantiate it.
\item The imported BEDC source coordinate is the bounded pinned-snapshot
interface of Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}; stronger readings require
the exact added coordinate they assert, such as exact source text plus byte
equality, a public fetch-and-compare record, a Lean/BEDC rebuild record, or a
semantic-validation record.
\item The implementation-soundness coordinate for Lean builds, BEDC audits,
publication-daemon behaviour, and dynamic artifact validators is absent unless a
row records the command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path for
that actual gate program.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, after the post-inventory refresh is run and the selected
2026--06--13 venue/bibliography pointer is synchronized as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-support-coordinate-refresh-closure}, the present
manuscript may use the refreshed theorem-inventory tuple as local finite-record
support for the main theorem chain, but it still proves no upload, archive
replacement, public repository reachability, public byte equality, Lean/BEDC
rebuild, daemon rerun, or dynamic artifact-validation claim beyond rows
explicitly carrying those fields.  For any attempted stronger reading, the bad subrecord is the
inclusion-minimal finite subset containing the proposed stronger claim together
with the first missing coordinate among the four items just listed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The finite-record certificate calculus spine,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine}, reduces every support
reading to projection, obstruction, and positive finite extension.  The four
coordinates in the statement are the four projections that remain after that
normal form is applied to the current presentation-only support surface.

The first coordinate is isolated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Its construction is
ordered: the inventory bytes must exist, the syntactic extractor and retained
finite-record verifiers must run on that post-inventory state, and the digest
manifest must be computed after the resulting logs exist.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
identifies the resulting tuple, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple} shows that later uses of
the tuple are only byte-level replays unless the sequence is rerun from a new
source state.  Thus the theorem-obligation coordinate is available precisely at
the refreshed local finite-record level and not as theorem semantics or as an
external availability claim.

The second coordinate is separated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:support-surface-normal-form},
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.  Those results make
external support a finite field containing either exact venue upload of the
selected support surface or an archive-equivalent locator with matching file
list, path semantics, manifest identity, digest rows, and pinned or same-state
byte equality.  Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}
proves that local rows in \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, local
manifest fields, and support-boundary records do not contain those upload or locator
fields.  Hence this coordinate cannot be glued out of the refreshed theorem
inventory tuple.

The third coordinate is the source-interface boundary proved near the start of
the supplement.  Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} fixes
the imported records as path, pinned commit, line range, label, extraction date,
and bounded summary; Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} makes
that finite interface maximal for the present package; and
Theorem~\ref{thm:public-source-reachability-non-escalation} rules out upgrading
it to a current public-source reachability or public byte-equality claim without
a new finite fetch-and-compare record.  Therefore a local bundled snapshot and a
source-interface verifier log support only the bounded snapshot reading stated in
the theorem.

The fourth coordinate is exactly the implementation-soundness boundary.
Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface} requires command, source
state, environment, exit code, and log path for command-result claims;
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:submitted-gate-implementation-contract-dichotomy} state that
actual gate implementation soundness is obtained only by adding such rows for the
gate programs; and Theorem~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade}
prevents external finite records from implying that stronger interface.  The
command-result closure theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}, applies only to rows actually
rerun and recorded; it explicitly excludes Lean/BEDC rebuild success, daemon
execution, theorem-proof semantics, and dynamic artifact validation when those
rows are absent.

The four coordinates are independent finite fields of the package state.  If a
proposed support reading adds upload, archive replacement, public-source
reachability, public byte equality, source-theory rebuild success, daemon
execution, or artifact-semantic validation, then it changes at least one of the
four fields just listed.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} the missing field is a
finite bad subrecord, so the stronger reading is rejected.  Conversely, the
refreshed post-inventory tuple supplies exactly the first field, and the other
three fields remain at their conditional or absent levels as stated.  This is the
claimed skeleton and connects the closing support boundary back to the finite
publication-safety chain of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-local-support-state-reconciliation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local support synchronization and external-support normal form]
\label{cor:final-local-fixed-point-external-normal-form}
Assume the post-inventory execution order of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} has been instantiated for
the accepted bytes of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}: the theorem-environment extractor and retained
finite-record verifiers are rerun on that source state with zero-exit command
logs, and \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated only after
those logs and the selected manifest bytes exist.  Then the present package has
the terminal support normal form required by the publication-safety theorem
chain:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the theorem-obligation coordinate is a current local post-inventory fixed
point for the accepted inventory, extractor log, retained finite-record verifier
logs, and final digest rows; and
\item every claim whose support uses \path{review_bundle/} or the theorem
inventory remains local/path-verified and conditional with respect to external
support unless the finite support surface is enlarged by either an exact
supplemental-upload receipt with matching digest rows or an archive-equivalent
public locator with the file-list, relative-path, manifest-identity, digest-row,
and pinned-commit or same-state branch-head byte-equality fields.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the current-byte fixed point closes the local theorem chain but is
not itself a DOI, venue-upload receipt, public archive coordinate, venue
acceptance record, Lean/BEDC rebuild, daemon run, or dynamic artifact-validation
record.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is the positive branch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  Its hypotheses place the
accepted inventory bytes before the extractor and verifier command records, and
they place the final digest table after those command records.  Therefore the
support tuple read by
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation} is the
tuple for the present bytes rather than a pre-inventory or stale-log tuple.  The
stable replay statement of
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple} then says that subsequent
uses of this coordinate factor through those same byte strings until a new
inventory write or command-result coordinate is added.

The second assertion is independent of the first coordinate.  The local fixed
point records path names, source-state descriptions, environments, exit codes,
log bytes, manifest bytes, and SHA--256 rows.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, an external-support
reading requires one of two additional positive finite coordinates: an exact
supplemental-upload receipt, or an archive-equivalent public locator together
with file-list, path-semantics, manifest-identity, digest-row, and public
byte-equality fields.  Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
prove that these fields are absent from the local bundle records, verifier logs,
and digest manifest.

Thus the ordered rerun supplies exactly the local theorem-obligation coordinate
and no external-support coordinate.  The finite-coordinate determination
boundary, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, forbids
gluing the missing upload, archive, public byte-equality, formal rebuild, daemon,
or artifact-validation fields out of the local coordinate.  Hence the package is
closed for the local finite-record theorem chain and remains conditional for all
stronger external or semantic readings, as claimed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Accepted-byte post-inventory support coordinate]
\label{prop:accepted-byte-post-inventory-support-coordinate}
Let $S$ be a source-package state in which the accepted bytes of
\path{main.tex}, \path{submission_abstract.tex}, \path{source_interface_record.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json},
\path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}, and
\path{review_bundle/certificate_schema.json} are fixed.  Suppose that, after
those inventory bytes are fixed, the following command-result records are
written with exit code \path{0} against the same source state: the theorem
extractor \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py}, the
certificate verifier \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
the source-interface verifier
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and the
primary-claim verifier
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}.
Assume further that \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated
only after those command logs and \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}
are in their selected final bytes.  Then $S$ contains a single closed local
post-inventory support coordinate: the accepted inventory byte pair, the four
zero-exit finite-record logs, the manifest byte string, and the final digest
rows over those bytes.  This coordinate is sufficient for the local
theorem-obligation and finite-record freshness conclusions used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}.  It is not sufficient for,
and cannot be glued into, any external upload or archive-equivalence claim,
concrete gate-implementation soundness claim, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild or
axiom-purity claim, daemon-execution claim, or dynamic artifact-semantic
validation claim unless the corresponding separate upgrade coordinate named in
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure} is also supplied.
Moreover this local coordinate is inclusion-minimal for post-inventory freshness:
deleting the accepted inventory byte pair, any one of the four zero-exit logs,
the selected manifest bytes, or the final digest rows leaves a proper subrecord
from which the current local fixed-point conclusion is not determined.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first four listed commands are finite functions of the displayed source
files and their own program bytes.  A zero-exit extractor log states exactly the
syntactic theorem-environment coverage predicate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-byte-extractor-inventory-inclusion}.  The certificate,
source-interface, and primary-claim verifier logs state exactly the row-shape,
pointer, bounded source-interface, and primary-support predicates specified by
their verifier contracts.  Because the commands are run after the two theorem
inventory files exist, these logs read the accepted inventory bytes rather than a
pre-inventory placeholder.  Because the final digest file is regenerated after
the logs and manifest are fixed, the digest rows bind the selected final local
support surface rather than an earlier surface.

Thus the ordered tuple consisting of inventory bytes, command-result logs,
manifest bytes, and digest rows is closed under the local projections read by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point},
Proposition~\ref{prop:final-support-coordinate-refresh-closure}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:final-local-fixed-point-external-normal-form}.  Those results
are precisely the local theorem-obligation and finite-record freshness inputs
used by Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}, so the positive
local support conclusion follows.

The negative part is the finite-coordinate separation already proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}.  An upload receipt or
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator changes the external-support
field; concrete implementation soundness changes the program-specification,
trace, digest-binding, and implementation-pass fields; a Lean/BEDC rebuild or
axiom-purity audit changes the formal-source command-result field; daemon
execution changes the daemon-run field; and artifact semantics changes the
artifact-validation field.  Two package states can agree on the entire local
post-inventory tuple just constructed and disagree on any one of these upgrade
fields.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, no local
digest or finite-record verifier row determines such a stronger field.  Hence the
closed coordinate is exactly local and post-inventory, and every stronger reading
requires its separate finite upgrade coordinate.

It remains to check minimality.  If the inventory byte pair is deleted, two
states may have the same logs and digest table format while one log was produced
against a different inventory; the theorem-obligation coverage predicate for the
accepted inventory is then not determined.  If the extractor log is deleted, the
remaining rows do not determine that every in-domain theorem-like source label is
present in the inventory.  If the certificate, source-interface, or primary-claim
verifier log is deleted, the remaining rows do not determine the corresponding
finite row-shape, bounded source-interface, or primary-support predicate.  If the
manifest bytes are deleted, the support surface named by the digest rows is not
fixed.  If the final digest rows are deleted, the selected files are no longer
byte-bound as a single final support surface.  In each case one can change only
the deleted field and keep all remaining fields equal while changing the
post-inventory freshness predicate.  Therefore no proper subrecord determines the
local fixed point, proving inclusion-minimality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record package-surface no-free-upgrade closure]
\label{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}
In the present source state, the finite-record theorem chain has exactly the
following terminal form.  The local finite-record certificate level is available
only for the rows named by the submitted support tuple of
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}, after the
post-inventory rerun and digest-regeneration order of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  The central output of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} is therefore conditional
finite-record software-audit safety under record-gate soundness, not a proof of
the record-gate implementations or of the artifacts and source theories behind
their rows.  None of the five stronger readings below follows from that tuple.
\begin{enumerate}
\item External support for a bundle-backed claim requires either an exact
supplemental-upload receipt for the selected final support surface with matching
digest rows, or an archive-equivalent public locator with matching file list,
path semantics, manifest identity, digest rows, and pinned or same-state
byte-equality evidence.
\item Implementation soundness for an actual gate program requires, for that
program and not merely for the abstract record gate, source path, specification,
source digest or commit, invocation command, runtime environment, input records,
output records, exit code, log path, digest binding to the support surface, and
an assigned implementation-gate pass row.
\item A fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity claim for this submission state
requires the corresponding formal-source command row: source commit, source
paths, environment, command, exit code, log path, and the axiom-purity or marker
predicate checked by that command.  The bounded source-interface and Lean-marker
rows already present remain path-verified snapshot evidence only.
\item Dynamic artifact-validation semantics for finite witness rows requires a
fresh artifact-validation gate row naming the artifacts, validator source,
validator specification, source state, environment, command, exit code, and log
path.  Finite manifest rows and the Rule~110 status snapshot remain finite
witness records rather than semantic artifact-validity records.
\item Treating the supplement-level route normal forms
Theorems~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness} and
\ref{thm:presentation-route-stronger-reading-classifier} as primary-paper claims
requires no new evidence coordinate, but it exceeds the intended compact
presentation role.  In the CICM presentation route they are admissible only as
supplemental classifiers used to justify the short finite-record safety summary;
they are not additional end-to-end correctness claims and are not needed as
standalone primary-note conclusions.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover these five failures have a common minimal-obstruction normal form.  For
each stronger reading $d$ of an accepted current-package claim, there is a finite
coordinate $m(d)$ selected from: an external upload/archive locator; a
gate-implementation coordinate; a formal-source rebuild or axiom-audit command
row; an artifact-validation command row; or a presentation-placement coordinate.
The reading $d$ is accepted exactly when $m(d)$ is present with the pass records
specified in the corresponding item above.  If $m(d)$ is absent, the pair formed
by the finite stronger-reading tag for $d$ and the missing coordinate $m(d)$ is an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord: deleting the tag returns to the already accepted
finite-record reading, and filling $m(d)$ removes this obstruction while leaving
all other current-package checks unchanged.
Consequently any statement in the manuscript that appears to assert one of these
five readings is interpreted, for this submission state, as the corresponding
conditional upgrade statement above.  If the required coordinate is absent, the
statement projects back to the finite-record/path-verified reading and has an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord for the stronger claim.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton} shows that every
support reading factors through four independent finite coordinates: the local
theorem-obligation tuple, the external-support coordinate, the bounded
source-interface coordinate, and the implementation or dynamic-validation
coordinate.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-calculus-spine} then imply that a
stronger reading is accepted only by adding the finite fields that distinguish it
from the current projection; otherwise two support states can agree on all
currently read fields and disagree on the stronger fact.

For item~1, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} gives the
two and only two positive external-support normal forms.  Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
show that local digest rows, local manifests, and bibliography notes omit both an
upload receipt and an archive-equivalent byte-equality locator.  Hence the
listed external field is the missing bad subrecord for any unconditional external
support claim.

For item~2, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction},
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support},
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} separate the
abstract record-gate hypothesis from correctness of the programs that generate
or check rows.  Their proofs identify the necessary implementation coordinate:
program identity, specification, source state, command execution data,
input--output trace, digest binding, and assigned pass row.  Those fields are not
read by the current certificate projection unless a row explicitly carries them,
so implementation soundness cannot be inferred from certificate acceptance.

For item~3, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality},
Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} identify
the imported BEDC evidence as bounded path, pinned-snapshot, marker-existence,
and source-interface evidence.  A fresh rebuild or axiom-purity statement is a
command-result statement, so Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} require the command,
environment, source state, exit code, and log path for that formal-source gate.
Without those rows, the stronger formal-source reading is not determined by the
current projection.

For item~4, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} make finite witness rows
a manifest-level interface and make semantic artifact validity the unique
positive upgrade supplied by an artifact-validation gate.  The Rule~110 status
snapshot and finite manifests therefore witness only the recorded finite rows
unless the fresh validator coordinate named in the statement is supplied.

For item~5, Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-five-interface-sharpness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-stronger-reading-classifier} are already
finite-record projection theorems: they classify how stronger readings fail or
which finite budgets would make them accepted.  Reprinting that classifier as the
central contribution of the primary note would add no certificate coordinate and
would only duplicate the supplement-level normal form.  Hence the compressed
presentation use is exactly the finite-record safety sentence backed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and the support-boundary summary;
all route-normal-form detail remains available in the supplement.

The five cases exhaust the issue coordinates because the first four are the
independent fields in Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}
or its formal-source subfield, while the fifth is a presentation-placement
normal form for those same fields.  The displayed minimal-obstruction normal form
is then obtained by applying the finite bad-record argument separately in the
five coordinates.  In item~1, removing the external-support tag leaves a local
path-verified digest claim; adding the upload receipt or archive-equivalent
locator removes exactly that obstruction.  In item~2, removing the
implementation-soundness tag leaves the conditional record-gate reading of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}; adding the concrete program
coordinate is precisely the upgrade criterion.  In item~3, removing the
formal-source semantic tag leaves the bounded source-interface certificate of
