Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}; adding the rebuild or
axiom-audit command row is the missing finite field.  In item~4, removing the
artifact-semantic tag leaves the manifest/evaluator-record theorem; adding the
artifact-validation gate supplies the unique semantic upgrade.  In item~5,
removing the primary-placement tag leaves the supplement-level classifier cited
as support for the compact finite-record lesson; changing presentation placement
is the only missing coordinate.  Each pair is inclusion-minimal because
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} reads no smaller
coordinate capable of distinguishing the stronger support state from the current
projection.  The final sentence follows by applying the
minimal-bad-subrecord clause of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}
to the first missing field in the proposed stronger reading; in the fifth case no
missing evidence field is asserted, so the normal-form result is simply retained
as supplement-level support rather than elevated into an additional primary-paper
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Terminal five-coordinate closure for the presentation package]
\label{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}
For the CICM presentation-only source state, after the post-inventory rerun and
digest regeneration required by Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point},
the finite-record theorem chain is closed in the following sharp sense.  Every
accepted load-bearing claim factors through exactly one of the already named
finite coordinates: the local theorem-inventory tuple, the local/path-verified
support bundle, the bounded formal-source interface, the abstract record-gate
soundness premise, or the finite manifest/evaluator-witness rows.  Any reading
which instead asserts external submitted support, concrete gate-implementation
soundness, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity, dynamic artifact semantics,
or post-edit current-package freshness is accepted if and only if its own finite
upgrade coordinate is present with the command, source-state, environment,
exit-code, log-path, digest-binding, and pass-row fields specified in
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}.  If that coordinate is
absent, the stronger reading has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord and the
manuscript statement projects back to the bounded local finite-record reading.
Thus the main theorem chain proves exactly schema-relative publication-safety
under record-gate soundness and does not silently import external support,
implementation verification, proof-assistant rebuild success, or artifact-suite
validation from any local digest or manifest row.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The positive part is the conjunction of the four support coordinates classified
by Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton} together with
the post-inventory ordering of Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.
That theorem makes the theorem-inventory component current only after the two
inventory files exist, the extractor and retained finite-record verifiers have
been rerun from that state, and the final digest table has been regenerated after
the resulting log bytes exist.  Hence a post-edit freshness claim has no smaller
support coordinate than this byte/log/digest tuple.

For external support, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
give the exhaustive alternatives: an exact supplemental-upload receipt or an
archive-equivalent public locator with byte-equality and digest evidence.  Local
paths and local SHA--256 rows are not one of those alternatives, so omitting the
external coordinate leaves only local/path-verified support.

For concrete gates, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton} separate
the abstract record-gate-soundness hypothesis from program implementation
soundness.  Their common positive coordinate consists of program identity,
specification, source state, invocation and environment, input--output trace,
digest binding, log, exit status, and an assigned implementation pass row.  These
fields are disjoint from the abstract certificate rows used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.

For formal sources, Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} identify the
current Lean/BEDC material as bounded source-interface and marker vocabulary.
A rebuild or axiom-purity assertion is a command-result assertion, so
Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} require its own command,
environment, source-state, exit-code, log-path, and checked-predicate row.
Similarly, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} identify finite artifact
rows as manifest/evaluator-witness evidence only, with dynamic semantics supplied
only by a fresh artifact-validation coordinate.

The five stronger readings are therefore exactly the five cases of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}.  In each case, deleting
the stronger-reading tag returns to one of the accepted bounded coordinates just
listed, while adding the missing coordinate is precisely the positive criterion
for the stronger reading.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}
no finite verifier in the current projection can distinguish the stronger state
without reading such a coordinate.  The pair consisting of the stronger-reading
tag and the first absent coordinate is consequently inclusion-minimal, and the
remaining accepted content is exactly the schema-relative publication-safety
statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-issue coordinate normal form]
\label{thm:five-issue-coordinate-normal-form}
Let \(C\) be the current presentation-package claim set after the theorem
inventory files have been accepted.  Suppose the theorem-environment extractor,
the retained certificate-record verifier, source-interface verifier, and
primary-claim inventory verifier are rerun on those accepted bytes with recorded
commands, environments, exit codes, and log paths, and suppose the final digest
manifest is regenerated only after those logs exist.  Then the five issue
coordinates named by the finite support-boundary schema have the following complete
normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The post-inventory current-byte coordinate is present exactly as a local
syntactic and finite-record coordinate: it asserts equality of the accepted
inventory bytes, extractor input, verifier inputs, verifier logs, and digest
rows at this source state, and it asserts no theorem semantics.
\item The external support coordinate is absent unless an exact venue-upload
receipt, DOI-bearing supplement, completed supplemental upload, or
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator is supplied.
\item The fresh formal-source coordinate is absent unless a fresh Lean/BEDC
rebuild row or axiom-purity audit row is supplied for the relevant formal source.
\item The gate-implementation soundness coordinate is absent unless the concrete
implementation-audit tuple for each gate is supplied; record-gate soundness
remains an explicit hypothesis of the certificate calculus.
\item The dynamic artifact-validation coordinate is absent unless the evaluator
contract and fresh artifact-validation rerun logs are supplied.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently every accepted theorem in \(C\) factors through the local
post-inventory coordinate and the four bounded non-escalation boundaries above.
Any stronger reading of \(C\) has as its minimal bad subrecord the stronger-reading
row together with the first missing coordinate in items~2--5, while deleting that
row returns to the accepted path-verified finite-record claim.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first item is exactly the positive branch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-support-coordinate-dichotomy}, strengthened to
the current package by Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point},
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}.  The
ordered hypotheses ensure that the extractor and retained verifiers read the
accepted inventory bytes rather than an earlier ledger, and that the digest
manifest reads the resulting logs rather than pre-rerun bytes.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple}, this supplies precisely a
byte-level replay criterion for the local tuple and nothing semantic beyond the
finite rows it records.

Item~2 is Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:local-fixed-point-external-boundary}: local bundle paths,
manifest rows, and digest rows are not upload receipts, DOI records, completed
supplemental uploads, or public byte-equality locators.  Item~3 is the formal
source branch of Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}: path,
line, label, digest, and marker rows do not prove a fresh rebuild or axiom-purity
audit.  Item~4 is Theorem~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}: the
certificate calculus may assume record-gate soundness as an interface premise,
but concrete gate programs require a separate implementation tuple.  Item~5 is
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}: finite witness rows and case
snapshots are manifest-bounded evidence and become artifact-semantic evidence
only after the evaluator contract and fresh rerun coordinate are added.

For the final assertion, apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}.  That theorem classifies the
same five axes by finite coordinates and proves the no-free-upgrade rule by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  The post-inventory
axis has been positively instantiated by the ordered reruns in the first
paragraph; the remaining four axes lack their positive coordinates by items~2--5.
Thus each stronger reading is rejected by the inclusion-minimal pair consisting
of the attempted stronger-reading row and the first absent coordinate it needs,
and the original claim set factors through the accepted finite-record projection.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Support-coordinate closure for bounded theorem evidence]
\label{prop:bounded-theorem-support-coordinate-closure}
Let \(C\) be the current presentation-package claim set and let \(S\) be the
submitted finite support surface after \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} have been written.  Suppose that the theorem
environment extractor, the certificate-record verifier, the source-interface
verifier, and the primary-claim verifier are rerun from this post-inventory
state with recorded zero-exit logs, and that
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated only after those log
bytes and the selected \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json} bytes are
fixed.  Suppose also that \(S\) contains no supplemental-upload receipt and no
archive-equivalent public locator accompanied by file-list, digest-row,
manifest-identity, path-semantics, and public byte-equality records.  Then the
accepted projection of \(C\) is exactly the following bounded interface:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the post-inventory theorem-ledger and verifier freshness coordinate is
present as a local byte/log/digest coordinate;
\item every bundle-dependent support assertion is local/path-verified rather
than externally supported; and
\item every publication-safety assertion remains conditional on the explicit
record-gate-soundness predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), with no
unconditional gate-implementation or end-to-end workflow-correctness conclusion.
\end{enumerate}
Conversely, any strengthening of this projection that asserts external bundle
support, concrete gate-implementation soundness, or unconditional end-to-end
correctness is accepted by the finite-record theorem chain only after adding the
corresponding missing coordinate named above; without it, the strengthening is
rejected by the inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting of the strengthening
tag and that absent coordinate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first clause is the positive branch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:five-issue-coordinate-normal-form}.  Its hypotheses are ordered:
the two inventory files exist before the extractor and verifier commands are
rerun, and the final digest manifest is generated only after the resulting logs
and selected manifest bytes exist.  Therefore the extractor and verifier rows
read the accepted inventory bytes rather than a pre-inventory placeholder, and
the digest rows bind the inventory files, the post-inventory logs, and the
selected manifest bytes.  This proves exactly a local byte/log/digest freshness
coordinate, not theorem semantics or external availability.

For the second clause, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.
Those results classify the two ways a bundle-dependent assertion can become an
external-support assertion: either by an exact supplemental-upload receipt or by
an archive-equivalent public locator together with the file-list, digest-row,
manifest-identity, path-semantics, and public byte-equality records.  By
hypothesis neither positive coordinate is present in \(S\).  Local paths, a local
manifest, and local digest rows therefore determine only the local/path-verified
support projection.

For the third clause, the core publication-safety theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, has record-gate soundness as an
explicit hypothesis.  Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}
identify this hypothesis with a finite row-and-pointer predicate and state that
it imports no implementation-level, semantic, fresh-execution, or venue claim not
present as a finite coordinate.  Theorems~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction}
and~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton} then give the
matching positive coordinates needed to upgrade a record-gate assertion to a
concrete implementation-soundness assertion.  Since those coordinates are not
part of the stated support surface, the theorem chain remains conditional at the
record-gate interface and cannot be read as an unconditional end-to-end
correctness theorem.

It remains to prove the converse rejection statement.  Each of the three
forbidden strengthenings changes a coordinate read by the stronger-reading
preorder: an external-support tag, a gate-implementation-soundness tag, or an
unconditional end-to-end-correctness tag.  The finite-coordinate determination
boundary, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, says that a
finite verifier cannot distinguish the stronger state from the accepted bounded
projection without reading the added coordinate.  Hence, when the matching
coordinate is absent, deleting every unrelated field leaves the same failure; the
strengthening tag together with the first absent required coordinate is an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  Adding that coordinate is exactly the positive
extension case already listed in Theorem~\ref{thm:five-issue-coordinate-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Supplemental schema-relative weak-interface maximality]
\label{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}
For the technical supplement to the CICM presentation-only package, the finite
schema is the five-channel
normal form obtained from \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}\),
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:five-issue-coordinate-normal-form}.  The preorder is the
schema-relative finite-record preorder of
Definitions~\ref{def:finite-record-projection-preorder} and
\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}; the only positive upgrade steps
available are the displayed finite coordinates for record-gate safety,
implementation/script soundness, formal-source rebuilding, dynamic artifact
validation, external support, theorem truth, and venue state.  Minimal bad
subrecords are inclusion-minimal relative to those finite coordinates, and this
supplement-level exhaustiveness claim is schema-relative: it classifies exactly the five weak
interfaces listed below and does not classify unsubmitted semantic states.  Let
\(Q\) be any load-bearing reading
whose asserted support is one of the following five challenged weak interfaces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the conditional publication-safety interface under record-gate soundness;
\item a named publication-boundary, projection-contract, or
gate-implementation-upgrade-boundary theorem in the finite-record chain;
\item the imported BEDC/newmath source interface;
\item the four finite case-study and artifact witness rows; or
\item the theorem-inventory and theorem-environment extractor interface.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(Q\) is accepted by the manuscript's finite-record theorem chain exactly at
its bounded interface level.  More precisely, the accepted projection of \(Q\) is
respectively: conditional certificate safety under the explicit
record-gate-soundness premise; finite input/output and projection-contract
classification for the publication-boundary and gate rows; bounded source
path/commit/line/summary evidence; historical path-verified snapshot and finite
witness-row evidence; or syntactic theorem-obligation indexing.  A stronger
reading of \(Q\) is accepted only after adding its matching upgrade coordinate: a
concrete gate-implementation audit tuple, a concrete compiler or script
implementation-soundness tuple, a fresh formal-source rebuild or axiom-audit
command row, a fresh dynamic artifact-validation command row, or a
proof-checking/theorem-truth coordinate outside the inventory extractor.  If the
matching coordinate is absent, the pair
consisting of the stronger-reading tag and that missing coordinate is an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord, and deleting the tag returns to the accepted
bounded interface reading.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The five items are projections of the terminal five-coordinate closure.  For the
publication-safety interface, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
assumes the finite predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_S(P,L,\Gamma)\) and
Theorems~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction} and
\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} prove that concrete gate
program soundness requires its separate implementation coordinate.  Thus the
accepted projection is conditional certificate safety, and the stronger
implementation reading has exactly the missing implementation tuple as its bad
subrecord.

For the named publication-boundary and implementation-boundary theorems,
Theorem~\ref{thm:auditable-compiler-boundary-completeness} proves only the
surjective finite input/output classifier for the publication-boundary interface,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} proves only the
projection-contract boundary for the submitted four-script verifier surface, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton} names the
six finite coordinates required before a row-level gate reading can be upgraded
to gate-implementation soundness.  These theorems do not assert truthful
production of the scripts, semantic adequacy of a compiler, clean-machine
reproducibility, or soundness of the underlying gate programs.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, any such reading
is accepted only after the submitted surface contains the concrete
implementation-soundness extension tuple, with source, specification, execution,
negative-test, reproducibility, and proof-link coordinates as appropriate.
Without that tuple the stronger implementation tag and the first absent member of
the tuple form the finite bad subrecord, while the bounded classifier or
projection-contract reading remains accepted.

For imported BEDC/newmath evidence,
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} identify the
maximal record available from the source-interface rows: path, pinned commit,
label, line range, extraction date, bounded summary, and evidence-level
qualifier.  A fresh rebuild, axiom-purity audit, exact source-statement import,
or semantic completeness assertion is not a function of those fields and is
accepted only by the formal-source command coordinate described in
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}.  Hence its bad
subrecord is the stronger formal-source tag together with that absent coordinate.

For the case-study and artifact rows,
Propositions~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} and
\ref{prop:review-bundle-case-snapshot-coverage},
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}, and
Proposition~\ref{audit:case-snapshot-non-rerun-boundary} give exactly historical
path strings, reviewer-visible snapshots, manifests, and finite witness rows.
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} makes dynamic artifact
semantics depend on a fresh artifact-validation coordinate.  Therefore live
current-daemon or artifact-semantics readings are precisely the stronger tag plus
the absent validator/run coordinate.

For theorem inventories,
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction}, and
Theorem~\ref{prop:manual-theorem-inventory-boundary} prove deterministic
syntactic coverage and theorem-obligation indexing only.  The inventory has no
field for proof checking, theorem truth, Lean/BEDC rebuilding, or semantic
validity.  Such a reading is accepted only after adding a separate proof-checking
or formal-source coordinate; without it, the stronger tag and absent coordinate
are the minimal bad subrecord.

The inclusion-minimality and the absence of any smaller gluing route are exactly
the finite-record normal-form argument of
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form}, together with the
finite-coordinate determination argument of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, instantiated through
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:five-issue-coordinate-normal-form}.  In each of the five cases,
removing the stronger-reading tag leaves one of the bounded projections proved
above, while filling the named coordinate is the positive upgrade criterion
already classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure}.
Thus the weak interfaces are not loose disclaimers: they are maximal finite-record
interfaces with classified upgrade budgets.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Primary presentation weak-interface compression]
\label{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression}
For the compact CICM presentation paper, the preceding supplemental maximality
theorem is used only through the following compressed consequence.  Every
reviewer-facing claim that mentions record-gate safety, a named finite-script or
implementation-boundary row, imported source-interface evidence, a finite case
witness, or a theorem inventory has exactly its bounded finite-record projection;
any implementation-soundness, fresh formal-source, artifact-semantic,
proof-truth, clean-machine reproducibility, external-support, or venue-status
reading requires its own positive upgrade coordinate.  If that coordinate is not
present, the stronger reading has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting
of the stronger-reading tag and the first absent upgrade coordinate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} to the five
challenged interfaces and then forget the handwritten finite-coordinate taxonomy
except for its output projection and first-missing-coordinate witness.  The
accepted projections listed in the theorem are exactly the five bounded readings
named in the statement: conditional record-gate certificate safety, finite-script
or implementation-boundary projection contracts, source path/commit/line/summary
evidence, historical path-verified case evidence, and syntactic theorem-inventory
coverage.  The theorem's converse clause says that every stronger reading in the
listed families is accepted only by adding the matching upgrade coordinate and,
when absent, is rejected by the corresponding inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
This corollary is therefore a compressed consequence of the supplemental
schema-relative classifier, not a new exhaustive taxonomy for unsubmitted
semantic states.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No finite-record gluing upgrade]
\label{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}
Under the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}, no conjunction of two or
more bounded accepted interfaces among the five listed channels yields a stronger
implementation-soundness, fresh formal-source, dynamic artifact-validation,
proof-checking, clean-machine reproducibility, or venue-acceptance claim unless
the matching upgrade coordinate for that stronger claim is itself present and
accepted.  Equivalently, the positive content of the package is closed under
finite conjunction only inside the product of the five bounded projections; every
cross-channel stronger reading has at least one of the named upgrade coordinates
as an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Each accepted bounded channel in
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} is a projection of the
finite schema coordinates read by the verifier.  A finite conjunction of such
channels therefore adds no new coordinate: it records several already accepted
projections in the same finite support surface.  If a proposed conclusion is still
inside those projections, it is exactly the corresponding bounded finite-record
claim and is already covered by the theorem.

Suppose instead that the conjunction is read as a stronger cross-channel claim,
for example as implementation soundness of a gate or compiler, a fresh BEDC/Lean
rebuild, semantic validation of an artifact row, theorem-body proof checking,
clean-machine reproducibility, or venue acceptance.  By the case analysis in
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}, each such reading
queries a coordinate not contained in at least one bounded channel: respectively
the concrete implementation tuple, the formal-source command or axiom-audit row,
the artifact-validation command row, the proof-checking/theorem-truth coordinate,
the reproducibility command/environment/log tuple, or the external venue-support
coordinate.  The finite-coordinate determination theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, says that a verifier
which reads only the old projections cannot distinguish two ambient states that
agree on them but differ on the new queried coordinate.  Hence the stronger claim
is not determined by the conjunction of bounded projections.

When the matching upgrade coordinate and its assigned pass rows are added,
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure} gives the positive
finite-extension case.  When it is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} and the final clause of
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} classify the stronger tag
together with the missing coordinate as an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  Thus
bounded interfaces cannot be glued into a stronger claim for free.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Four-family upgrade-obstruction classification]
\label{thm:four-family-upgrade-obstruction-classification}
Fix the submitted finite surface $S$, acceptance ledger $L$, dispatch table
$\Gamma$, and verifier tuples of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}.
Consider a load-bearing use in this manuscript belonging to one of the following
four families:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a portable, presentation-compressed, publication-safety, weak-interface, or
six-role publication interface theorem;
\item a named concrete-script or gate-row result whose label or title uses
``soundness'' but whose hypotheses expose only parsed finite inputs, printed
predicates, exit codes, and declared implementation-projection coordinates;
\item an imported-source result whose evidence is the pinned newmath path,
commit, line interval, bounded summary table, mirrored JSON row, and bundled
source snapshot; or
\item a venue or bibliography readiness result whose evidence is a dated local
record rather than an upload-time venue check.
\end{enumerate}
Then the accepted content of the use is completely classified by the bounded
projection named in the corresponding row below:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{family} & \text{accepted projection} & \text{first upgrade coordinate}\\
\hline
1 & \Pi_{\mathrm{pres}},\ \Pi(c),\ \mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L),\ \mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma,S}(L)
  & \text{object-theory, end-to-end, or external-support coordinate}\\
2 & \text{finite parsed-input/printed-predicate projection}
  & \text{implementation-projection tuple}\\
3 & \text{bounded source-interface row}
  & \text{fresh source-statement, formal-build, axiom-audit, or semantic row}\\
4 & \text{historical dated readiness row}
  & \text{upload-time venue/bibliography freshness row.}
\end{array}
\]
For each family, a stronger reading is accepted by the manuscript's finite-record
calculus if and only if the upgrade coordinate in the third column, together with
its assigned passing gate rows, is added to $S$.  If the coordinate is absent,
the stronger-reading tag together with that first missing coordinate is an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  Consequently the four families are finite-record
software-method interfaces over concrete artifacts and dated records; they are
not new object-language mathematics, end-to-end proof-system soundness,
whole-program implementation soundness, Lean/BEDC rebuilds, semantic source
completeness, or submission-time venue compliance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each listed family is already a projection of the same finite certificate
calculus, so the proof is a case analysis on the first coordinate not read by the
bounded projection.

For family~1, Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface} defines
$\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}(S,L,\Gamma)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface}
defines the six-role record $\Pi(c)$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} constructs the accepted certificate
set and bad-subrecord report under the explicit record-gate-soundness premise.
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} gives the converse:
semantic object-theory content, external support, venue state, implementation
soundness, and end-to-end workflow correctness are accepted only after their
matching finite coordinates are added.  Hence the first row of the table is
exactly the accepted projection and its upgrade boundary.

For family~2, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}
is read through its statement: the concrete scripts are checked only against the
finite fields they parse and the predicates they print.  Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton}
separates the six finite input coordinates needed even for a gate-implementation
projection, and Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}
is the positive-and-negative criterion for adding them.  Thus the word
``soundness'' in these labels denotes schema-relative projection exactness for a
finite script record until the implementation-projection tuple is present; the
whole-program or gate-soundness reading has that tuple as its first missing
coordinate.

For family~3, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} fixes the
pinned path, commit, line intervals, extraction date, and bounded summaries;
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency} compares the
printed table with the machine-readable row; and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} states the maximal positive
content of those rows.  Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
then proves that exact source-statement import, a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, axiom
purity, and semantic source-theory validation are distinct coordinates.  Holding
the bounded row fixed while changing one of those stronger facts changes no
accepted source-interface projection, so the first missing stronger source
coordinate is precisely the minimal obstruction.

For family~4, Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion} defines the
fresh venue-record criterion, Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}
prevents a dated local rule check from escalating to later venue compliance, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} requires a
fresh upload-time coordinate for submission-time compliance.  Proposition~\ref{prop:dated-venue-record-instantiation}
therefore supplies only a historical dated readiness instance.  Changing the
future venue page, bibliography state, upload receipt, or submission date while
leaving the dated row fixed changes the stronger claim without changing the
accepted projection, so the upload-time venue/bibliography freshness row is the
first missing coordinate.

The four cases exhaust the theorem's families.  In each case, when the third-column
coordinate and its assigned passing gate rows are added, the positive extension
direction of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}, specialized by
the implementation, source-interface, and venue theorems just cited, accepts the
stronger row at its declared level.  When it is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} supplies two ambient
states agreeing on the bounded projection and differing on the stronger fact, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} reduces the rejected
claim to the stronger tag plus the first missing coordinate.  Removing either
component destroys the stronger claim or its failure, so the bad subrecord is
inclusion-minimal.  The final sentence is exactly the conjunction of these four
bounded projections and their non-escalation clauses.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Certificate-reading spine maximality]
\label{thm:certificate-reading-spine-maximality}
Let $P$ be a CICM presentation-only package with submitted finite surface $S$,
acceptance ledger $L$, dispatch table $\Gamma$, and verifier tuple
$\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ as in
Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}.  Assume the record-gate
soundness predicate $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ and assume that the compact
article cites only the reviewer-facing spine consisting of
Theorems~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface},
\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine},
and \ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, together with the portable support
projections
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:portable-workflow-schema-factorisation}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:portable-method-normal-form-local-pullback}.  Then the
positive content of that entire spine is exactly the certificate-reading
projection
\[
\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)=
\bigl(
\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma),
\mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L),
\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma,S}(L),
\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}(S,L,\Gamma),
\Pi(c)
\bigr),
\]
where $\mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ is the accepted finite certificate set,
$\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ is the finite bad-subrecord report,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}$ is the five-coordinate presentation projection, and
$\Pi(c)$ is the six-role record of
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface}.  In particular, the spine proves
certificate reading under record-gate soundness for the submitted finite rows.  It
does not prove implementation soundness, artifact semantics, Lean or BEDC build
soundness, source-theory truth, clean-machine reproducibility, external archive
availability, upload-time venue compliance, venue acceptance, or end-to-end
workflow correctness.

Moreover this boundary is sharp in the schema-relative finite-record preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:finite-record-projection-preorder}.  Any sentence whose conclusion is not a
function of $\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord:
the stronger tag together with the first missing coordinate among, respectively,
an implementation-projection tuple, a semantic artifact-validation tuple, a
formal-source command or axiom-audit tuple, a source-theorem truth/import tuple, a
clean-machine replay tuple, an external upload or archive-equivalence tuple, a
venue-status tuple, or an end-to-end workflow-correctness budget.  Adding exactly
that coordinate and its assigned passing gate rows is, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form}, the unique finite-record
way to upgrade the corresponding conclusion inside this calculus; without it, no
finite conjunction of the cited spine and portable-support projections yields the
stronger reading.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypotheses place every cited label inside one of the bounded projections
already classified.  Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} reads the
finite surface, ledger, dispatch table, and verifier tuple under
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ and constructs exactly
$\mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ together with the bad-subrecord list
$\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$.  Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface}
projects these data, the axis map, and the boundary fields to
$\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}(S,L,\Gamma)$.  Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine}
states that the compact spine has no other publication-safety normal form under
the same record-gate premise.  Finally,
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface} expresses the accepted claim
through the six roles $\Pi(c)$, while
Propositions~\ref{prop:portable-workflow-schema-factorisation} and
\ref{prop:portable-method-normal-form-local-pullback} show that replacing local
paths, tool names, and route directories preserves only the seven sorted fields
and their six-role pullback.  Therefore the listed tuple
$\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ contains every coordinate read by the cited theorem
spine and portable support projections.

Conversely each coordinate of $\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$ is constructed by one
of those cited results: record-gate soundness is the premise, the output and bad
records are constructed by the publication-safety theorem, the five-coordinate
projection is constructed by the compressed-interface theorem, and the six-role
record is constructed by the portable six-role theorem.  Thus the positive
content of the spine is exactly certificate reading for the submitted finite
rows.  The negative list in the statement follows because none of the
listed stronger conclusions is a coordinate of
$\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$: each asks about an implementation, semantic
artifact, formal build, source-theory truth, replay environment, external support
locator, venue state, or whole-workflow budget not read by the finite certificate
projection.

For sharpness, take any proposed stronger sentence not determined by
$\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)$.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form}, the stronger sentence has a
least missing coordinate in the finite-record preorder whenever its required
domain properly contains the domain of \(\mathsf{Read}_{\Gamma,S}(L)\).  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, two ambient workflow
states can agree on all coordinates read by the finite verifier while disagreeing
on the first unsubmitted coordinate queried by the stronger sentence.  Therefore
the old verifier cannot accept that stronger conclusion without also accepting it
in an ambient state where the queried fact fails.  The obstruction skeleton of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} identifies the stronger
tag and this first missing evidence, pass, boundary, command-run, promotion, or
extension field as an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  If the missing coordinate
and its assigned passing gate rows are added, the extension criterion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-no-free-upgrade-closure} gives the corresponding
positive finite-record upgrade; if it is not added,
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} rules out obtaining it by
conjoining bounded spine and support projections.  This proves both maximality
and the claimed unique upgrade route.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Support: conditional RGS six-role publication interface]
\label{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}
Assume the finite submitted surface, ledger, dispatch table, record-gate
soundness, discovery-input, promotion-boundary, verifier-boundary, and
case-snapshot hypotheses used in
Theorems~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, and
\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity}, and the certificate-reading maximality
classification of Theorem~\ref{thm:certificate-reading-spine-maximality}.  Then the CICM presentation package
has the following six-role support interface for the master presentation theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface}.  Theorems~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality},
\ref{thm:certificate-reading-spine-maximality},
\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support},
\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton},
\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion},
\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality},
\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity},
\ref{prop:presentation-case-matrix-sufficiency}, and
\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}; the final route classification is
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-dichotomy}.  These are support-coordinate results for
the six clauses below, not separate stronger claims.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every accepted load-bearing claim factors through a finite six-role record
\(\Pi(c)=(S_c,F_c,W_c,A_c,G_c,M_c)\) consisting of source object, formal
interface, finite evidence row, advisory agent action, deterministic gate, and
human promotion boundary.
\item The publication checker constructs exactly the finite certificate
\(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) for that six-role record and a finite list
of bad subrecords for rejected stronger readings.
\item The only implementation-positive content currently supplied by the named
four-script verifier surface is finite-script projection-contract exactness: on
the parsed finite projection, exit code \(0\) is exact for the printed finite
predicate of the named script and no predicate outside that projection is
certified.
\item The imported BEDC/newmath discovery-gate content is exactly the bounded
source-interface certificate: pinned path, pinned commit, label, line range,
extraction date, bounded summary, evidence-level qualifier, and the finite
record-comparison fields.  It is not exact import of the full source theorem
statements, a Lean/BEDC rebuild, an axiom-purity audit, or semantic validation
of the imported source theory.
\item The supplemental support coordinate is conditional on exact inclusion of
the selected support bytes in the submitted package, or on an archive-equivalent
locator whose byte-equality fields pass the stated file-list, path-semantics,
manifest, digest, and pinned-state checks.  Local digest rows and branch/path
notes are not by themselves DOI, upload-receipt, public-archive, or
venue-compliance claims.
\item The four case studies are accepted only as historical/path-complete
illustrations with the finite matrix coordinates gate, observed issue, accepted
coordinate, and safe lesson; they are not live daemon reruns, benchmarks,
artifact-semantic validations, or empirical system-validation claims.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover this interface is maximal.  Any reading which strengthens one of these
six conclusions to whole-program implementation soundness, fresh formal-source
or Lean/BEDC rebuilding, dynamic artifact validation, live case-study rerun,
clean-machine reproducibility, public archive/upload status, venue acceptance,
theorem-truth checking, or an empirical claim about current system behaviour is
accepted by the finite-record calculus if and only if the submitted surface adds
the matching upgrade coordinate with its assigned passing gate rows.  If that
coordinate is absent, the stronger tag together with the first absent coordinate
is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord, while the bounded six-role conclusion
above remains accepted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For an accepted claim \(c\),
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface} constructs the six-role record
\(\Pi(c)\) and proves invariance under replacement of local path and route names
by role-preserving records.  Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
then constructs from the same submitted fields the certificate
\(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\), and
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} identifies verifier acceptance
with the six finite schema predicates for that tuple.  This proves the first two
items and shows that rejected stronger readings are represented by finite bad
subrecords rather than by informal reviewer judgment.

For the implementation clause, the support-coordinate results are deliberately
projection-scoped.
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} applies to the
submitted four-script family and states exactly the parsed-projection contract:
the accepted exit-code row is exact for the script's printed finite predicate on
the fields read by that script.  Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} prove the
necessity and sufficiency of the additional finite-input implementation
projection coordinates before any gate row is upgraded even to that bounded
implementation-projection reading.  Hence no whole-program implementation,
runtime, or semantic claim is supplied by the current script rows.

For the imported-source clause, the support-coordinate results are deliberately
bounded to source-interface records.
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} identify the complete
positive source content available to this chain: the path, commit, labels, line
ranges, extraction date, bounded summaries, JSON/table/manifest agreement, and
label containment in the bundled snapshot intervals.  The same maximality
theorem proves that exact source-statement import, Lean/BEDC rebuilding,
axiom-purity auditing, and semantic source-theory validation are strictly
stronger readings requiring their own finite source-statement, formal-build,
command-run, axiom-audit, or semantic-check coordinates.  Thus the master
interface reads the BEDC/newmath rows as bounded certificate input, not as a
complete BEDC exposition or rebuild.

For the support-availability clause, the support-coordinate results separate
local byte identity from external availability.
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} lists the only two
ways to instantiate external support in this manuscript: exact supplemental
upload of the selected support surface with matching final digests, or an
archive-equivalent locator with the stated byte-equality and path-semantics
fields.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that the current local digest rows, support-boundary text, branch/path
notes, and zero-exit verifier logs do not instantiate either coordinate.  Hence
the master interface may use support records only as exact-inclusion or
archive-equivalence conditions; it does not assert a DOI, upload receipt, public
byte-equality proof, or venue compliance.

For the case-study clause, the support-coordinate results are deliberately
historical and illustrative.
Theorem~\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity} factors each case row through
one of the four historical skeleton lessons, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:presentation-case-matrix-sufficiency} displays the exact
presentation matrix.  The finite-row closure theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}, says that these rows close
under the finite path-verified evidence level only; a live rerun, benchmark,
artifact-semantic validation, or empirical current-system conclusion changes the
boundary or artifact coordinate and therefore is outside the submitted row.

It remains only to prove maximality across the six clauses.  A stronger reading
changes either a six-role component, an evidence level, an implementation
projection, a formal-source or proof-checking coordinate, an artifact or case
rerun coordinate, a reproducibility coordinate, or an external support/venue
coordinate.  If the corresponding coordinate and pass rows are added, the
positive-extension direction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} accepts the
enlarged finite record at its declared evidence level.  If it is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} identifies the missing
upgrade coordinate for each channel, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} rules out obtaining it by
conjoining bounded accepted projections.  The finite-coordinate determination
theorem supplies two submitted states agreeing on the bounded record but
differing on the absent stronger fact, so the stronger claim is not determined
by the old projection.  The obstruction-skeleton theorem then gives the
stronger tag and the first absent coordinate as an inclusion-minimal bad
subrecord.  Therefore the theorem is both positive for the submitted six-role
finite-record method and sharp against all listed upgrades.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compressed master boundary classifier]
\label{thm:compressed-master-boundary-classifier}
Let \(P\) be the CICM presentation-only package with finite submitted surface
\(S\), acceptance ledger \(L\), dispatch table \(\Gamma\), and record-gate
soundness predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\).  Assume the discovery-input,
promotion-boundary, verifier-boundary, case-snapshot, and support-coordinate
hypotheses used by Theorems~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}, and
\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}.  Then the compact
presentation theorem surface has a unique maximal finite-record reading
\[
\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma,S}(P,L)=
\bigl(\Pi(c),\mathcal C(c),\mathsf{ImplProj}_{S},
\mathsf{SrcBound}_{S},\mathsf{Supp}_{S},\mathsf{Neg}_{S}\bigr)_{c\in
\mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L)},
\]
where \(\Pi(c)\) is the six-role record of
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
\(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) is the schema-relative certificate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, \(\mathsf{ImplProj}_{S}\) consists
only of the named finite-input projection contracts for the submitted script
rows, \(\mathsf{SrcBound}_{S}\) consists only of pinned path, commit or snapshot,
label, line-range, bounded-summary, and finite comparison fields for the
BEDC/newmath imports, \(\mathsf{Supp}_{S}\) is local package support unless an
exact selected-bundle upload coordinate or archive-equivalent byte-equality
locator is present, and \(\mathsf{Neg}_{S}\) is the negative-boundary list for all
properly stronger readings.

Moreover this classifier is sharp.  Let \(c\preceq_{\Gamma}c^{+}\) be any
proper strengthening of an accepted compact-presentation claim.  If \(c^{+}\)
adds whole-program or runtime implementation soundness, workflow implementation
soundness, exact source-theorem import, a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, an axiom audit,
source-theory semantic completeness, dynamic artifact validation, live daemon or
case-study rerun, clean-machine reproducibility, external support availability,
upload-time venue compliance, or venue acceptance, then \(c^{+}\) is accepted by
the same finite-record calculus if and only if the submitted surface contains the
corresponding positive extension coordinate and the gate rows assigned to that
coordinate pass.  If the coordinate is absent, the stronger reading is routed to
\(\mathsf{Neg}_{S}\) and rejected by an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord;
the bounded claim represented by \(\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma,S}(P,L)\) remains accepted.
Thus this six-role support theorem is a finite-record interface theorem under
the explicit record-gate-soundness hypothesis, not a theorem-proving,
proof-assistant, implementation-soundness, external-support, or venue-acceptance
result, and its compact-route use is through
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The construction is finite and unique because every component is read from a
fixed finite coordinate already present in the submitted interface, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form} gives unique projection to any
displayed coordinate domain.  The six-role
component \(\Pi(c)\) is constructed from the source, formal-interface,
finite-evidence, advisory-agent, deterministic-gate, and promotion fields by
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface}; role-preserving renamings of local
paths do not change it.  Under the explicit hypothesis
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
constructs exactly the certificate tuple \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) and
the finite bad-subrecord list, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} identifies verifier acceptance with
the same six finite schema predicates.  Hence the first two displayed
coordinates are determined by \((S,L,\Gamma)\) and the record-gate predicate.

The implementation coordinate is determined by the projection-contract theorems,
not by whole-program analysis.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}
states exit-code exactness only for the finite projection parsed by each named
script and its printed finite predicate.  Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}
shows that any finite-input implementation-projection upgrade requires a separate
record \(\mathsf{ImplProj}(c)=(K^{\mathrm{impl}},E^{\mathrm{impl}},
R^{\mathrm{impl}},B^{\mathrm{impl}})\), and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-implementation-upgrade-absence} shows that the
current package does not instantiate such a package-wide upgrade.  Thus
\(\mathsf{ImplProj}_{S}\) is exactly the named script-projection surface and no
larger implementation-soundness claim.

The source coordinate is determined by the bounded source-interface results.
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} gives the manual pinned
path, label, line-range, extraction-date, and bounded-paraphrase interface, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} prove that
exact source statements, a fresh Lean verification run, axiom-purity auditing,
and source-theory semantic completeness are stronger coordinates.  Therefore any
``Lean-backed'' wording in the compact presentation is read through
\(\mathsf{SrcBound}_{S}\): source-interface evidence plus finite comparison rows,
not a fresh proof-assistant rebuild or a semantic completeness theorem.

The support coordinate is determined by the local/external support dichotomy.
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness},
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form} provide only the
row-frozen local package support, inventory, log, and digest coordinates for the
current bytes.  Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} gives
the two positive external-support extensions: an exact upload receipt for the
selected support surface or an archive-equivalent byte-equality locator for the
same bytes.  In their absence, the support reading remains local/path-verified
and cannot be read as public archive, DOI, venue upload, or venue acceptance.

It remains to prove sharpness.  A proper strengthening
\(c\preceq_{\Gamma}c^{+}\) changes at least one finite coordinate in the
preorder of Definition~\ref{def:finite-record-projection-preorder}: an axis,
evidence level, implementation field, formal-source field, artifact or rerun
field, support/upload field, venue field, or boundary field.  If the matching
positive extension coordinate is present and its assigned gate rows pass, the
positive direction of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} accepts the
enlarged finite tuple at its declared evidence level; for implementation
projection upgrades this is exactly the sufficiency direction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}.  Conversely, if
the coordinate is absent, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}
gives two submitted states agreeing on every coordinate read by
\(\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma,S}(P,L)\) and differing on the first stronger fact.  No
finite verifier reading only the old projection can determine that stronger
fact.  Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-record-preorder-normal-form} identifies the first
absent coordinate in the printed finite order, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} then identifies
the stronger tag together with that first absent evidence, pass, boundary,
command-run, promotion, source, support, or implementation field as an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} rules out manufacturing the
missing coordinate by conjoining bounded rows from other channels.  This proves
both maximality of the compressed classifier and the negative-boundary routing
for every stronger reading listed in the statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record route dichotomy and upgrade-budget lower bound]
\label{thm:presentation-route-dichotomy}
Let \(P_{0}\) be the current CICM presentation-only package with submitted
surface \(S_{0}\), acceptance ledger \(L_{0}\), and dispatch table
\(\Gamma_{0}\).  In the finite-record preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:finite-record-projection-preorder}, the reviewer-facing route
has exactly the following dichotomy.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the submitted package is read with only the currently available RGS,
source, artifact, and case-study coordinates, then its maximal positive content is
the finite-record interface
\(\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma_{0},S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0})\) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:compressed-master-boundary-classifier}.  The portability part of
this content is the schema/interface coordinate supplied by
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:portable-workflow-schema-factorisation},
Proposition~\ref{prop:portable-method-normal-form-local-pullback}, and the four
path-complete historical case rows of
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}; it is not an independent
deployment, clean-machine rerun, or empirical software-validation coordinate.
The RGS part is conditional on
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\), and the source and artifact
parts are respectively the bounded source-interface and finite manifest/status
interfaces.  Hence the compact article may assert only a conditional
finite-record workflow/interface theorem illustrated by the four local cases.
\item Any reading that upgrades this route to end-to-end workflow correctness,
unconditional current-package workflow or venue publication safety, validated gate implementation
soundness, general software-methodology portability, fresh Lean/BEDC or
formal-source verification, dynamic artifact semantics, live rerun evidence,
clean-machine reproducibility, external support availability, or venue acceptance
must add the matching positive upgrade coordinate and its assigned passing rows.
Moreover the four upgrade families
\[
\mathsf{RGS},\qquad \mathsf{PortRun},\qquad
\mathsf{FormalSrc},\qquad \mathsf{ArtSem}
\]
are pairwise independent finite coordinates: an accepted RGS row for
\((P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\), an independent deployment or clean-machine
case rerun row, a formal-source row with source commit, command, environment,
exit code, and log path, and an artifact-semantic validation row with evaluator
contract, artifact bytes or digest binding, semantic predicate, command,
environment, exit status, and log path.  A single extension claiming all four
stronger readings therefore has upgrade budget at least four distinct nonempty
coordinate families.  If any one family is absent, the corresponding stronger
tag together with its first missing field is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord;
if a family is present and its assigned rows pass, the stronger reading is
accepted only on that family and only at the evidence level recorded by the
enlarged finite tuple.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently no headline sentence of the CICM route can be read as end-to-end
workflow correctness, broad implementation validation, fresh formal verification,
or dynamic artifact validity unless the corresponding upgrade rows are actually
part of the submitted finite record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first alternative is the positive finite-record alternative already isolated
by the compressed classifier.  Theorem~\ref{thm:compressed-master-boundary-classifier}
constructs the maximal record
\(\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma_{0},S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0})\) from exactly the submitted finite
coordinates: the six-role record, the conditional certificate tuple, the
finite-input script projections, the bounded source-interface fields, the local
support fields, and the negative-boundary list.  For portability, the portable
six-role theorem and the two factorisation/pullback propositions identify a role
schema and a local-support normal form; Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} supply four
path-complete historical rows at their declared evidence level.  None of these
fields names a second implementation, a clean-machine environment, a rerun
command, an exit code for such a rerun, or a log path for an independent
deployment.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-only-bounded-support-normal-form},
the case-study coordinate is therefore a finite schema/interface illustration,
not a software-validation experiment.  The RGS coordinate is similarly bounded:
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-package-no-implicit-rgs-discharge} state that the
current rows instantiate the RGS-dependent conclusions only conditionally unless
an accepted RGS row for the same package, surface, ledger, and dispatch table is
submitted.  The source and artifact coordinates are bounded by
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction},
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  Thus, with the current
coordinates fixed, the maximal positive route is exactly the conditional
finite-record interface stated in item~1.

For the upgrade alternative, consider a proper strengthening of any accepted
headline claim.  The finite-record preorder forces a first coordinate at which
the stronger tuple differs from
\(\mathsf{M}_{\Gamma_{0},S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0})\).  If the strengthening removes the
RGS hypothesis, Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary}
identifies the first missing coordinate as the accepted RGS row for
\((P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\).  If it asserts general methodology portability,
live rerun evidence, clean-machine reproducibility, or independent deployment,
the first missing coordinate is a case/deployment command row: environment,
source or artifact state, command, exit status, and log path are not present in
the historical case matrix.  If it asserts fresh formal verification, exact
formal-source import, axiom purity, or source-theory semantic completeness,
Theorems~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction} identify a formal-source upgrade
coordinate containing the source commit, command, environment, exit code, log
path, and assigned pass row.  If it asserts dynamic artifact semantics,
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} identifies the
artifact-semantic validation coordinate containing the evaluator contract,
artifact bytes or digest binding, semantic predicate, command, environment, exit
status, log path, and pass row.  The remaining external-support and venue
readings are handled by the same first-missing-coordinate classification through
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}.

The four displayed families are pairwise independent because they occupy
different coordinates of the submitted tuple and are read by different gate
predicates: the RGS row ranges over accepted ledger rows and their gate/evidence
membership; the portability-rerun row ranges over an independent deployment or
clean-machine execution surface; the formal-source row ranges over proof-source
or Lean/BEDC build commands and logs; and the artifact-semantic row ranges over
an evaluator contract applied to artifact bytes and a semantic predicate.  Holding
three of these families fixed while varying the fourth gives two finite package
states that agree on every other coordinate and differ on the corresponding
stronger fact.  The finite-coordinate determination theorem therefore prevents
any one family, or any conjunction of the other three bounded families, from
determining the missing fourth.  This is exactly the no-gluing conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, specialized to the four
upgrade axes above.

It follows that a claim asserting all four stronger readings must add at least
one nonempty coordinate family in each of the four displayed positions, giving
the stated budget lower bound.  When the matching coordinate and its assigned
passing rows are present, the positive finite-extension direction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} accepts the enlarged tuple at the
declared evidence level; for implementation-projection readings this is the
sufficiency direction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}.  When the family
is absent, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} supplies the
stronger tag and first absent field as an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord.
Thus every headline reading lies on exactly one side of the dichotomy: bounded
conditional finite-record interface, or explicit finite extension with the
necessary upgrade budget.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-node dependency spine exactness]
\label{thm:five-node-dependency-spine-exactness}
For the CICM presentation-only route, the reviewer-facing theorem chain is the
following five-node spine:
\[
\boxed{\text{six-role interface}}
\Longrightarrow
\boxed{\text{record-gate hypothesis}}
\Longrightarrow
\boxed{\text{finite-record exactness}}
\Longrightarrow
\boxed{\text{no-free-upgrade maximality}}
\Longrightarrow
\boxed{\text{case-row lessons}}.
\]
More explicitly, every public claim in the compact article factors through this
ordered spine as follows: the method claim is
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}; the record-gate node is
the explicit predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\) used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}; the finite-record exactness node
is Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}; the no-free-upgrade node is
Corollary~\ref{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression} together
with Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}; and the case-row node
is Proposition~\ref{prop:presentation-case-matrix-sufficiency} together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}.  The finite-script label
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}, despite its
legacy label name, enters this spine only as projection-contract support for the
finite-record exactness node.  It is not a verified implementation-correctness
node and cannot be used as a shortcut around the record-gate hypothesis or the
no-free-upgrade node.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Start with an accepted compact-article claim.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}, the claim has a finite
six-role record and no load-bearing assertion is admitted outside that record.
The publication-safety theorem does not derive the gate rows from program
semantics; it assumes the external record-gate predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), so the record-gate node is a necessary second
node of the chain.  Once that predicate and the submitted fields are fixed,
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} is exactly the finite-record
acceptance theorem: the verifier accepts precisely the printed finite schema
clauses.  Hence the first three nodes are forced for every positive public
claim.

Now consider any stronger reading of that public claim.  The weak-interface
compression corollary classifies the stronger reading by the first missing
upgrade coordinate, and the no-gluing corollary proves that finite conjunctions
of accepted bounded projections cannot create that coordinate.  Therefore the
fourth node is necessary for every negative boundary in the compact article.  If
the public sentence is one of the four methodological examples, the case matrix
proposition supplies exactly the gate, observed issue, accepted coordinate, and
safe lesson, while the finite-row closure theorem keeps the row at the
historical/path-verified evidence level.  Thus the fifth node is the only
additional node needed for case evidence.

Finally, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} proves
only that each named script's zero-exit row is exact for the finite predicate on
the parsed projection printed by that script.  Its own statement excludes
whole-program implementation soundness, runtime semantics, proof truth, artifact
semantics, upload, archive, and venue acceptance.  Consequently it can discharge
only finite-record exactness subchecks inside the third node.  Promoting it to a
separate implementation-correctness node would change a finite coordinate and is
rejected by the fourth node unless a new positive implementation-coordinate
record is supplied.  This proves both the displayed dependency spine and its
exact support-boundary reading.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Master-spine support-coordinate compression]
\label{thm:master-spine-support-coordinate-compression}
In the CICM presentation-only route, every load-bearing use of the support labels
\[
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality},
\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support},
\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton},
\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion},
\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality},
\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
\ref{thm:case-witness-skeleton-rigidity},
\ref{prop:presentation-case-matrix-sufficiency},
\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}
\]
factors uniquely through one of the six clauses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}.  The first two labels
support the finite certificate and bad-subrecord clauses; the next three labels
support only finite-script or finite-input implementation-projection contracts;
the next label supports only the bounded imported-source interface; the next two
labels support only the exact-inclusion or archive-equivalent support-availability
condition; and the last three labels support only historical/path-complete case
illustrations.  Consequently the compact article may cite
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface} as the single method theorem
and cite the displayed labels only as support.  No
citation to the displayed labels upgrades the package to whole-program
implementation soundness, proof truth, fresh formal rebuilding, artifact-semantic
validation, live case-study rerun, benchmark evidence, empirical current-system
validation, archive/upload status, or venue acceptance unless the submitted
surface also contains the corresponding positive upgrade coordinate and its
assigned passing gate rows.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface} has six positive
clauses: six-role factorization, finite certificate construction with rejected
bad subrecords, finite-script projection-contract exactness, bounded imported
source-interface evidence, conditional support availability, and historical
case-row illustration.  The support labels listed in the statement have pairwise
fixed targets among these clauses.  The publication-safety theorem constructs
\(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) from the submitted six-role fields, and the
weak-interface maximality theorem classifies absent upgrade coordinates; hence
both feed the certificate and bad-subrecord clause.  The finite-script theorem
states exactness only for each named script's parsed finite projection and
printed predicate; the six-coordinate skeleton and the implementation-extension
criterion name the additional finite-input coordinates needed before even that
bounded implementation-projection reading is accepted for a gate.  Hence those
three labels feed only the implementation-projection clause.  The bounded-source
maximality theorem feeds only the imported-source clause, since its positive
fields are path, commit, labels, line ranges, bounded summaries, and finite
record-comparison checks.  The upload-or-archive corollary and current-absence
proposition feed only the support-availability clause, since their positive
fields are exact supplemental inclusion or archive-equivalent byte equality and
their negative content is absence of upload, DOI, or public-byte-equality status.
The case skeleton, case matrix, and finite-row closure results classify the four
case rows by gate, observed issue, accepted coordinate, and safe lesson at the
path-verified historical-snapshot level.  Hence those three labels feed only the
case-row clause.

The factorization is unique because these targets alter disjoint finite
coordinates of the record calculus.  A certificate or bad-subrecord claim reads
the claim-kind, evidence, pass-row, discovery, and boundary fields of
\(\mathcal C(c)\).  A finite-script implementation-projection claim additionally
reads the implementation source identity, invocation/environment, parsed input
projection, byte binding, declared finite predicate, and proof-obligation link.
A source-interface claim reads path, commit, label, line range, summary, and
evidence-level fields.  A support-availability claim reads exact-inclusion or
archive-equivalence fields.  A case-row claim reads the four-coordinate
historical matrix and its path-verified boundary.  A citation that tries to move from one target to a
stronger target therefore changes a finite coordinate: implementation source or
runtime for whole-program soundness, proof/source coordinates for fresh formal
rebuilding or proof truth, artifact-semantic coordinates for dynamic validation,
rerun command tuples for live case behaviour, support coordinates for archive or
upload status, or external decision coordinates for venue acceptance.  By
Theorems~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality},
\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, and
\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}, such a changed coordinate is accepted
exactly when the positive upgrade record and assigned passing gate rows are
submitted.  If it is not submitted, Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} return the first
absent coordinate as an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  Thus the displayed
support labels compress to the master theorem for the compact article and cannot
be read as independent stronger empirical, semantic, implementation, archive, or
venue claims.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-record interface and support-boundary classification]
\label{thm:finite-record-interface-support-boundary-classification}
In the CICM presentation-only package, the three families of labels isolated in
the local support-scope audit have the following exact normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The interface labels
\[
\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface},\quad
\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},\quad
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
\]
are primary only as finite-record software-method interfaces over submitted
records, verifier predicates, finite certificates, and bad-subrecord reports.
They are not independent deep mathematical claims about the BEDC object theory,
and no stronger novelty reading is accepted unless it adds a new finite coordinate
outside the displayed interface.
\item The verifier and script labels
\[
\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract},\quad
\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness},\quad
\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}
\]
are exactly finite-script projection-contract results.  Their positive content is
that the retained verifier or script accepts precisely the finite projection that
it parses and the predicate that its specification prints.  They do not assert
workflow implementation soundness, truthful production of all gate rows, clean
machine reproducibility, or semantic correctness of the underlying gates.
\item The source-interface labels
\[
\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},\quad
\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation},\quad
\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}
\]
are bounded-source results for a pinned path, commit, line-range table, bounded
summary, and declared evidence level.  They do not import exact BEDC theorem
statements, prove the imported source statements, rerun Lean, or audit axioms for
the current package.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover this classification is sharp: a reading that upgrades any of the three
families respectively to a new theory theorem, implementation-soundness theorem,
or fresh formal-source theorem is accepted by the manuscript's finite-record
calculus if and only if the corresponding upgrade coordinate named in
Corollary~\ref{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression},
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} is added to the
submitted support surface and accepted by the assigned gates.  If that coordinate
is absent, the stronger-reading tag together with its first absent upgrade
coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord, while the bounded interface
claim remains accepted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For item~1, Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface} defines the
presentation claim as the finite tuple
\(\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}(S,L,\Gamma)\),
