Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface} factors an accepted claim through
six finite roles, and Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} constructs
accepted certificates and bad-subrecord reports only under its explicit
record-gate-soundness hypotheses.  All three proofs inspect the same kind of
submitted finite fields: records, tables, manifests, logs when declared,
evidence-level tags, pass rows, and boundary fields.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a conclusion whose
truth can change while those fields are held fixed is not determined by the
interface.  Thus semantic BEDC novelty, a new object-theory theorem, venue
acceptance, or end-to-end workflow correctness is not a conclusion of this family
unless it is added as a separate finite coordinate.

For item~2, Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract} lists the six input
predicates read by the verifier and states that the positive output is the finite
acceptance bit for those predicates.  Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}
proves exactness only between that verifier and the six-clause record-acceptance
semantics.  Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}
restricts the concrete retained scripts to the finite input projection parsed by
each script and to the predicate printed for that script.  Hence the common
mathematical content is projection-contract exactness.  A stronger claim that a
workflow implementation truthfully generated every row, that every gate program is
sound, or that the scripts are reproducible in a fresh environment queries the
implementation tuple isolated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}; without that tuple
it is outside the parsed projection.

For item~3, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} states the
manual pinned-path, pinned-commit, line-range, extraction-date, and bounded
summary interface.  Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation}
shows that the current package has no accepted formal-source row with build and
axiom-purity pass records, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction} rejects any promotion to a
formal-source or fresh-execution claim without those rows and the command-run
fields.  This is exactly the source-coordinate obstruction proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}: exact source
text, public-byte equality, Lean/BEDC rebuild success, axiom purity, and semantic
source-theory validation are nonempty finite extensions of the bounded source
interface, not consequences of it.

The sharpness clause is now common to the three cases.  When the relevant upgrade
coordinate and its assigned pass rows are present, the positive finite-extension
criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} and the
specialized implementation and source-interface extension theorems accept the
enlarged record at the stronger level.  When the coordinate is absent,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} supplies the
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting of the stronger tag and the first
missing coordinate.  Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} rules out
recovering the same coordinate by conjoining the bounded families.  Therefore the
three weak-looking families are not promoted novelty claims; they are sharp
finite-record interfaces with explicit upgrade budgets.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Presentation-only bounded-support normal form]
\label{thm:presentation-only-bounded-support-normal-form}
For the CICM presentation-only package, every load-bearing use in the compact
article of finite-record publication safety, imported BEDC/newmath source evidence,
Rule~110/GroundCompiler or other artifact evidence, and the four case-study rows
factors through the following finite product of bounded interfaces:
\[
\mathcal N_{\rm pres}=\mathcal N_{\rm safe}\times\mathcal N_{\rm src}\times
\mathcal N_{\rm art}\times\mathcal N_{\rm case}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal N_{\rm safe}\) is the conditional finite-record certificate
interface of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} under the explicit
record-gate-soundness predicate \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\);
\(\mathcal N_{\rm src}\) is the pinned source-interface record consisting only of
the newmath path, commit \path{3fb3d6a0641767388a401883062aa522ea0b397b}, label,
line range, extraction date, bounded summary, and evidence-level fields of
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation};
\(\mathcal N_{\rm art}\) is the manifest/snapshot/status/limitation record of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}; and
\(\mathcal N_{\rm case}\) is the portable audit schema illustrated by the four
path-complete local historical witnesses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}.

Consequently the compact presentation article may cite the theorem chain only as
a conditional finite-record audit/interface result.  It may assert a portable
audit schema illustrated by four local historical cases, and it may assert finite
manifest, snapshot, source-path, line-range, and evidence-level support.  It may
not, without adding the corresponding fresh upgrade coordinate and pass rows,
assert end-to-end workflow correctness, soundness of gate implementations, a
fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, an axiom-purity audit, exact import of the full BEDC
source theorem statements, dynamic Rule~110/GroundCompiler semantic validation,
broad empirical benchmarking of AI-assisted mathematics, external upload/archive
availability, clean-machine reproducibility, upload-time venue compliance, or
venue acceptance.  For each such stronger reading the first missing coordinate is
the unique axis named by
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}, and the stronger tag
together with that absent coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The product coordinates are already finite-record interfaces in the manuscript
chain.  The safety coordinate is exactly the output of
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}: its input is the submitted record
surface, ledger, dispatch table, schema files, and the external predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), and its output is a finite accepted-certificate
set together with finite bad subrecords.  The proof of that theorem explicitly
does not read gate source code, daemon traces, formal-source rebuilds, artifact
semantics, venue upload records, or venue outcomes.  Therefore any compact-paper
safety sentence using that coordinate is a conditional finite-record audit
sentence and no stronger safety property is a function of the supplied fields.

The source coordinate is finite for the same reason.
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} fixes one repository
path, the pinned commit, the extraction date, the imported labels and line
ranges, and bounded paraphrases;
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} separates these
fields from executable or formal-source evidence.  Hence holding the
path/commit/line/summary/evidence-level tuple fixed while varying an unsubmitted
Lean build, axiom audit, or exact BEDC theorem statement leaves the accepted
source-interface record unchanged.  Those stronger readings therefore require
the formal-source upgrade coordinate identified in
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}.

The artifact coordinate is the finite witness surface of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface}.  Its fields are
manifest, snapshot, status/evaluator-record, and limitation-ledger fields;
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} proves that dynamic
artifact semantics is accepted only after an artifact-validation coordinate names
the evaluator contract, artifact bytes, semantic predicate, command, source
state, environment, exit status, log path, and digest binding.  Thus
Rule~110/GroundCompiler semantic validation is not determined by the submitted
finite witness row.

Finally, the case-study coordinate is finite and local.
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} give historical path-complete
witness rows for the four displayed gates.  These rows instantiate the
schema--gate--lesson pattern, but they contain no sampling frame,
population-level measurement, statistical estimator, or fresh cross-project
benchmark log.  Therefore they prove portability of the audit schema as a
checkable record format illustrated by four cases, not a broad empirical
benchmark of AI-assisted mathematics.

The four coordinates are disjoint axes in the stronger-reading preorder:
record-gate safety, source import, artifact validation, and case/empirical
support.  Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} classifies
the first missing upgrade coordinate on each axis and proves inclusion-minimal
bad-subrecord rejection; Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}
rules out obtaining a missing coordinate by conjoining other bounded interfaces.
Thus every compact-paper load-bearing claim factors through
\(\mathcal N_{\rm pres}\), and every listed stronger reading is rejected unless
its own finite upgrade coordinate is supplied.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Support-coordinate routing for the compact article]
\label{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}
In the CICM presentation-only article, Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface}
is the unique headline theorem.  Every load-bearing citation to the support chain
of this supplement must be routed through that master projection and has the
following unique finite-record classification.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The portable six-role result, the record-gate interface and exactness
results, the record-gate conditional compact spine, the publication-safety
interface, and the presentation-only bounded-support normal form may be cited
only as support coordinates for the master conditional finite-record workflow
interface:
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{Theorems~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface},
\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine},
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface},
\ref{thm:presentation-only-bounded-support-normal-form}},\quad
\text{Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}},\quad
\text{Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Their common hypothesis is the finite external predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), and their common conclusion is a certificate,
bad-subrecord, or role-interface statement about the submitted finite record
surface.
\item The finite-script result and its corollary may be cited only as
projection-contract support for four named scripts:
\[
\text{Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-script-rgs-instantiation-boundary}}.
\]
They certify exactness of the printed finite predicate on the parsed input
projection; they do not certify semantic implementation soundness beyond that
projection.
\item The current-package and manual-ledger results may be cited only as
ledger-relative support:
\[
\text{Theorems~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} and
\ref{thm:manual-ledger-dependence-boundary}}.
\]
They are exact for the manually declared rows after the post-inventory rerun and
digest evidence, not for all possible manuscript claims.
\item The theorem-environment extractor and inventory obstruction results may be
cited only as a syntactic scope ledger:
\[
\text{Theorems~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction}}.
\]
They provide labelled-environment coverage and obstruction to treating the
inventory as a proof checker; they do not certify proof correctness, theorem
quality, or object-language verification.
\item The review-bundle availability, case-snapshot, and command-run inventory
labels may be cited only as audit records or audit conditions:
\[
\text{Audit records~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition},
\ref{audit:case-snapshot-non-rerun-boundary}, and
\ref{audit:command-run-boundary-inventory}}.
\]
They provide finite support availability, historical-snapshot, or command-row
boundary coordinates; they are not independent mathematical theorems in the
object language.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the compact article may not present the labelled support chain,
including the portable six-role, publication-safety, compact-spine,
current-package, script-projection, or theorem-inventory label sets, as a second
headline theorem, as object-language verification of the mathematics, or as
end-to-end verified pipeline correctness.  Any such
stronger reading has a first missing upgrade coordinate in the sense of
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} and is rejected by an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The classification is by the coordinate read by each cited result.  For item~1,
Theorem~\ref{thm:portable-six-role-interface} factors accepted claims through the
six finite roles, Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}
states that record-gate soundness is the external finite predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), and
Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness} proves
that this predicate is exactly the one used by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.  The latter theorem then
constructs only certificates and bad subrecords from the submitted surface, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine} says that this conditional
finite-record form is forced for the compact spine.  Finally,
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-only-bounded-support-normal-form} identifies the
safety coordinate of the presentation package with precisely that conditional
interface.  Thus every primary citation in item~1 has the same finite-record
input and no larger semantic output.

For item~2, the statement of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} restricts the
four retained scripts to the finite input projection parsed by each script and to
the predicate printed by that script.  Its proof uses only schema files,
manifest/source-interface rows, primary-claim inventory rows, theorem-environment
extraction, and command-run boundary fields.  Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-script-rgs-instantiation-boundary}
then transfers exactly those rows into the record-gate interface.  Therefore a
semantic implementation-soundness reading would require an additional positive
implementation-audit coordinate rather than following from these two labels.

For item~3, Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness} is explicitly
relative to the finite package ledger printed in the current support tables, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:manual-ledger-dependence-boundary} isolates the fact that this
ledger is manual and row-bound.  The later post-inventory closure results supply
the rerun and digest coordinates needed for the current bytes.  Hence the
current-package labels are exact for that ledger state only.

For item~4, Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}
describes a deterministic extractor for theorem-like labelled environments, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction} proves that such an
inventory is not a proof checker.  The only common coordinate is therefore
syntactic environment coverage.  Proof correctness, theorem quality, Lean/BEDC
semantic import, and object-language verification are outside the fields read by
the inventory coordinate.

For item~5, the cited labels are audit-record environments.  Their statements
record availability of local review-bundle support, historical case-snapshot
limitations, and command-run boundary rows.  Each is a finite coordinate used by
the certificate schema; none has an object-language theorem statement whose truth
would imply mathematical correctness of the underlying BEDC or artifact claims.

The five classes are disjoint because they read disjoint coordinates of the
finite product \(\mathcal N_{\rm pres}\): workflow safety, script projection,
manual ledger, syntactic inventory, and audit support.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a conclusion whose
truth depends on a coordinate not read by one class cannot be determined by the
records of that class.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, conjoining several
bounded classes still does not create an absent upgrade coordinate.  The finite
obstruction skeleton of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}
then supplies an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord for any stronger tag that treats
the support chain as object-language verification or end-to-end pipeline
correctness.  This proves both the allowed citation normal form and the rejected
stronger reading.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Presentation-route spine projection and overload obstruction]
\label{thm:presentation-route-spine-projection-overload-obstruction}
Let \(\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\) be the finite set of labelled theorem, proposition,
lemma, corollary, and audit-record statements in this supplement, read from the
current source bytes.  Let \(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\subset\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\)
be the compressed spine named in the reader map: the six-role architecture and
certificate tuple, record-gate soundness and the six acceptance predicates,
verifier exactness and finite-coordinate rigidity, the conditional
publication-safety theorem and no-free-upgrade boundary, the finite-record
maximality/classification result, and the present projection theorem.  For a
CICM presentation-only compact article, every load-bearing citation to an element
of \(\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\) has a unique accepted projection of exactly one of the
following two forms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the cited label lies in \(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\), its accepted
projection is the conditional finite-record spine under
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), with conclusions only about submitted finite
records, certificates, bad subrecords, role interfaces, and finite upgrade
coordinates.
\item If the cited label lies in
\(\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\setminus\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\), its accepted projection is
support-only: one of the five classes of
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}---script
projection support, ledger-relative support, syntactic theorem-inventory support,
audit-record support, or a local/path-verified support-boundary instantiation of
the same finite schema.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the exhaustive theorem ledger of this supplement cannot be promoted
inside the compact article to a second primary theorem surface.  Such a promotion
is accepted only after adding a positive finite coordinate that explicitly states
the stronger object-language, implementation-soundness, semantic-completeness,
external-support, or end-to-end automation claim and supplies the matching proof,
command, upload/archive, or implementation-audit row.  If that coordinate is
absent, the promoted-primary tag together with the first missing upgrade
coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord; deleting the tag returns the
claim to its accepted support-only projection.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The set \(\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\) is finite because it is obtained by the
deterministic labelled-environment extractor of
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} from a
finite TeX source.  The reader map explicitly names the labels that form
\(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\).  For those labels,
Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine} proves the normal form
\[
\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\Longrightarrow
\bigl(\mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L),\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma,S}(L),
\Pi_{\mathrm{pres}}(S,L,\Gamma)\bigr),
\]
and Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}
identifies this hypothesis with the standalone record-gate interface.  Hence a
spine citation has the conditional finite-record projection in item~1 and no
larger semantic output.

Now take a labelled statement outside \(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}
classifies every compact-article citation to the supplement support chain by the
finite coordinate it reads: script projection, manual ledger, syntactic
theorem-environment inventory, audit record, or support-boundary instantiation.
The support-boundary convention in the reader map states that package-shape,
digest, archive/upload, command, venue, theorem-inventory, local fixed-point,
source-interface, and case-study rows are retained for auditability rather than
as co-primary mathematical contributions.  Thus every non-spine label factors
through exactly one support coordinate of the finite product normal form.  The
factor is unique because the five classes in
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification} are proved
there to read disjoint coordinates of \(\mathcal N_{\rm pres}\).

It remains to prove obstruction to overload.  A compact-paper sentence that
treats a non-spine support label as a primary object-language theorem, an
implementation-soundness theorem, a semantic-completeness theorem, an external
support theorem, or an end-to-end automation theorem asserts an additional
coordinate not read by that support projection.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, no finite verifier can
determine a conclusion depending on an unread coordinate from the old projection.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-weak-interface-maximality} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, conjoining finitely many
bounded support rows still does not create the missing upgrade coordinate.  The
finite obstruction skeleton of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} then gives an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting of the stronger promoted-primary tag
and the first absent coordinate.  Removing that tag leaves exactly the support
projection already classified, while adding the coordinate is precisely the
positive extension case allowed by the no-free-upgrade boundary.  This proves the
two-form projection and the claimed overload obstruction.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Four-case foreground support-boundary normal form]
\label{thm:four-case-foreground-support-boundary}
Let \(A\) be a compact CICM presentation article whose theorem citations to this
supplement are restricted by
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-spine-projection-overload-obstruction}.  Assume
the article foregrounds exactly the six-role finite-record interface under
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\) and uses the four case rows of
Section~\ref{sec:gate-summary} only as examples.  Then every load-bearing
mathematical or software-safety assertion in \(A\) has a unique normal form
\[
\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)
\Longrightarrow
\bigl(\mathsf{SixRole}(P,L,\Gamma),\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma,S}(L),
\mathsf{Case}_{1},\ldots,\mathsf{Case}_{4}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathsf{SixRole}\) is the source/formal-interface/evidence-row/agent/gate/
human-promotion factorization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface},
\(\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma,S}(L)\) is the finite certificate family constructed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, and each \(\mathsf{Case}_{j}\) is
only the gate, observed issue, accepted finite coordinate, and safe lesson recorded
in the corresponding row of Section~\ref{sec:gate-summary}.  No theorem-like
environment outside the compressed spine may be used in \(A\) as a second primary
theorem surface.

Moreover, this normal form is maximal for the stated presentation route.  If a
sentence of \(A\) assigns any support-only theorem, local digest row, ledger fact,
source-state fact, or case row a stronger role---object-language theorem,
gate-implementation soundness, proof-assistant correctness, artifact semantics,
external archive availability, dynamic rerun, venue acceptance, or end-to-end
workflow correctness---then the sentence has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord
consisting of that stronger role tag together with its first missing upgrade
coordinate.  Removing the stronger role tag restores the unique normal form;
adding the missing coordinate is exactly a new finite-record theorem outside this
presentation article's present scope.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cited theorem-projection hypothesis gives a finite partition of the
supplement labels into the compressed spine \(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\) and the
support-only complement
\(\mathcal T_{\rm sup}\setminus\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\).  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:presentation-route-spine-projection-overload-obstruction}, a
citation to \(\mathcal S_{\rm pres}\) has only the conditional finite-record
projection under \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\), while a citation to the
complement has only one of the support projections classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}.  Hence every
foreground assertion of the compact article factors through the same conditional
spine as Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine}.

The first coordinate of the displayed normal form is fixed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}: it is precisely the six
role factorization into source object, formal interface, finite evidence row,
advisory agent action, deterministic gate, and human promotion boundary.  The
second coordinate is fixed by Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, which
constructs only the finite publication certificates accepted by the verifier from
the submitted ledger and support surface.  The four remaining coordinates are
fixed by the four rows of Section~\ref{sec:gate-summary}; each row records a gate,
an observed issue, an accepted finite coordinate, and the safe lesson, and the
reader map explicitly excludes dynamic rerun, artifact-semantic validation, venue
acceptance, and implementation-soundness readings from those rows.  Since these
coordinates are disjoint in the finite product normal form of
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}, the
factorization is unique.

For maximality, suppose a compact-article sentence gives a support-only label or
case row one of the stronger roles listed in the statement.  That role depends on
an upgrade coordinate not read by the support projection: respectively an
object-language proof, implementation-audit tuple, proof-assistant command row,
semantic evaluator record, upload or archive-equivalent locator, fresh rerun row,
venue record, or end-to-end workflow-correctness budget.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, the old finite record
cannot determine a conclusion depending on an unread coordinate.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, conjoining finitely many
bounded support rows cannot create the absent coordinate.  The obstruction
skeleton theorem, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, then
returns an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting of the stronger role tag and
the first missing coordinate.  Deleting the tag leaves the already classified
support projection, while adding the coordinate is a new positive finite-record
claim and therefore a separate theoremization obligation rather than a consequence
of the present compact route.  This proves both maximality and the stated
support-boundary classification.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Supplemental schema-relative dependency-map irredundancy]
\label{thm:compact-dependency-map-irredundancy}
For the technical supplement to the CICM presentation-only route, the
reviewer-facing theorem chain has the
following five-node dependency map and no larger automatic reading:
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{six-role interface}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{record-gate soundness hypothesis}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{finite-record exactness}\\
\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{no-free-upgrade maximality}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{four methodological case rows.}
\end{gathered}
\]
More precisely, every load-bearing presentation claim accepted from the support
surface factors uniquely through
\begin{enumerate}
\item the six source/formal-interface/evidence-row/agent/gate/human-promotion
roles of Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface};
\item the explicit finite predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\) of
Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}, rather than an
implementation-soundness assertion about the concrete gate programs;
\item the schema-relative finite-record exactness supplied by
Theorems~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} and
\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness};
\item the no-free-upgrade obstruction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}; and
\item exactly the four historical/path-verified case-row lessons of
Section~\ref{sec:gate-summary}, read only as methodological evidence through
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}.
\end{enumerate}
Relative to the finite-coordinate taxonomy printed in this supplement, the five
nodes are irredundant at the finite-record level: deleting any one of
them either leaves the compact article with no accepted primary workflow claim,
or changes a remaining assertion into a proper stronger reading with a first
missing upgrade coordinate and hence an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.  In
particular, neither the finite-script projection-contract theorem, nor the
bounded source-interface rows, nor the historical case rows can be promoted by
conjunction into end-to-end correctness of automath/newmath, semantic soundness
of all gate implementations, clean-machine formal rebuild, fresh artifact rerun,
or venue acceptance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The existence of the displayed factorization is the compressed form of
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-case-foreground-support-boundary}.  Its first coordinate is
exactly the six-role factorization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface}.  Its second coordinate is
not a conclusion but a hypothesis: Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness}
identify \(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\) as the finite external predicate read by
the publication-safety interface.  The third coordinate follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, which constructs finite
certificates and bad-subrecord reports from the submitted surface, together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, which identifies verifier
acceptance with schema-relative record acceptance.  The fourth coordinate is
Theorem~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade}, strengthened for
finite conjunctions by Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}: a
stronger reading is accepted only after its own positive finite coordinate is
added and passed.  The fifth coordinate is supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}, which classifies the four
case rows as promotion, route/submission blocking, theorem-content non-growth,
and artifact-limitation-disclosure skeletons and restricts each one to its
bounded safe lesson.  The uniqueness of this five-node factorization is the
coordinate-disjointness proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification} and used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-case-foreground-support-boundary}.

It remains to prove irredundancy and the no-larger-reading clause.  If the
six-role node is deleted, an accepted claim no longer has a typed source object,
formal interface, finite evidence row, advisory action, deterministic gate, and
human boundary; by Theorem~\ref{thm:six-role-publication-master-interface} this is
precisely the role record needed for the primary workflow claim.  If the
record-gate-soundness node is deleted, Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
has lost one of its hypotheses, so the remaining rows cannot be read as accepted
publication certificates.  If finite-record exactness is deleted, the verifier
output is no longer identified with schema-relative record acceptance, so the
compact article has no proved finite certificate semantics.  If no-free-upgrade
is deleted, the article no longer has an obstruction preventing support rows from
being overread as implementation, source-semantic, artifact-semantic, external,
or venue coordinates.  If the four case rows are deleted, the method remains a
formal interface but loses the presentation-route methodological witnesses; if a
case row is kept but read as a fresh rerun or semantic validation, the added role
depends on command-run or artifact-semantic coordinates that the row does not
contain.  In each deletion or promotion, the stronger role tag together with the
first absent coordinate is exactly the obstruction returned by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}.

Finally consider the named tempting upgrades.  The finite-script theorem is used
only through the projection-contract reading classified in item~2 of
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-article-finite-record-spine-classification}; therefore
an all-runtime or all-daemon implementation-soundness reading adds an unread
implementation-audit coordinate.  The bounded source-interface rows are limited
by Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-source-interface-non-escalation}; therefore a clean
formal rebuild, axiom audit, or complete source-theory import adds an unread
formal-source coordinate.  The case rows are limited by
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}; therefore a fresh artifact
rerun or semantic artifact validation adds an unread command-run or
artifact-semantic coordinate.  Venue acceptance requires the separate coordinate
isolated by Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}.  Since finite
conjunctions of bounded rows do not create any of these missing coordinates, none
of the listed end-to-end readings follows from the compact dependency map.  This
proves both irredundancy and maximality of the five-node presentation spine.
\end{proof}




\begin{corollary}[Compact five-node presentation consequence]
\label{cor:compact-five-node-presentation-consequence}
The compact paper may cite the dependency-map analysis only in the following
compressed form: its load-bearing theorem surface consists of the six-role
interface, the explicit record-gate-soundness hypothesis, schema-relative
finite-record exactness, no-free-upgrade boundary, and the four methodological
case rows.  The citation does not license an end-to-end implementation,
formal-rebuild, artifact-semantic, external-support, or venue-status conclusion;
each such conclusion requires its own upgrade coordinate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-dependency-map-irredundancy} proves the five-node
factorization and irredundancy relative to the supplement's finite-coordinate
taxonomy.  Projecting away the handwritten taxonomy leaves exactly the five
named nodes and the no-larger-reading clause.  The no-larger-reading clause is
also the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}: bounded finite-record
rows cannot be conjoined into missing implementation, formal-source,
artifact-semantic, external-support, or venue coordinates.  Therefore the compact
paper receives the five-node support consequence stated here and nothing stronger.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Issue-coordinate discharge for the local support surface]
\label{thm:submitted-support-issue-coordinate-discharge}
For this presentation-package source state, the five support-boundary issue
coordinates have the following sharp finite-record normal form.  The coordinate
\path{missing:post-inventory-rerun-after-current-bytes} is discharged
positively exactly by the ordered post-inventory tuple consisting of the accepted
bytes of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}, the
theorem-environment extractor log, the certificate-record verifier log, the
source-interface verifier log, the primary-claim verifier log, and the final
SHA--256 digest manifest generated after those logs exist.  The labels
\path{missing:external-upload-or-archive-coordinate},
\path{missing:fresh-newmath-lean-rebuild-and-axiom-audit},
\path{missing:fresh-artifact-semantic-validation-rerun}, and
\path{missing:venue-live-check-at-actual-submission-date} are discharged at their
proper evidence levels: the current presentation package asserts no positive
coordinate for the first three absent-support readings, and reads venue facts
only through the dated 2026-06-13 local-readiness record until an upload-time
live check or unchanged-rule bridge is added.  Thus every accepted
current-package theorem factors through the local/path-verified finite-record
tuple, and no accepted theorem depends on an absent upload or archive locator,
fresh formal-source command row, dynamic artifact-validation rerun, or
upload-time venue-compliance record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The positive post-inventory coordinate is precisely the first coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}, instantiated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}.  Those
results require the accepted inventory bytes to exist before the extractor and
retained finite-record verifiers are run, and require the final digest surface to
be generated only after the resulting logs exist.  In the present source state the
four verifier logs named above record Python 3.10.11 on Windows 10 and exit code
\path{0}, while \path{review_bundle/final_digest_generation_run.log} records the
subsequent digest-generation command, environment, exit code, and output
manifest.  Therefore the first support-boundary coordinate is discharged by an ordered
byte-refresh coordinate.  By the extractor-boundary theorems cited in
Corollary~\ref{cor:presentation-route-support-coordinate-normal-form}, this is a
syntactic theorem-environment and finite-record replay claim, not a fresh proof of
the semantics of the displayed theorem statements.

The remaining absent-support labels are exactly the stronger readings classified
by Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}.  External submitted
support requires an upload receipt or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator;
fresh newmath/Lean or axiom-purity support requires a formal-source command row;
and dynamic artifact semantics requires an artifact-validation command row.  In
each case the cited theorem applies
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} to show that the
current finite projection cannot supply the absent coordinate by gluing it from
local paths, digest rows, marker rows, manifest rows, or abstract record-gate
hypotheses.  The venue label is the dated-record branch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}: the
2026-06-13 log is a local-readiness coordinate, while actual submission-date
compliance requires an upload-time replacement check or an explicit unchanged-rule
bridge.  Therefore deleting any stronger-reading tag returns to the accepted
bounded finite-record claim, while adding the named coordinate is the unique
positive upgrade route.  This proves the stated discharge of all five support-boundary
coordinates and connects the theorem to the terminal theorem chain rather than
to a separate audit convention.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Exact submitted issue-coordinate skeleton]
\label{prop:exact-submitted-issue-coordinate-skeleton}
Let \(I\) be the accepted theorem-inventory byte pair consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} for the
current source state, let \(R\) be the ordered post-inventory command tuple
consisting of the theorem-environment extraction run, certificate-record
verification run, source-interface verification run, and primary-claim inventory
freshness run, and let \(D\) be the final SHA--256 digest manifest generated
after \(I\) and \(R\).  For the exact finite issue-coordinate set, write
\(e_1\) for
\path{missing:post-inventory-rerun-after-current-bytes}, \(e_2\) for
\path{missing:external-upload-or-archive-coordinate}, \(e_3\) for
\path{missing:fresh-newmath-lean-rebuild-and-axiom-audit}, \(e_4\) for
\path{missing:fresh-artifact-semantic-validation-rerun}, and \(e_5\) for
\path{missing:venue-live-check-at-actual-submission-date}.  The accepted
current-package claim is the unique finite-record projection with the following
skeleton.  The coordinate for \(e_1\) is positive exactly when the ordered tuple
\((I,R,D)\) is present.  The coordinates for \(e_2,e_3,e_4,e_5\) are not silently
supplied by \((I,R,D)\): \(e_2\) requires an upload receipt, DOI-bearing
supplement, completed supplemental upload, or archive-equivalent byte-equality
locator; \(e_3\) requires a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity audit
coordinate; \(e_4\) requires an evaluator contract and fresh artifact-validation
rerun logs; and \(e_5\) requires either a venue/bibliography live check at actual
submission time or an explicit finite bridge tying the upload to the unchanged
2026-06-13 venue-rule state.  Hence any accepted theorem using the local support surface factors through the single positive coordinate \((I,R,D)\), the
dated local-readiness venue record, and the three absent-support boundaries
above.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The coordinate \(e_1\) is exactly the post-inventory fixed-point coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}.  That theorem orders the
inventory bytes before the extractor and finite-record verifier logs and orders
the digest manifest after those logs.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation}
identifies the resulting current support tuple, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-replay-post-inventory-tuple} proves that subsequent
uses of the tuple factor through the same byte strings until a new inventory or
command-result coordinate is added.  Thus the positive branch for \(e_1\) is
precisely \((I,R,D)\), and it supplies only byte-level local replay, not theorem
semantics.

For \(e_2\), Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} lists
the only positive external-support coordinates, while
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that the current local bundle, verifier logs, and digest manifest do not
contain one.  For \(e_3\), Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} separate
bounded source-interface rows from fresh formal-source validity, rebuild
success, and axiom-purity evidence.  For \(e_4\),
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} separate finite witness rows
and historical case snapshots from fresh evaluator semantics.  For \(e_5\),
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} show that the
2026-06-13 venue/bibliography log is a dated local-readiness record only.  It
does not determine a later upload-time form state unless the later support
surface adds an upload-time rerun or unchanged-rule bridge.

It remains only to rule out gluing the absent coordinates from the one positive
post-inventory coordinate.  This is the finite-coordinate determination boundary
of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}: a conclusion whose
field is not present in the finite support tuple is not determined by that tuple.
The terminal classification in Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:end-to-end-upgrade-decomposition-obstruction} applies this
boundary to the external, formal-source, and artifact axes, while the venue
freshness theorem supplies the same minimal-coordinate argument for \(e_5\).
Therefore every stronger reading has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord
consisting of the stronger-reading row and the first missing coordinate among
\(e_2,e_3,e_4\), or the upload-time venue coordinate for \(e_5\), while deleting
that row returns to the accepted local/path-verified finite-record projection
through \((I,R,D)\) and the dated 2026-06-13 venue record.  This proves the

\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[External-coordinate admissibility trichotomy]
\label{prop:external-coordinate-admissibility-trichotomy}
For the present CICM presentation-route submission state, consider the three
stronger support readings: \(u\), that the review bundle is externally uploaded
or archived; \(f\), that the pinned newmath source has a fresh rebuild or axiom
audit; and \(a\), that the Rule~110/artifact rows have fresh semantic validation.
In the finite-record preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}, these readings are accepted by
the theorem chain if and only if the submitted support surface contains the
following corresponding positive coordinates:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for \(u\), either a venue-upload receipt for the exact support bundle or an
archive-equivalent public branch/path locator whose file list, path semantics,
manifest identity, digest rows, and byte-equality fields identify the same bundle
bytes;
\item for \(f\), a formal-source command row recording the pinned commit, source
paths, environment, command, exit code, log path, and the rebuild, marker, or
axiom-purity predicate checked by that command;
\item for \(a\), an artifact-validation command row recording the validator
specification, validator source path and source state, inputs, environment,
command, exit code, log path, and digest binding between the checked artifacts and
the submitted manifest rows.
\end{enumerate}
If the corresponding coordinate is absent, the maximal admissible reading is,
respectively, local/path-verified conditional bundle support, bounded
source-interface and marker-row support without formal-source validity, and
manifest/evaluator-record support without dynamic artifact semantics.  Moreover,
for each absent coordinate the pair consisting of the stronger-reading tag and
that missing coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord: deleting the tag
returns to the accepted finite-record projection, while filling exactly that
coordinate removes this particular obstruction without changing the other two
axes.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The proof is by the finite-coordinate classifier already established for the
submission surface.  The external-support case is exactly the normal form of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}: a positive external
support reading is not a consequence of a local digest, local manifest, local
path, or bibliography row, but requires either the upload receipt or the
archive-equivalent byte-equality locator listed there.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
shows that the current support tuple contains neither such coordinate.  Hence an
unconditional instance of \(u\) is not determined by the current projection, while
the local/path-verified conditional reading is exactly the projection that
remains after the stronger tag is removed.

The formal-source case follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction},
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  Those results identify the
available newmath evidence as finite path, commit-string, line-range, marker,
snapshot, JSON-equality, manifest-agreement, and label-containment rows.  A fresh
Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity audit additionally reads a command execution
state and a checked predicate.  Since those fields are not coordinates of the
bounded source-interface record, two support states can agree on every current
source-interface field and differ on rebuild success or axiom purity.  Therefore
\(f\) is accepted exactly after the stated formal-source command row is added;
without it the accepted reading is bounded source-interface support only.

The artifact case is the same coordinate argument applied to evaluator rows.
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} say that finite witness
manifests, evaluator-record rows, historical status snapshots, and digest rows do
not by themselves run a validator or interpret Rule~110/artifact semantics for
this submission.  A dynamic semantic-validation claim reads the validator
contract, source, inputs, run environment, command result, log, and digest binding
named in item~3.  Absent those fields, two support states can have identical
manifest and evaluator records while differing on the fresh semantic-validation
outcome; hence \(a\) is not determined by the current projection and the maximal
current reading is manifest/evaluator-record support.

For minimality, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} to each of the
three coordinates.  Removing the stronger-reading tag removes the only claim that
queries the missing coordinate and returns to the accepted finite-record
projection described above.  Adding the named coordinate supplies precisely the
finite field on which that stronger reading depends; the remaining two axes are
independent by the product decomposition in
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton} and by the terminal
classification of Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}.  Thus each
bad subrecord is inclusion-minimal and axis-specific.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded manuscript reading]
\label{cor:manuscript-reading-boundary}
In the present manuscript, every bundle-backed, public-source, or artifact-row
claim is read through
Proposition~\ref{prop:external-coordinate-admissibility-trichotomy}.  Thus
the paper makes no unconditional external-support claim without the coordinate
\(u\), no fresh formal-source rebuild or axiom-purity claim without the coordinate
\(f\), and no dynamic artifact-semantic-validation claim without the coordinate
\(a\).  The positive contribution that remains in all three cases is the
finite-record safety theorem chain headed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, with the evidence level projected
to local/path-verified support, bounded source-interface rows, and
manifest/evaluator records as appropriate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The proposition gives the exhaustive admissibility trichotomy for exactly the
three readings named in the statement.  The finite-record safety theorem is the
common accepted projection because its hypotheses read only the submitted record
surface, record-gate rows, source-interface rows, manifests, logs, and explicit
boundary fields listed in Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}; it does
not query the absent upload/archive, formal-source command, or artifact-validator
coordinates.  Therefore every occurrence of the three classes of claim factors
through the corresponding projected evidence level until its positive coordinate
is added.
\end{proof}

\label{cor:local-only-artifact-support-closure}
For the current CICM presentation-route package, after the accepted

\begin{proof}

Proposition~\ref{prop:external-coordinate-admissibility-trichotomy} then

In the current source package the four issue coordinates

records the pinned commit, source paths, environment, command, exit code, log
path, and checked predicate.  The artifact component is the manifest/evaluator
record projection of
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}; it is not semantic
Rule~110/GroundCompiler validation unless a fresh evaluator contract and command
tuple with digest binding are added.  The venue component is the dated
local-readiness projection of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}; it is not an
upload-time compliance coordinate unless an upload-time live check or explicit
unchanged-rule bridge is added.  Consequently no accepted theorem in the current
manuscript can use any of the four stronger readings without first extending the
finite support surface by the corresponding positive coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let \(P\) be the finite projection consisting of the local bundle paths, local
SHA--256 digest rows, pinned source-interface rows, historical artifact manifest
rows, and the dated 2026-06-13 venue/bibliography log.  The proof is by the
finite-coordinate classifier.  For review-bundle support,
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
and Proposition~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition} identify the
positive external-support coordinates and prove that local paths, local digest
rows, and manifest statements do not instantiate them.  Therefore every support
state agreeing with \(P\) has the same local exact-inclusion reading, while two
extensions can agree on \(P\) and differ on whether an upload receipt or public
byte-equality locator has been supplied.  External support is therefore not
determined by \(P\) and is accepted only after that positive coordinate is added.

For the formal-source component,
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} prove that the
current imported-source evidence consists only of path, commit, line-range,
snapshot, manifest-agreement, and bounded-summary fields.  A fresh Lean/BEDC
rebuild, marker-existence audit, or axiom-purity audit queries an additional
command-result predicate: the command, environment, source state, exit code, log
path, and checked property.  Since those fields are absent from \(P\), two
support states may agree on \(P\) and differ on the rebuild or audit outcome.
The finite-coordinate determination theorem therefore forbids reconstructing the
formal-source coordinate from the bounded source-interface projection, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} accepts it once the named
command row is added.

For the artifact component,
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure} make the evaluator contract and
fresh command tuple the unique semantic upgrade over the historical
manifest/evaluator rows.  The current projection \(P\) contains no such contract,
run environment, command result, log path, or digest-bound semantic predicate, so
artifact semantic validity is independent of \(P\).  It is consequently rejected
as a stronger reading until the fresh evaluator coordinate is added.

For the venue component,
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} separate a
dated local-readiness observation from actual upload-time compliance.  The dated
2026-06-13 log records only the rule state observed at that date; it contains no
completed-upload timestamp and no finite bridge proving that the same rule state
governed a later upload.  Thus upload-time compliance is independent of \(P\) and
requires exactly the stated upload-time or unchanged-rule coordinate.

The four coordinates are distinct projections of the certificate schema by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}; changing one of them
does not populate the others.  The accepted normal form is therefore unique: the
accepted package reads the four axes only as local/path-verified support, bounded
source-interface evidence, manifest/evaluator-record evidence, and dated
local-readiness evidence.  Any stronger use adds the corresponding positive
coordinate before it can enter the theorem chain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-chain closure]
\label{cor:support-chain-closure}
After the ordered post-inventory tuple \((I,R,D)\) of
Proposition~\ref{prop:exact-submitted-issue-coordinate-skeleton} has been produced, the
current presentation-route theorem chain has no additional positive support
coordinate beyond the local/path-verified finite-record projection.  In
particular, any use of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} in the
accepted package is conditional on record-gate soundness and factors through the
positive post-inventory byte coordinate, the dated 2026-06-13 local-readiness
venue record, and the three negative boundaries for external support, fresh
formal-source rebuilding or axiom audit, and dynamic artifact validation.  Hence
the support-boundary issue set is discharged inside the main theorem chain exactly as a
finite-record support theorem, not as an upload theorem, formal-source theorem,
artifact-semantic theorem, or actual-submission-date venue-compliance theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:submitted-support-issue-coordinate-discharge} gives the five
support-boundary coordinates.  Proposition~\ref{prop:exact-submitted-issue-coordinate-skeleton}
identifies the post-inventory coordinate as \((I,R,D)\), identifies the venue
coordinate as dated local-readiness evidence only, and proves that the external,
formal-source, artifact-semantic, and upload-time venue-compliance upgrades are
not determined by that tuple.  The factorisation assertion is therefore the
terminal classification of Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-five-coordinate-closure}
combined with
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-support-normal-form-four-live-coordinates} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}.
The final sentence is only a restatement by cases of the missing coordinates:
external support requires its upload or archive coordinate, formal-source
semantics requires its rebuild or axiom-audit coordinate, artifact semantics
requires its evaluator rerun coordinate, and actual-submission-date venue
compliance requires its upload-time check or unchanged-rule bridge.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-obstruction finite-coordinate normal form]
\label{thm:five-obstruction-finite-coordinate-normal-form}
For the current presentation-package source state, the following five
missing-support readings have disjoint first positive upgrade coordinates:
record-gate implementation soundness; fresh formal-source rebuild or
axiom-purity audit; dynamic artifact semantic validation; external upload or
archive-equivalent support; and upload-time venue compliance or acceptance.  More
precisely, let \(P\) be
the finite submitted projection consisting of the current abstract
record-gate-soundness hypothesis, the bounded imported-source interface, the
manifest-bounded artifact rows, the local support paths and digest rows, and the
dated 2026-06-13 venue-readiness record.  Then every accepted theorem in the
current manuscript that factors through \(P\) has exactly the bounded reading
printed in the relevant theorem statement.  A stronger reading in one of the five
directions above is accepted only after adjoining, respectively,
\begin{enumerate}
\item an implementation-audit row for the gate predicate, with program identity,
specification, source state, command, environment, input/output records, exit
code, log path, digest binding, and the checked implementation predicate;
\item a formal-source row naming the Lean/BEDC or newmath source state, paths,
command, environment, exit code, log path, and rebuild or axiom-purity predicate;
\item an artifact-validation row naming evaluator source, evaluator contract,
inputs, command, environment, exit code, output manifest, digest binding, and the
semantic predicate checked;
\item an external-support row consisting of either a venue-upload receipt for the
same digest-identified support surface or an archive-equivalent public
byte-equality locator for those bytes;
\item an upload-time venue row consisting of a live venue/bibliography compliance
check at the actual upload time, or a finite unchanged-rule bridge from the dated
local-readiness record to that upload time, together with any receipt, decision,
acceptance, or proceedings-publication status claimed.
\end{enumerate}
Without the corresponding row, the stronger reading has a finite bad subrecord
and projects back to the bounded current-package theorem chain.  In particular,
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} remains an explicitly conditional
record-gate-soundness theorem; the source-interface theorems remain bounded
source-interface theorems; the Rule110/GroundCompiler material remains
manifest/path and historical-limitation evidence; the support-surface theorems do
not assert upload or archive instantiation; and the venue theorems do not infer
acceptance or upload-time compliance from local readiness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All five readings are stronger readings in the preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}: each asserts the current finite
coordinates of \(P\) and adds at least one implementation, formal-source,
artifact-semantic, external-support, or venue-status coordinate.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, an accepted stronger reading must
pass the same finite certificate schema after that added coordinate is present;
by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, two workflow
states that agree on \(P\) but differ only outside \(P\) cannot be distinguished
by any certificate constructor used by the current manuscript; and by
Theorem~\ref{thm:external-interface-projection-no-free-upgrade}, a missing
external coordinate cannot be manufactured by conjoining accepted bounded
projections.  It remains only to identify the first missing coordinate in each
of the five typed directions.

For record-gate implementation soundness, the current use of
Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine} supplies the abstract predicate
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)\) and the finite rows read by that predicate.  It
does not include a submitted audit of the concrete gate programs or their runtime
histories.  Theorem~\ref{thm:three-boundary-upgrade-sharpness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion} identify the
first positive upgrade as the implementation-audit coordinate containing the
program identity, specification, source state, command, environment, input/output
records, exit code, log path, digest binding, and checked predicate.  Holding
\(P\) fixed while varying such an unsubmitted implementation audit leaves the
publication certificate unchanged, so the stronger implementation reading is not
determined by \(P\).  Its omission is therefore a finite bad subrecord.

For formal-source rebuild and axiom purity, the current source interface is the
bounded projection classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}: source path,
commit or snapshot information, labels, bounded paraphrase, table or JSON
agreement, and in-range checks.  Theorem~\ref{thm:local-support-normal-form-four-live-coordinates}
separates that projection from a fresh command-result predicate for a Lean/BEDC
or newmath rebuild, marker audit, or axiom-purity audit.  Since the command,
environment, exit code, log path, source state, and checked rebuild or axiom
predicate are absent from \(P\), two states may agree on \(P\) and differ on that
audit.  Thus the formal-source stronger reading is accepted exactly after the
formal-source row in item~2 is added, and otherwise has the stated bad subrecord.

For dynamic artifact semantic validation,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade} identify
the current coordinate as manifest-bounded artifact evidence: manifest entries,
local paths, reviewable snapshots, boundary fields, status rows, and limitation
rows.  They also identify the first semantic upgrade as an evaluator contract and
fresh command tuple bound to the artifact bytes or manifest.  Varying an
unsubmitted evaluator source, evaluator run, output manifest, or checked semantic
predicate while preserving \(P\) leaves the accepted manifest certificate fixed.
Therefore semantic Rule110/GroundCompiler validation is not a theorem of the
accepted package; it becomes one only through the artifact-validation row in
item~3.

For external support, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
and Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness} prove
that local support paths, review-bundle availability, inventory closure, and
digest rows are a local byte-coordinate and not a venue-upload receipt, DOI, or
public archive-equivalent byte-equality locator.  Hence two states can agree on
all local bytes and digests in \(P\) while differing on whether an external
receipt or public locator exists.  The first positive external-support coordinate
is consequently exactly the receipt or locator of item~4.

For venue compliance and acceptance,
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Proposition~\ref{audit:venue-submission-pack-gate}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} separate the
dated 2026-06-13 local-readiness record from actual upload-time compliance,
reviewer decision, acceptance, and proceedings publication.  A later upload time
may have a different venue-rule state unless a fresh live check or unchanged-rule
bridge is supplied, and a receipt or decision status is a further finite record.
Those fields are absent from \(P\), so the venue-status stronger reading is
accepted only through the row in item~5 and otherwise projects back to dated
local readiness.

The five first positive coordinates lie on distinct typed axes of the certificate
schema: gate implementation, formal source, artifact semantics, external support,
and venue status.  The disjointness and bad-subrecord normal form therefore
follow from Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-record-certificate-rigidity}.  Applying the
projection theorem once more gives the final sentence: deleting the unsupported
stronger tag returns exactly to the bounded current-package theorem chain, while
adding the appropriate row creates a new finite coordinate that must be checked on
its own terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inventory-synchronized byte closure]
\label{cor:current-byte-closure}
In the current presentation-package state, suppose the four finite checks
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py} have been rerun
after the accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes are present, and suppose
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} has then been regenerated over the
resulting source, inventory, verifier-log, and review-bundle bytes.  Then the
post-inventory support tuple for this round is closed as the ordered tuple
\((I,R,D)\): \(I\) is the pair of accepted inventory files, \(R\) is the four
passing finite-check logs with zero omitted theorem labels in the extractor log,
and \(D\) is the final digest manifest computed after those logs exist.  This
current-byte closure is exactly the positive coordinate needed by
Corollary~\ref{cor:presentation-route-support-coordinate-normal-form} for the
theorem-inventory row, and it does not change the negative boundary for
actual-submission-date venue or bibliography verification.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inventory pair is accepted before the four commands are run, so the
extractor compares the current theorem-like environment labels against the
accepted JSON inventory rather than against a missing or pre-round file.  Its
zero omitted-label count is therefore the syntactic coverage coordinate supplied
by Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}.  The
other three commands are the retained finite-record verifiers for certificate
records, source-interface records, and primary-claim records; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}, their command-result content
is current for this package only with the displayed command, source state,
environment, exit status, and log bytes.  These four logs are precisely the
rerun component \(R\).

Regenerating \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after the inventory
files and the four log files exist makes the digest row \(D\) a digest of the
post-inventory support surface rather than a digest of an earlier placeholder.
Hence \((I,R,D)\) is ordered exactly as required in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point},
Proposition~\ref{prop:exact-submitted-issue-coordinate-skeleton}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-chain-closure}.  Those results
identify this tuple as a local finite-record coordinate only: it is syntactic
inventory coverage plus verifier-log and digest binding, not semantic
proof-checking, external upload, dynamic artifact validation, or venue outcome.
Finally,
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} keep the venue and
bibliography coordinate dated; no actual-submission-date venue fact follows
unless an upload-time check or unchanged-rule bridge is added at submission time.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted inventory coordinate realization]
\label{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}
For the presentation package, an accepted theorem-inventory coordinate is
realized exactly by the ordered local tuple
\[
  (I,E,C,S,P,D),
\]
where \(I\) is the pair \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} in the repository root, with the JSON inventory
containing every labelled theorem-like environment extracted from the current
\path{main.tex}; \(E\) is the post-inventory theorem-environment extraction log
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log} for the command
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py}, including zero
omitted labels against those inventory bytes; \(C\), \(S\), and \(P\) are
respectively the post-inventory verifier logs
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_verification_run.log} for the three
commands \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py},
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}, and
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}; and \(D\) is
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} regenerated after those four logs
exist and containing digest rows for \(I,E,C,S,P\).  This coordinate is
sufficient and necessary for current-byte local theorem-inventory support, and it
is not a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, axiom-purity audit, external upload/archive
locator, upload-time venue-compliance record, venue-acceptance coordinate, or
dynamic artifact-semantic validation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Sufficiency is the positive direction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}: once the inventory bytes are accepted,
the extractor log supplies syntactic coverage of labelled theorem-like
environments against those bytes, and its zero omitted-label field is precisely
the finite predicate that the accepted JSON inventory contains the current
manuscript's theorem labels.  The three verifier logs supply the retained finite
certificate, source-interface, and primary-claim checks on the same package state.
The final digest manifest binds the resulting byte surface after those logs exist;
because it contains rows for the inventory pair and for each log path, the digest
coordinate is a digest of the post-inventory support surface rather than a digest
of a prior or temporary ledger.  Therefore the tuple \((I,E,C,S,P,D)\) is an
accepted local current-byte theorem-inventory support coordinate.

Necessity is the stale-coordinate direction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}.  If \(I\) is missing, there is
no accepted inventory byte pair for the extractor to compare against.  If \(E\)
is missing, label coverage has not been evaluated on the accepted inventory
bytes.  If any of \(C\), \(S\), or \(P\) is missing, the corresponding retained
finite-record predicate lacks a current command-result row.  If \(D\) is missing
or predates one of the four logs, the support surface lacks the last-byte digest
binding required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}.  In each
case two package states may agree on all older records and differ on the missing
current-byte predicate, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} forbids accepting the
current-byte inventory claim.

The non-upgrade clause follows because every component of
\((I,E,C,S,P,D)\) is a local inventory, finite-verifier, or byte-digest record.
The formal-source rebuild and axiom-purity fields are separated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}; the upload/archive fields
are separated by Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}; the
upload-time venue and acceptance fields are separated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}; and the
artifact-semantic fields are separated by
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  Thus the tuple closes
only the local theorem-inventory coordinate and none of the stronger coordinates.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Fresh post-inventory byte-closure rerun discharge]
\label{prop:fresh-post-inventory-byte-closure-rerun-discharge}
Fix a presentation-package state in which the accepted root theorem inventory is
the pair \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  The
issue labelled \path{fresh post-inventory byte-closure rerun} is discharged for
that state exactly when the following ordered byte operation has occurred after
those two inventory files exist: first the theorem-environment extractor and the
three retained finite-record verifiers are rerun, producing the four logs named
in Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization} with exit code
\path{0}; then \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated over
the resulting source, inventory, log, and review-bundle bytes.  In that case the
discharged coordinate is the local finite-record coordinate
\((I,E,C,S,P,D)\) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}.  If any manuscript,
inventory, verifier-log, manifest, or digest byte named by that coordinate is
changed later without repeating the same ordered operation, the issue reopens as
a stale-byte coordinate until the operation is repeated.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The forward direction is only an unfolding of the issue.  The issue exists
because a digest or support row that names \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} cannot be current before those root files have final
bytes.  Once the files exist, Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure} requires
the extractor and finite-record verifier tuple to be rerun against that accepted
inventory state and requires the final digest surface to be regenerated last.
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization} identifies the
resulting ordered data with the local coordinate \((I,E,C,S,P,D)\), where
\(E\) records zero omitted theorem labels and \(C,S,P\) record the three retained
finite checks.  Therefore the ordered operation is sufficient to discharge the
fresh-rerun issue at the local finite-record level.

Conversely, suppose the issue is discharged for a package state.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}, a positive current-byte
theorem-inventory reading cannot be inferred from an old extractor log, an old
verifier log, or a digest manifest that predates the accepted inventory or the
logs it is supposed to bind.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}, the
digest row contributes only the byte state it actually hashes; it does not make
later inventory or log bytes retroactively present.  Hence any discharge must
contain the accepted inventory pair, the post-inventory extractor run, the three
post-inventory finite-verifier runs, and the last regenerated digest manifest.
This is exactly the ordered operation stated above, and its coordinate is exactly
\((I,E,C,S,P,D)\).

For the final sentence, changing any byte named by the coordinate changes one of
the finite predicates whose value is determined by that byte: inventory coverage,
one of the finite verifier outcomes, or the final digest binding.  The finite
coordinate determination boundary,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, then separates the
new package state from the old one.  Without repeating the ordered operation,
the package has only an earlier-byte record and so falls back to the stale-byte
case of Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}.  Repeating the
operation restores the same local coordinate and discharges the issue again.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Realized post-inventory verifier--digest coordinate]
\label{prop:realized-post-inventory-verifier-digest-coordinate}
In the accepted package state, the post-inventory coordinate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization} is realized by the
root inventory pair \path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md},
the four logs
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_verification_run.log}, and the final
manifest \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, provided these are read
with the following finite fields: the extractor log has
\path{exit_code: 0}, \path{errors: 0}, \path{missing_label_count: 0}, and
\path{omitted_from_inventory_count: 0}; each of the three verifier logs has
\path{exit_code: 0}; and the final digest manifest contains rows for the two
inventory files and all four post-inventory logs.  This realization closes the
local theorem-inventory issue and still leaves the external upload/archive
coordinate absent unless a separate uploaded supplement receipt, DOI, or
archive-equivalent public byte locator is supplied.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
