The accepted inventory coordinate has six components.  The first component is
the root inventory pair, which is present by hypothesis as the two named root
files.  The extractor component is a syntactic predicate on the current
\path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json}; the four displayed extractor
fields say exactly that the command terminated successfully, found no extractor
errors, found no labelled theorem-like environments missing from the current
inventory, and omitted no current labels from the inventory comparison.  Thus it
supplies the \(E\)-component of
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}.  The three retained
verifier logs, each with exit code \path{0}, supply the certificate,
source-interface, and primary-claim components \(C,S,P\) of that theorem, and
their role is finite-record verification only by the verifier boundary stated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract}.

It remains to check the last coordinate.  A digest manifest that contains rows
for the two inventory files and all four just-named post-inventory logs binds
the byte surface after those records exist; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:fresh-post-inventory-byte-closure-rerun-discharge}, this
is precisely the \(D\)-component required after inventory acceptance and verifier
rerun.  Combining the six components gives the tuple \((I,E,C,S,P,D)\), so
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization} identifies it as the
realized local theorem-inventory support coordinate.

The final sentence is not an additional computation but the non-upgrade clause
of the same theorem together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary}: all files just named
are local inventory, verifier-log, or digest records.  None is an uploaded
supplement receipt, DOI, or public byte-equality locator.  Therefore the local
coordinate is closed, while the external upload/archive coordinate remains
uninstantiated until one of those separate byte locators is added.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current accepted inventory tuple instantiation]
\label{thm:current-accepted-inventory-tuple-instantiation}
In the current local package, the accepted theorem-inventory coordinate is
realized exactly by the finite tuple whose components are as follows:
\(I\) is the pair \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}; \(E\) is
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log}; \(C\) is
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log}; \(S\) is
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log}; \(P\) is
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_verification_run.log}; and \(D\) is
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
The tuple closes the local theorem-obligation-ledger coordinate precisely when
the extractor log and the three retained verifier logs are zero-exit reruns made
after the accepted bytes of \(I\) exist, the extractor log has no omitted current
theorem labels, and \(D\) is regenerated after those logs with digest rows for
\(I,E,C,S,P\).  This is a local/path-verified finite-record coordinate only: it
does not instantiate record-gate soundness for
\((P_0,S_0,L_0,\Gamma_0)\), a fresh formal-source rebuild, an axiom-purity audit,
dynamic Rule110/GroundCompiler artifact validation, venue acceptance, or an
external upload/archive support coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed tuple is the concrete specialization of the abstract tuple
\((I,E,C,S,P,D)\) in
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}.  The two root files
are the accepted inventory component \(I\).  A post-inventory zero-exit extractor
log with no omitted current labels supplies the syntactic label-coverage
component \(E\).  The three zero-exit verifier logs supply the retained
certificate, source-interface, and primary-claim finite predicates \(C,S,P\).
Finally, a digest manifest regenerated after those four logs and containing rows
for all five prior components supplies \(D\).  Hence the sufficiency direction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}, equivalently
Proposition~\ref{prop:realized-post-inventory-verifier-digest-coordinate}, closes
the local theorem-obligation-ledger coordinate.  The necessity direction of that
theorem gives the converse: without one of these ordered components, the package
has either missing accepted inventory bytes, a stale extractor or verifier row,
or a digest that does not bind the post-rerun support surface.

The non-upgrade assertion follows by coordinate separation.  The tuple contains
only local inventory files, finite-verifier logs, and local digest rows.  It has
no accepted record-gate-soundness row for \((P_0,S_0,L_0,\Gamma_0)\), no
formal-source command with source state, environment, exit code, log path,
rebuild predicate, marker predicate, and axiom-purity pass row, no artifact
evaluator contract with input bytes and semantic predicate, no venue decision or
upload-time compliance row, and no supplemental-upload receipt or public
byte-equality locator.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:presentation-package-five-coordinate-support-closure}, bounded evidence
on one finite coordinate cannot be glued into any absent independent coordinate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Presentation-route support-coordinate normal form]
\label{cor:presentation-route-support-coordinate-normal-form}
For the presentation-only route of this source package, the five issue
coordinates resolved by the terminal theorem chain have the following exact
normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-inventory support coordinate is present exactly when
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} exist before the
theorem-environment extractor and retained finite-record verifiers are rerun,
and \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those log
bytes exist.  Its content is syntactic and finite-record only.
\item The external support-surface coordinate is absent from the local package
unless an exact supplemental upload or an archive-equivalent public locator with
matching byte-equality fields is added.  Local digest rows and local verifier
logs therefore support only local/path-verified bundle claims.
\item Fresh formal-source semantics is not current evidence in this route.
Lean/BEDC marker rows, bounded source paths, and axiom-purity vocabulary remain
path-verified source-interface records unless a fresh rebuild or axiom-audit
command-result coordinate is supplied.
\item Dynamic artifact semantics is not current evidence in this route.
Rule~110/GroundCompiler rows, daemon rows, manifests, evaluator records, and
historical status rows remain finite witness records unless a fresh
artifact-validation rerun coordinate is supplied.
\item Venue and bibliography facts are dated local-readiness facts, not
actual-submission-date facts.  The 2026-06-13 live check remains dated route
context unless the package adds an upload-time live check or an explicit
unchanged-rule bridge tying the completed upload to that dated record.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the current theorem chain is strong enough for the stated scope exactly as
a schema-relative finite-record safety theorem under record-gate soundness, and
any stronger end-to-end reading has a missing finite coordinate rather than an
implicit proof; its classifier is the inclusion-minimal bad subrecord consisting
of the stronger-reading row and the first missing coordinate named in items~1--5.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Item~1 is precisely the positive local coordinate constructed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}, instantiated by
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-post-inventory-support-tuple-instantiation} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-accepted-inventory-tuple-instantiation}, and closed for the local package by
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}: the inventory bytes
precede the extractor and verifier logs, and the digest manifest is computed
only after those logs exist.  The extractor boundary results,
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
Theorem~\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-inventory-proofchecker-obstruction}, identify the
coordinate as syntactic coverage rather than proof semantics.

Item~2 follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
Proposition~\ref{prop:no-external-instantiation-from-local-bundle-records}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.
Those results classify the only positive external-support records and prove that
the local digest and verifier surface does not contain them.

Item~3 is the formal-source case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure},
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}: bounded
marker, snapshot, path, line-range, and source-interface rows do not assert a
fresh rebuild or axiom-purity audit without their own formal-source command row.

Item~4 is the artifact-validation case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}: finite manifests,
evaluator rows, and historical status snapshots remain manifest/evaluator-record
evidence unless the validator source, specification, command row, exit status,
log, and digest-binding coordinate is supplied.

Item~5 is the venue-freshness case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}: dated venue
and bibliography checks are historical/local-readiness records, whereas actual
submission-date compliance requires an upload-time check or a finite
unchanged-rule bridge.

Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} to the five
displayed projections gives the minimal-bad-subrecord classifier, and the
schema-relative safety statement is Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}
with the record-gate premise left explicit and the venue record kept dated.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Inventory and venue-coordinate closure]
\label{thm:inventory-venue-coordinate-closure}
Let \(Q\) be the current presentation-route package state after local theorem-inventory acceptance.  Suppose the accepted root inventory
pair is the byte pair
\(I\), consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Then the
strongest support claim available in \(Q\) is the following finite-coordinate
classification.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The post-inventory theorem-ledger coordinate is positive exactly when,
after the bytes of both files in \(I\) are fixed, the command
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py} is rerun with exit
code \path{0} and zero omitted theorem labels, the retained finite-record
verifiers are rerun at the same post-inventory package state, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those log
bytes exist with digest rows for both files in \(I\) and for the resulting
extractor and verifier logs.
\item Before that ordered tuple is present, every current-byte or
post-inventory fixed-point reading of the theorem inventory has an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord: the first absent member among the accepted
inventory pair, the post-inventory extractor log, the retained verifier logs,
and the post-log digest manifest.
\item No local digest row, extractor log, inventory row, or verifier log supplies
a submission-time venue or upload coordinate.  A completed-submission support
claim therefore remains inadmissible unless the package separately adds an
upload receipt, DOI-bearing supplement, archive-equivalent public byte locator,
fresh upload-time venue-compliance check, or explicit unchanged-rule bridge for
the completed upload state.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the local package may close the missing inventory and
extraction issues only as a local, syntactic, finite-record fixed point; it may
not use those same rows to assert completed external support or
actual-submission-time venue compliance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For item~1, apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} with the accepted inventory
pair \(I\) as the first two coordinates of the package state.  That theorem
orders the inventory write before the theorem-environment extraction, the
finite-record verifiers, and the final digest pass.  The extractor contributes
only the syntactic coverage fact isolated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}: the run
must be over the same \path{main.tex} and accepted
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, must exit with the recorded zero status, and must
have no omitted labelled environments in the extractor domain.  The retained
verifier logs contribute exactly the command-result fields classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  Finally,
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} force the
digest manifest to be generated after those files and logs exist; otherwise its
rows identify earlier bytes.  Thus the positive coordinate is exactly the
ordered tuple stated in item~1.

For item~2, suppose a stronger current-byte or post-inventory fixed-point
reading is made before the ordered tuple of item~1 exists.  If a member of the
inventory pair is absent, there is no accepted theorem-inventory coordinate.  If
the extractor log is absent or stale, the coverage assertion has not been
computed over the accepted inventory bytes.  If one of the retained verifier
logs is absent or stale, the finite-record rows that depend on the package state
are not current command-result coordinates.  If the digest manifest is absent or
pre-log, its SHA--256 rows cannot bind the accepted inventory and command-log
bytes.  In each case the single stronger-reading row together with the first
missing coordinate is precisely the bad-subrecord skeleton of
Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-minimal-bad-record-witness}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} prevents the missing
coordinate from being reconstructed from the remaining local rows.

For item~3, the positive coordinate in item~1 contains only local paths, command
metadata, exit codes, log bytes, and SHA--256 rows.  Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
lists the separate positive forms for external support, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that local bundle records do not instantiate them.  Similarly,
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} separate a
dated local-readiness check from upload-time venue compliance.  Therefore the
inventory/extractor/digest fixed point can close only the local syntactic
support coordinate and cannot supply a completed-submission, upload, DOI,
archive-equivalence, or actual-submission-date venue coordinate.  This proves
the classification and the final consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Four-coordinate local-support discharge]
\label{thm:four-coordinate-local-support-discharge}
Let \(Q_6\) be the current presentation-route package state after accepting the
root theorem-inventory pair \(I_6\), namely \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Let \(R_6\) be the ordered tuple of post-inventory local command records
consisting of the theorem-environment extractor and the certificate-record,
source-interface, and primary-claim verifiers, and let \(D_6\) be the
SHA--256 digest manifest regenerated after the bytes of \(I_6\) and \(R_6\)
exist.  Then the four support issues for this route have the following complete
classification.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The post-inventory rerun-and-digest coordinate is positive exactly for the
local finite-record tuple \((I_6,R_6,D_6)\), with zero-exit command records,
zero omitted theorem labels in the extractor record, and digest rows for both
root inventory files and all four post-inventory logs.
\item The external support/upload/archive coordinate is negative unless the
support surface also contains an exact upload receipt, a DOI-bearing
supplemental coordinate, or an archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator
for the final support bytes.
\item The fresh formal-source verification coordinate is negative unless the
support surface also contains a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, source-verification,
or axiom-purity record with command, source commit or local source state,
environment, exit code, and log path.
\item The fresh artifact-semantic validation coordinate is negative unless the
support surface also contains a fresh artifact-validation tuple with the
manifest rows, semantic contract, command, environment, exit code, log path, and
digest binding for that validation.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the strongest admissible reading of the current package is local
and path-verified: accepting \((I_6,R_6,D_6)\) closes the theorem-inventory
support issue but does not upgrade bounded source-interface rows to fresh
formal verification, finite artifact witness rows to dynamic artifact semantics,
or local review-bundle bytes to an external upload/archive coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Item~1 is the realized positive coordinate of
Proposition~\ref{prop:realized-post-inventory-verifier-digest-coordinate} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:inventory-venue-coordinate-closure}.  Those results order the
root inventory write before the extractor and finite-record verifier reruns and
order the digest pass last.  The extractor component is purely syntactic by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}: its
positive fields say that the current theorem-like labels are represented in the
accepted inventory, not that the displayed proofs were checked.  The three
verifier components are finite-record checks by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  The digest component is a
byte-binding coordinate by Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}.
Combining these four facts gives exactly the tuple \((I_6,R_6,D_6)\), and any
missing member of that ordered tuple is the first missing finite coordinate
classified by Proposition~\ref{prop:fresh-post-inventory-byte-closure-rerun-discharge}.

Item~2 is independent of item~1.  The local tuple \((I_6,R_6,D_6)\) contains
only repository paths, command metadata, exit statuses, logs, and SHA--256 rows.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:upload-or-archive-instantiation-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}, the positive
external forms are exactly an exact-upload record or an archive-equivalent
public byte locator, with a DOI-bearing supplemental coordinate serving as the
same external byte locator when present.  Since none of these fields is a
function of the local inventory, verifier, or digest rows, the finite-coordinate
determination boundary, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary},
keeps the external coordinate negative until a separate external record is
added.

Item~3 is the formal-source projection.  Proposition~\ref{prop:formal-source-gate-instantiation},
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} prove that
pinned source paths, marker rows, line ranges, and axiom-purity vocabulary are
bounded source-interface evidence only.  A fresh formal-source assertion changes
the evidence kind to a build, source-verification, or axiom-audit command-result
claim.  The command-result closure theorem therefore requires the command,
source state, environment, exit status, and log path for that run.  If those
fields are absent, the stronger reading has the missing formal-source gate or
missing command-result subrecord named in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}; hence the current
bounded rows cannot be read as fresh formal verification.

Item~4 is the artifact-semantics projection.  The finite witness rows identified
by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} carry manifest,
evaluator, limitation-ledger, and historical snapshot content.  A dynamic
artifact-semantic claim adds a semantic contract and a fresh validator execution
coordinate.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, that
upgrade is possible only through the displayed artifact-validation tuple; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, it cannot be
reconstructed from local theorem-inventory, source-interface, or digest rows.

The four projections use disjoint finite coordinates of the support schema.  A
positive value in the post-inventory projection therefore leaves the external,
formal-source, and artifact-semantic projections unchanged.  The final sentence
is exactly the normal form of
Corollary~\ref{cor:presentation-route-support-coordinate-normal-form} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-support-surface-classifier} specialized to the four
issues named here.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Local-support classifier]
\label{thm:local-support-surface-classifier}
Let \(Q_5\) be the presentation-route package state after the local theorem-inventory write.  Let \(I_5\) be the byte pair consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}, let
\(R_5\) be the ordered command tuple consisting of the theorem-environment
extractor, certificate-record verifier, source-interface verifier, and
primary-claim verifier rerun after the bytes of \(I_5\) are fixed, and let
\(D_5\) be the SHA--256 digest manifest regenerated after those command-log
bytes exist.  In \(Q_5\), the five local missing-support coordinates have
the following exact normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-inventory coordinate is positive exactly when the ordered
tuple \((I_5,R_5,D_5)\) is present with zero-exit command logs and digest rows
for the inventory pair and for the resulting extractor and verifier logs.
\item The actual-submission-date venue coordinate is absent unless the support
surface also contains either an actual-submission-date venue/bibliography live
check or a finite unchanged-rule bridge from the dated local-readiness check to
the upload action.
\item The external upload-or-archive coordinate is absent unless the support
surface contains an upload receipt, DOI-bearing supplement, or
archive-equivalent public locator with byte-equality/digest fields for the
submitted support surface.
\item The fresh newmath/BEDC formal-source coordinate is absent unless the
support surface contains a fresh rebuild, source-verification, or axiom/audit row
with source commit, environment, command, exit code, and log path.
\item The dynamic artifact-semantic coordinate is absent unless the support
surface contains a fresh artifact-evaluator tuple with manifest rows, semantic
contract, command, environment, exit code, log path, and digest binding.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the local package can close the theorem-inventory issue only
as a local, syntactic, post-inventory finite-record fixed point.  It does not
thereby acquire upload/archive support, actual-submission-date venue compliance,
fresh newmath/BEDC rebuild evidence, or fresh dynamic artifact semantics.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first coordinate is the same fixed-point pattern as
Theorem~\ref{thm:inventory-venue-coordinate-closure}, with the accepted
inventory pair replaced by the local inventory bytes \(I_5\).  The extractor and the
three retained finite-record verifiers are command-result claims, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} requires their post-inventory
command rows rather than earlier logs.  The digest manifest is a byte claim about
the files it names; by Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}, it closes
the coordinate only when regenerated after the accepted inventory and post-log
bytes exist.  Thus the positive theorem-inventory coordinate is precisely the
ordered tuple \((I_5,R_5,D_5)\), and before any member of this tuple exists the
first missing member is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord by
Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-minimal-bad-record-witness}.

For the venue coordinate, Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} separate a
dated local-readiness check from an upload-time compliance record.  The former
records the observed rule state on its stated date; it contains no upload action,
form state, or finite bridge proving that the same rule state governed a later
actual submission.  Hence the actual-submission-date coordinate is absent unless
one of the two positive records listed in item~2 is added.

For external support, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
lists the positive upload/archive forms and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that local review-bundle paths, local digest rows, and local verifier logs
do not instantiate them.  Since \((I_5,R_5,D_5)\) contains only local path,
command, exit-code, log-byte, and digest data, it has no receipt, DOI, public
locator, or byte-equality bridge for a submitted support surface.  Item~3
follows.

For the newmath/BEDC coordinate,
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} prove that
pinned source-interface rows, public reachability, and imported labels are
bounded interface evidence only.  They do not assert a fresh rebuild, full source
verification, or axiom-purity audit.  Clause A6 of
Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table} supplies the finite
command-result fields needed for such a stronger reading.  Without a row naming
those fields, item~4 is exactly the bad-subrecord case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.

For dynamic artifacts,
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade},
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary},
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-row-case-evidence-closure}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-case-behaviour-evidence-criterion} show that manifest
rows and historical case snapshots remain finite evidence for the recorded rows.
A semantic artifact-validation claim changes the command-boundary and semantic
contract coordinates, so it requires the fresh evaluator tuple listed in item~5.
If that tuple is missing, the finite-coordinate determination boundary prevents
recovering it from inventory, verifier, digest, or case-snapshot rows.

The five coordinates are independent projections of the certificate schema in
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}.  Adding
\((I_5,R_5,D_5)\) changes only the local theorem-inventory projection.  It leaves
the venue/upload/source/artifact projections exactly at their stated bounded or
absent values, proving the final consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Support-coordinate closure]
\label{thm:local-support-coordinate-closure}
Let \(Q_{3}\) be the package state obtained after the manuscript and inventory records are fixed.  Let \(I_{3}\) denote the inventory
byte pair consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Let \(R_{3}\) be the ordered tuple of command rows
\begin{enumerate}
\item \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py};
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py};
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}; and
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py},
\end{enumerate}
and let \(D_{3}\) denote \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
Suppose that
each row of \(R_{3}\) is executed after the bytes of \(Q_{3}\) and \(I_{3}\)
are fixed, exits with status \(0\), writes the log path named by its verifier,
and that \(D_{3}\) is regenerated only after those four log bytes exist.  Then
the local support surface closes exactly the local theorem-inventory,
certificate-record, source-interface-record, primary-claim-inventory, and digest
coordinates.  It does not close, imply, or upgrade any external supplemental
upload/archive coordinate, actual-submission-date venue-compliance coordinate,
fresh full Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity coordinate, or dynamic
Rule~110/GroundCompiler artifact-semantic-validation coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypotheses place the two inventory files first, the four verifier command
rows second, and the digest manifest last.  Therefore
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} applies to the inventory
projection: the extractor row is computed against the accepted inventory bytes,
the finite-record verifiers are computed against the same package state, and the
digest row binds the resulting log bytes rather than an earlier pre-inventory
state.  The extractor contributes only the syntactic labelled-environment
coverage isolated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}; the
certificate, source-interface, and primary-claim verifiers contribute only the
finite command-result fields classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}; and the final digest row is
exactly the refresh coordinate required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}.  Hence the listed local
coordinates are positive.

No further coordinate is among the fields just enumerated.  External support
requires the upload receipt or archive-equivalent byte locator of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}; actual venue
compliance requires the upload-time or unchanged-rule coordinate of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}; a fresh
formal-source claim requires the command-row fields separated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}; and a
dynamic artifact-semantics claim requires the validator contract and command row
of Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  Since none of those
coordinates is a member of \(I_{3}\), \(R_{3}\), or \(D_{3}\),
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} forbids recovering it
from the local inventory/verifier/digest tuple.  The closure is therefore exact:
it proves the local finite-record fixed point and no stronger submission,
venue, source-rebuild, or artifact-semantics assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Four-blocker coordinate budget]
\label{thm:four-blocker-coordinate-budget}
Let \(S\) be any reading of the current presentation-only package obtained by
adding to the finite-record theorem chain one of the following four stronger
assertions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a post-inventory current-byte theorem-inventory fixed point;
\item an external support-surface, supplemental-upload, or archive-equivalence
claim for \path{review_bundle/};
\item a fresh full Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-audit claim for the imported
formal source; or
\item a dynamic Rule~110/GroundCompiler artifact-semantic-validation claim.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(S\) is accepted by the manuscript exactly in the following coordinate
budget.  Item~1 requires the ordered tuple \((I,R,D)\), where the accepted
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes precede the
theorem-environment extractor and the three retained finite-record verifiers,
and \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those log
bytes exist.  Item~2 requires either an exact upload receipt for the selected
support surface or a public archive-equivalent locator with matching file list,
relative paths, manifest identity, digest rows, and byte-equality data.  Item~3
requires a formal-source command row naming the source commit, environment,
commands, exit codes, logs, and axiom/assumption audit outputs.  Item~4 requires
an artifact-validation command row naming the validator source, semantic
acceptance criterion, artifact bytes, command, exit status, log path, and digest
binding.  Without the matching coordinate, the accepted projection is
respectively only conditional post-inventory closure, local/path-verified bundle
support, bounded source-interface evidence, or finite historical witness-record
evidence; the missing coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For item~1, Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:presentation-route-support-coordinate-normal-form} identify
the theorem-inventory coordinate as an ordered byte fixed point.  The inventory
pair must be present before the extractor and retained finite-record verifiers
run, because the extractor compares the current theorem-like labels against the
accepted inventory bytes.  The digest manifest must be regenerated last, because
otherwise its rows are rows for a pre-inventory or pre-log support surface.  Thus
the tuple \((I,R,D)\) is both sufficient for the local syntactic inventory
coordinate and necessary for any current-byte reading of that coordinate.

For item~2, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} lists the
two positive forms of an external support coordinate, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that local bundle paths, local logs, and local digest rows do not
instantiate either form.  Consequently the same files support only a local or
path-verified reading until an upload receipt or archive-equivalent byte locator
is supplied.

For item~3, Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction},
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure} separate bounded marker,
commit, path, snapshot, and line-range evidence from a fresh formal-source
rebuild.  A rebuild or axiom-purity assertion reads command, environment, exit,
log, and audit-output fields that are not determined by the bounded
source-interface rows, so it is accepted only after those fields are supplied.

For item~4, Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} separate manifest and
historical evaluator records from dynamic artifact semantics.  A semantic
validity assertion reads the validator, semantic criterion, artifact bytes,
command result, log, and digest-binding fields; those fields are absent from the
finite witness manifests alone.

The four coordinates lie on distinct axes of the stronger-reading preorder of
Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder} and the product decomposition in
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-coordinate-submission-support-skeleton}.  Therefore no one
coordinate can be reconstructed from another.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, two states that agree
on the submitted finite projection and differ only in one missing coordinate are
indistinguishable to the accepted finite verifier.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}, the stronger-reading
row together with the first absent required coordinate is an inclusion-minimal
bad subrecord.  This proves the exact coordinate budget and the four projected
accepted readings.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Terminal local rerun tuple]
\label{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}
Let \(Q_{\mathrm{A2}}\) be the package state obtained after the present
the local manuscript and theorem-inventory bytes have been accepted.
Let \(I_{\mathrm{A2}}\) be the byte pair consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  Let
\(R_{\mathrm{A2}}\) be the ordered command-result tuple consisting of
\begin{enumerate}
\item \path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py};
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py};
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py}; and
\item \path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}.
\end{enumerate}
Suppose that each command in \(R_{\mathrm{A2}}\) is run after the bytes of
\(I_{\mathrm{A2}}\) and \path{main.tex} are fixed, that each run records its
command, source state or source hashes, environment, exit code, and log path,
and that the final SHA--256 digest manifest is regenerated only after those log
bytes exist.  Then the strongest instantiated inventory claim in
\(Q_{\mathrm{A2}}\) is exactly the local post-write fixed point
\((I_{\mathrm{A2}},R_{\mathrm{A2}},D_{\mathrm{A2}})\), where
\(D_{\mathrm{A2}}\) is \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  This tuple
closes the theorem-environment extraction, certificate-record verifier,
source-interface verifier, primary-claim verifier, and digest coordinates for the
accepted local bytes, but it does
not instantiate any exact supplemental-upload receipt, archive-equivalent public
byte locator, upload-time venue-compliance record, fresh formal-source rebuild,
or dynamic artifact-validation record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The ordered construction supplies the positive coordinates required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: the accepted inventory
bytes precede the extractor and verifier command rows, and the digest manifest
is computed after the command-log bytes exist.  The extractor contributes only
syntactic environment coverage, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}; the
certificate-record verifier, source-interface verifier, and primary-claim
verifier contribute only the finite command-result fields classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  Regenerating
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after those logs exist is exactly
the digest-closure condition of Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}.
Therefore the inventory coordinate is positive precisely for the byte tuple
\((I_{\mathrm{A2}},R_{\mathrm{A2}},D_{\mathrm{A2}})\); before any member of that
tuple exists, the first absent member is the inclusion-minimal bad subrecord of
Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-minimal-bad-record-witness}.

It remains to show that the tuple has no stronger interpretation.  Every member
of \((I_{\mathrm{A2}},R_{\mathrm{A2}},D_{\mathrm{A2}})\) is a local path,
source-hash or source-state, command, environment, exit-code, log-byte, or digest
row.  Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
list the additional receipt or byte-equality fields required for external
support, and Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} lists the
additional upload-time or unchanged-rule fields required for actual-submission
venue compliance.  The formal-source and artifact-validation coordinates are
separate command-boundary projections by
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  Since the terminal
post-write rerun tuple contains none of those additional fields,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} prevents their
reconstruction from the inventory, verifier, or digest rows.  Hence the tuple
closes exactly the local post-write inventory support coordinate and no stronger
external, venue, source-rebuild, or artifact-semantic coordinate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional current-byte support fixed point and non-upgrade boundary]
\label{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}
Assume that the accepted local inventory pair \(I\), consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}, exists on disk,
that the theorem-environment extractor and the three retained finite-record
verifiers are rerun after those inventory bytes and the current manuscript bytes
are fixed, and that \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated
after the resulting log bytes exist.  Then, and only then, the accepted local
support state has the current-byte finite-record fixed point consisting exactly
of
\begin{enumerate}
\item the two inventory files;
\item the four post-inventory command logs for theorem-environment extraction,
certificate-record verification, source-interface verification, and
primary-claim verification; and
\item the final digest manifest computed after those inputs and logs exist.
\end{enumerate}
If any manuscript, inventory, log, or digest byte is changed after this ordered
tuple is produced, the theorem supplies only this conditional rerun criterion and
not a current-byte claim for the changed state.  The fixed point proves only
syntactic theorem-inventory coverage and the stated finite-record verifier
predicates at local/path-verified or command-run evidence level.  It does not
instantiate a venue-upload receipt, DOI-bearing replacement, archive-equivalent
byte-equality locator, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, axiom-purity audit,
marker-existence audit, dynamic Rule~110/GroundCompiler semantic rerun, artifact
evaluator contract, or venue-acceptance coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The positive part is the support-coordinate fixed-point rule applied in the
order displayed in the statement.  The inventory bytes are the first coordinate.
The extractor is then run against \path{main.tex} and
\path{theorem_inventory.json}; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}, a passing
run contributes exactly the finite predicate that every labelled theorem-like
environment extracted from the manuscript has a corresponding inventory label,
with no semantic proof-checking consequence.  The three retained verifier logs are the certificate-record verifier,
source-interface verifier, and primary-claim verifier command-result coordinates
classified by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}: they contribute their printed
commands, source hashes or source state, environments, exit codes, log paths, and
finite schema predicates, and nothing outside those predicates.  Regenerating
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} after those log bytes exist is
precisely the digest-closure condition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point},
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}.  Hence the accepted
positive coordinate is exactly the displayed local tuple.

It remains to identify the boundary.
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
show that external support needs a separate upload receipt or public
byte-equality locator; these fields are not among the three displayed
coordinates.  Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} show that
fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-existence, and axiom-purity claims require their
own command and audit predicates; the fixed point supplies only the bounded
source-interface verifier.  Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} show that dynamic
Rule~110/GroundCompiler or other artifact semantics require a fresh evaluator
contract, command, environment, exit code, log path, and digest binding; the
fixed point contains no such evaluator row.  Finally,
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation} show that venue acceptance
or upload-time venue compliance requires its own submission-time coordinate.
By the finite-coordinate determination boundary, none of these absent stronger
coordinates can be reconstructed from the accepted local tuple.  The stated
non-upgrade boundary follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Post-inventory rerun closure]
\label{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}
Let the present local source state be the state in which the
accepted manuscript bytes, \path{theorem_inventory.json}, and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} have first been written.  The assertion that this
state is a current-byte inventory fixed point is accepted by the manuscript if
and only if, after those writes, the following ordered record is present:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the fresh theorem-environment extraction log for
\path{python review_bundle/extract_theorem_environments.py};
\item the fresh certificate-record verifier log for
\path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py};
\item the fresh source-interface verifier log for
\path{python review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py};
\item the fresh primary-claim verifier log for
\path{python review_bundle/verify_primary_claim_inventory.py}; and
\item a regenerated \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} computed
after the inventory files and the four log files above exist.
\end{enumerate}
Equivalently, any pre-inventory extractor, verifier, or digest row is a stale
coordinate for this round and cannot witness current-byte fixed-point closure.
The closure remains local and does not by itself assert external support-bundle
upload, archive equivalence, DOI assignment, public availability, upload-time
venue compliance, venue acceptance, or dynamic artifact semantics.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first write in the round changes at least one of the source coordinates read
by the extractor or digest manifest: the inventory files themselves, the
manuscript bytes, or both.  A log produced before those bytes are fixed is
therefore a command-result record for a different input tuple.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}, the
positive local fixed point requires the inventory pair first, the extractor and
three retained finite-record verifier logs second, and the digest manifest last.
The four listed logs are exactly the command-result coordinates named in that
theorem and in Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}; after
they are rerun on the accepted bytes, regenerating the digest manifest binds the
resulting byte surface.  Thus the ordered five-part record is sufficient.

For necessity, remove any one part of the ordered record.  Without the fresh
extractor log, the inventory-label coverage predicate is not evaluated on the
accepted inventory bytes.  Without any one of the three verifier logs, the
corresponding finite certificate, source-interface, or primary-claim predicate
has no current command-result coordinate.  Without the final regenerated digest
manifest, the support surface has no last-byte SHA--256 binding after the new
logs exist.  In each case two package states can agree on all older records and
differ on the missing current-byte predicate, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:submission-support-obstruction-skeleton} forbid promoting the
stale row to current-byte closure.  The non-upgrade claims are exactly the
external-support, venue, formal-source, and artifact coordinates excluded in
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Submission-support obstruction skeleton]
\label{thm:submission-support-obstruction-skeleton}
Let \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be the current local support state after the accepted
inventory files, extractor log, retained finite-record verifier logs, and final
digest manifest have been regenerated in the order required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary}.  Consider
any proposed reviewer-visible package reading \(R^{+}\) that strengthens
\(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\) in one of the following three ways:
\begin{enumerate}
\item it treats \path{review_bundle/} as externally uploaded or archive-visible
support;
\item it treats a dated venue/bibliography check as actual submission-date venue
compliance or venue readiness for a later date; or
\item it treats a digest or verifier row produced before the accepted inventory
bytes as final evidence for the accepted inventory bytes.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(R^{+}\) is accepted by the finite-record support interface if and only if
the corresponding missing coordinate is added: respectively an upload receipt or
archive-equivalent byte-equality locator for \path{review_bundle/}, a
submission-time venue/bibliography record naming the checked URLs, source state,
environment, exit code, and log path, or a post-inventory fixed point in which
the extractor, retained finite-record verifiers, and final digest manifest are
regenerated after the accepted inventory and manuscript bytes are fixed.  Without
that added coordinate, the inclusion-minimal bad subrecord is exactly the single
strengthened coordinate just listed, and the strongest accepted reading remains
local/path-verified support, dated local-readiness evidence, or stale-preinventory
evidence rather than reviewer-visible external support, submission-time venue
compliance, or final digest evidence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof is a finite-coordinate separation argument.  First suppose that
\(R^{+}\) strengthens \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\) by declaring
\path{review_bundle/} to be externally uploaded or archive-visible support.
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} gives the two and
only two admissible external-support branches: a venue upload receipt or an
archive-equivalent byte-equality coordinate.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
states that local digest rows, local manifests, local paths, and bibliography
rows do not instantiate either branch.  Hence a state with the added receipt or
byte-equality locator is accepted at the stronger external-support level by the
record-gate exactness theorem, while a state agreeing with \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\)
on all local rows and lacking that coordinate cannot determine the stronger
reading.  The failed schema clause is precisely the missing external-support
coordinate, so the bad subrecord is minimal.

Second suppose that \(R^{+}\) upgrades a dated venue/bibliography check to
submission-date compliance or later-date readiness.  Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}
proves that venue rules and bibliography locator states are time-indexed support
coordinates, and Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}
identifies the coordinate required for an upload-time or submission-time claim:
the observed URLs, observation time, source state, environment, command result,
exit code, and log path.  Adding that coordinate supplies exactly the finite
record read by the venue branch.  Omitting it leaves only the earlier dated
local-readiness row, and two support states can agree on that dated row while
differing on later page contents or submission-form behaviour.  Therefore the
single missing time-indexed venue coordinate is both necessary and sufficient for
the stronger venue reading.

Third suppose that \(R^{+}\) uses a digest or verifier row produced before the
accepted inventory bytes as final evidence for the accepted inventory bytes.
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} makes the
extractor predicate a function of \path{main.tex} and
\path{theorem_inventory.json}; Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} require
the digest manifest to be regenerated after the files and command logs it names
exist.  Thus a passing post-inventory extractor run, the retained finite-record
verifier reruns, and a final digest regeneration close the accepted local fixed
point, while a preinventory row may hash or verify different bytes and cannot be
read as evidence for the accepted inventory.  The missing coordinate is exactly
the post-inventory fixed point, and removing any other coordinate from the bad
record would leave no asserted stale-to-final upgrade to reject.  These three
cases are the three strengthened coordinates in the statement, so the skeleton is
exhaustive for the proposed readings and the theorem follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Accepted-inventory final verifier--digest criterion]
\label{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}
For the accepted package state, once \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} are the accepted inventory bytes, the only possible
positive post-inventory support coordinate available from the local support
surface is the finite tuple consisting of \path{theorem_inventory.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.md},
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/source_interface_verification_run.log},
\path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory_verification_run.log}, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.
It is instantiated exactly when the four command logs are regenerated after the two
accepted inventory files and \path{main.tex} are fixed, each command exits with
status \(0\), the extractor omits no labelled theorem-like environment, the
three retained finite-record verifiers accept their bounded schemas, and the
final digest manifest is regenerated last with rows for the accepted inventory
files and the resulting command logs.  This tuple is a local finite-record
certificate only: it does not add an external upload/archive locator, an
actual-submission-date venue-compliance record, a fresh formal-source rebuild or
axiom-purity audit, or a dynamic artifact-semantic validation row.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple} with the
displayed concrete file names for \(I_{\mathrm{A2}}\),
\(R_{\mathrm{A2}}\), and \(D_{\mathrm{A2}}\).  The theorem gives sufficiency of the
ordered tuple: accepted inventory bytes first, post-inventory extractor and
finite-record verifier logs second, and the digest manifest last.  It also gives
necessity at the local support level, because any current-byte theorem-inventory
claim whose first absent member is one of these files is an inclusion-minimal bad
subrecord.  The zero-omission extractor condition is the syntactic exactness
condition of Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}
and the three verifier acceptances are precisely the retained finite-record
schemas classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}.  Finally,
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-support-surface-classifier} proves that the
other four coordinates named in the statement are independent stronger readings;
since the displayed tuple contains none of their required upgrade fields, they
remain absent.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Local submitted-support locator and freshness boundary]
\label{prop:submitted-support-locator-freshness-realization}
For the current presentation-route package, the submission-facing support
surface is the finite bundle consisting of \path{submission_abstract.tex},
\path{main.tex}, \path{source_interface_record.json},
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md}, and the directory
\path{review_bundle/}.  Its local locator is the bundle-relative path set named
in \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}.  Any archive-equivalent
locator is absent from the present local support surface unless a public locator
and byte-equality or digest-equality record binding that public surface to the
accepted bytes is added.  The manifest branch/path is therefore only a candidate
external coordinate, not an instantiated archive-equivalent locator.  The local
venue/bibliography coordinate for this package is the dated record
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log}, with
companion summary
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.md}; it supersedes
the older dated readiness rows only for the 2026--06--13 source state.  These
coordinates instantiate local reviewer-visible support and dated route
readiness, but they do not instantiate a DOI, venue upload receipt, venue
acceptance, public byte-equality fetch result, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, or
dynamic artifact-semantic validation.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The named files are finite paths in the submitted package and are exactly the
objects whose hashes are required by Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}
for the accepted-inventory fixed point, together with the source-interface file
and the primary presentation source used by Table~\ref{tab:primary-claim-support-map}.
The manifest records the direct bundle-relative path set and may record a
candidate public branch/path.  The direct-inclusion case supplies only
reviewer-visible local paths and digest rows.  A public branch/path becomes the
archive-equivalent case of Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
only after a public locator and byte-equality or digest-equality record are added;
without that equality the public branch/path remains only a candidate locator by
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.
The venue/bibliography row is a command-result coordinate: it names the official
route and bibliography locators checked, the source state, command form,
environment, exit code, and log path.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}, such a row is indexed by
its run date and therefore replaces older dated readiness rows only for claims
about the stated 2026--06--13 source state.  The negative clauses follow from
the same typed-coordinate separation: none of the displayed fields is a DOI, an
upload receipt, an acceptance notice, a public byte-equality fetch log, a
formal-source rebuild row, or an artifact evaluator row, so the corresponding
stronger readings are not functions of this finite support coordinate.
\end{proof}

This long technical supplement reports path-verified source architecture and case evidence.
It does not claim a fresh rebuild of the full newmath source tree.  A command-run
claim is outside the present evidence level unless the source commit,
environment, command, exit code, and log path are recorded with the submission.
This boundary is deliberate: the workflow is meant to make unsupported claims
visible rather than to hide them behind generated prose.

For the current presentation-only submission route, the public source link is
the newmath repository \cite{bedc-newmath-source} at pinned commit
\path{3fb3d6a0641767388a401883062aa522ea0b397b}.  The submission-facing support
surface is the included bundle-relative file set named in
Proposition~\ref{prop:submitted-support-locator-freshness-realization}: the
primary note, this supplement, \path{source_interface_record.json}, the accepted
inventory pair, and \path{review_bundle/} with
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  The automath branch/path in the
manifest is an archive-equivalent fallback only when its bytes are checked equal
to those digest rows.  The dated local venue/bibliography readiness record is
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log}.  No DOI,
venue upload receipt, venue acceptance, dynamic validation service, fresh
Lean/BEDC rebuild, or public byte-equality fetch result is claimed here.

\begin{theorem}[Four live noninstantiation coordinates]
\label{thm:four-live-noninstantiation-coordinates}
For the current CICM presentation-only package, the submitted support surface
instantiates the bounded local finite-record theorem chain and does not instantiate
any of the following four stronger coordinates:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a fresh clean-source Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-existence audit, or
axiom-purity audit for the pinned newmath commit;
\item a public archive, DOI-bearing supplement, venue-upload receipt, or
archive-equivalent byte-equality locator for the review bundle;
\item a dynamic semantic validation record for Rule~110, GroundCompiler, or any
other finite artifact row; or
\item an upload-time venue-compliance or venue-acceptance record.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently every citation from the compact article to this support surface
factors through the path-verified source-interface rows, local digest rows,
finite verifier records, historical case rows, and the dated 2026--06--13 local
venue-readiness observation.  Any reading that asserts one of the four stronger
coordinates is accepted by the manuscript only after adding the corresponding
command row, upload-or-archive byte-equality row, artifact-validation row, or
upload-time venue row; without that addition, the stronger-reading tag together
with its missing coordinate is an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The positive support surface is the local fixed point of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-byte-support-fixed-point-nonupgrade-boundary} and the
submitted-support realization of
Proposition~\ref{prop:submitted-support-locator-freshness-realization}.  Those
results name the inventory pair, local verifier logs, final digest manifest,
source-interface record, review-bundle paths, and the dated 2026--06--13
venue/bibliography check.  They therefore establish exactly the bounded
finite-record projection used by the compact article.

For item~1, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Proposition~\ref{prop:manual-source-interface-non-escalation},
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} separate the
pinned path/commit/line-range interface from any fresh formal-source command
claim.  A fresh rebuild, marker-existence audit, or axiom-purity audit reads a
source commit, environment, command, exit code, log path, and checked predicate;
those fields are not among the bounded source-interface fields and hence are not
instantiated.

For item~2, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} lists the
positive external-support forms, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves that local bundle paths, local digest rows, and local verifier logs do not
instantiate any of them.  The manifest's branch/path fallback is therefore only a
candidate public coordinate until a matching upload receipt or byte-equality
locator is added.

For item~3, Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} identify semantic
artifact validation as a separate validator-contract and command-result
coordinate.  Finite manifests, status snapshots, and historical case rows can be
held fixed while a fresh Rule~110, GroundCompiler, or other artifact semantic
validation run is absent or changed, so dynamic semantic validity is not a
function of the submitted finite witness rows.

For item~4, Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} separate a
dated local venue-readiness observation from an upload-time compliance bridge,
upload receipt, or venue outcome.  The 2026--06--13 log supplies the former only;
it contains no later upload action and no finite unchanged-rule bridge to such an
action.

The four missing coordinates lie outside the local finite-record projection just
described.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, no conjunction of the bounded
source, digest, verifier, case, and dated-readiness rows reconstructs an unread
coordinate.  The inclusion-minimal bad-subrecord clause is therefore exactly the
finite-certificate obstruction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}: delete the stronger tag
and the accepted bounded projection remains; add the missing coordinate and the
positive upgrade criterion applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Scope-contract six-coordinate boundary]
\label{thm:scope-contract-three-coordinate-boundary}
In the current presentation-only package, the following six support readings have
the displayed finite-coordinate status.  The first is the only positive local
current-byte support coordinate; the remaining five are false as claims of the
submitted finite record and true only as conditional upgrade forms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Post-inventory current-byte support.}  The local theorem-inventory
support coordinate is instantiated exactly after the accepted inventory bytes are
written, the theorem-environment extractor and finite-record verifiers are rerun
against those bytes, and the final digest manifest is regenerated after those
logs exist.  A pre-inventory or pre-edit log cannot certify later inventory
bytes.
\item \emph{External submitted support.}  A review-bundle reference becomes an
external submitted-support claim exactly when the finite record contains either
an exact venue-upload receipt for the submitted support surface or an
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator for the same bytes.  Without one
of those two coordinates, bundle paths, local manifests, verifier logs, and
digest rows support only the local/path-verified bundle boundary.
\item \emph{Fresh formal-source verification.}  A source-interface reference to
BEDC/newmath becomes a fresh formal-source verification claim exactly when the
finite record contains the source commit, command, environment, exit code, log
path, and checked rebuild, marker-existence, or axiom-purity predicate for that
run.  Without those command-result fields, the import remains the pinned
path/commit/line-range source-interface extraction only.
\item \emph{Fresh artifact-semantic validation.}  A Rule~110, GroundCompiler, or
other artifact row becomes a semantic artifact-validation claim exactly when the
finite record contains evaluator source, artifact/input bytes, environment,
command, exit code, output manifest, log path or equivalent result pointer,
digest binding, and the semantic validation criterion being checked.  Without
those fields, the row remains a finite status, witness, or limitation record.
\item \emph{Actual gate-implementation soundness.}  A publication-safety reading
becomes verified correctness of the implemented daemons, scripts, dispatch
tables, projection code, or human procedures exactly when the finite record
contains the implementation proof or pass tuple assigned to that gate and checks
it against the same package, ledger, schema, and projection contract.  Without
those rows, the core safety theorem remains conditional on record-gate soundness
and finite projection contracts.
\item \emph{Upload-time venue compliance and outcome.}  A dated local
venue/bibliography check becomes upload-time venue compliance, EasyChair upload,
acceptance, or proceedings status exactly when the finite record contains the
upload timestamp, receipt or form-state record, unchanged-rule bridge from the
checked venue state to that upload action, and any separate acceptance or
proceedings notice being claimed.  Without those fields, the 2026--06--13 check
is only dated local readiness.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover the five noninstantiated coordinates are independent extension
coordinates over the accepted local theorem-obligation and digest tuple: adding
prose, bounded source rows, local digest rows, historical case rows, dated venue
checks, or local verifier logs cannot instantiate any missing one of the five,
and adding one of the five does not instantiate the other four.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the post-inventory item,
Proposition~\ref{prop:post-inventory-fixed-point-support-certificate} identifies
the accepted inventory bytes as finite support coordinates of the selected local
package.  Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure} gives the necessary
ordering: after the inventory files are written, rerun the syntactic theorem
environment extractor and the retained finite-record verifiers, and only then
regenerate \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}.  Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}
then identifies the accepted tuple.  If a log or digest was generated before the
inventory write, its source hash is a hash of a different byte string or it omits
the later verifier output; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} it cannot determine a
claim about the later bytes.  Thus the current-byte coordinate is positive only
for the ordered post-inventory rerun-and-digest tuple.

For the external-support item, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
lists the positive forms of the coordinate: an exact upload receipt or an
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator.  Proposition~\ref{prop:submitted-support-locator-freshness-realization}
identifies the current support surface as the included local file set, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
proves the negative direction: local paths, local manifest entries, verifier
logs, digest rows, branch/path fallbacks, and dated venue-readiness observations
do not contain either positive external-support field.  Hence the current
bundle-backed reading is local/path-verified, while adding either listed locator
is exactly the finite coordinate needed for the external submitted-support
reading.

For the formal-source item, Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency} give the
positive bounded source-interface fields: pinned repository path, pinned source
commit, table and JSON rows, line ranges, bundled snapshot digest, line count,
and label containment.  Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} prove that
this interface does not read or type-check the Lean/BEDC development and does not
audit marker existence or axiom purity.  Those stronger predicates are
command-result predicates: their finite witness must name the source commit on
which the command runs, the command, the environment, the exit code, the log
path, and the checked rebuild, marker, or axiom-purity property.  Since those
fields are not among the bounded source-interface fields, the current package has
only the pinned source-interface extraction and no fresh formal-source
verification claim.

For the artifact-semantic item, Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}
identifies semantic artifact validation as a separate gate reading rather than a
consequence of the finite case-status row, and Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}
lists the required validation fields.  The Rule~110 and GroundCompiler rows used
in this manuscript are path-verified or historical finite witnesses naming an
observed issue and safe lesson; they do not supply evaluator source, fresh
artifact/input bytes, a run environment, command, exit code, output manifest,
semantic criterion, log/result pointer, and digest binding.  Therefore they
cannot be promoted from status or limitation evidence to fresh semantic
validation.

For the gate-implementation item,
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} states the safety theorem with
the record-gate-soundness and finite-projection hypotheses visible in the
headline, and Theorem~\ref{thm:five-interface-finite-skeleton-classification}
separates those hypotheses from verified implementation correctness of a gate,
daemon, script, runtime, or human workflow.  The implementation reading requires
the implementation tuple named there for the particular gate together with the
corresponding pass or proof-obligation rows, checked against the same package,
ledger, schema, and projection contract.  The current support surface contains
finite schema and projection records but no such implementation-soundness tuple;
therefore implementation correctness is not instantiated by the conditional core
safety theorem.

For the upload-time venue item,
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion},
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} make venue
readiness a time-indexed finite coordinate.  The record
\path{review_bundle/VENUE_BIBLIOGRAPHY_LIVE_CHECK_2026-06-13.log} is a local
check of venue and bibliography facts on 2026--06--13.  It names no later upload
timestamp, upload receipt, EasyChair form state, unchanged-rule bridge to an
upload action, acceptance notice, or proceedings notice.  Hence it is local
readiness evidence only and cannot be read as upload-time compliance or venue
outcome.

It remains to prove independence.  The five noninstantiated coordinate
predicates read disjoint finite fields: external support reads an upload receipt
or public byte-equality locator; formal-source verification reads formal-source
command-result and audit fields; artifact semantics reads evaluator, artifact,
semantic-criterion, and artifact-run fields; implementation soundness reads
gate-specific implementation proof or pass tuples; and upload-time venue status
reads upload, unchanged-rule bridge, acceptance, or proceedings fields.  The
accepted local theorem-obligation and digest tuple supplies inventory bytes,
finite verifier logs, source-interface rows, case rows, venue-readiness rows, and
digest rows only at their stated levels.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary},
two packages agreeing on all submitted finite fields cannot differ on an accepted
claim determined by those fields; conversely a claim requiring an unsubmitted
field is not determined by the submitted tuple.  By Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade},
conjoining bounded rows from other channels cannot reconstruct a missing upgrade
coordinate.  Hence none of the five noninstantiated support readings follows from
prose, bounded source rows, local digests, historical case rows, dated venue
checks, or local verifier logs; and because each positive upgrade adds only its
own finite field family, no one upgrade supplies the field family required by any
other upgrade.  The minimal
bad-subrecord statement is the corresponding instance of
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}: the stronger tag plus
the first absent required coordinate is rejected, while the bounded local
projection remains accepted.
\end{proof}
