\begin{theorem}[Five-interface finite-skeleton classification]
\label{thm:five-interface-finite-skeleton-classification}
For the CICM presentation-only package, the five weak interfaces isolated by the
scope audit have the following common normal form.  Let $r$ be a load-bearing
reading which uses one of the five interfaces
\[
\mathcal W=\{\mathrm{RGS},\mathrm{ImplProj},\mathrm{SrcBound},
\mathrm{ArtWitness},\mathrm{ThmInv}\}.
\]
Then $r$ is accepted by the present theorem chain exactly at the bounded
finite-record level displayed below, and every stronger reading requires the
listed independent upgrade coordinate:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathrm{RGS}$ supports conditional finite-record publication safety under
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$; unconditional safety requires an accepted
record-gate-soundness row for the same package, ledger, surface, and dispatch
table.
\item $\mathrm{ImplProj}$ supports only the named scripts' parsed
projection-contract predicates; verified implementation correctness of a gate,
daemon, runtime, or human workflow requires the implementation tuple
$\mathcal I(g)=(Q_g,U_g,M_g,X_g,N_g,\Pi_g)$ with the corresponding pass or
proof-obligation rows.
\item $\mathrm{SrcBound}$ supports only the pinned path, commit, line-range,
bounded-summary, and finite record-comparison fields of the source-interface
snapshot; exact source-statement import, semantic source completeness, Lean/BEDC
rebuild, or axiom-purity claims require the corresponding formal-source,
command-run, or semantic-audit coordinate.
\item $\mathrm{ArtWitness}$ supports only finite manifest and witness rows for
the artifact case study; dynamic artifact semantics, evaluator correctness, or
unbounded Rule110/GroundCompiler validity requires a separate
artifact-validation coordinate naming the evaluator contract, artifact bytes,
semantic predicate, and pass record or command-run tuple.
\item $\mathrm{ThmInv}$ supports only syntactic theorem-environment label
coverage and ledger inclusion for the final inventory bytes; proof checking,
semantic theorem completeness, formal rebuild, or external upload requires the
appropriate proof-checking, semantic-extractor, formal-source, or
upload/archive-equivalence coordinate, and the extractor and digest records must
be regenerated after the final inventory bytes are fixed.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover the five upgrade coordinates are independent over the present local
finite-record package: conjoining bounded rows from the other four interfaces
cannot supply a missing upgrade coordinate for the fifth.  Consequently the
stronger tag together with the first absent upgrade coordinate is an
inclusion-minimal bad subrecord, while deleting that stronger tag leaves the
bounded finite-record reading accepted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each of the five interfaces has already been reduced to a finite projection and
a non-escalation theorem.  For $\mathrm{RGS}$, Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface},
Theorem~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine},
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary},
Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-record-gate-soundness-boundary} identify the positive
content as conditional finite-record publication safety from the finite predicate
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$, and identify the missing unconditional premise as
the bad subrecord when the premise is omitted.  For $\mathrm{ImplProj}$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} proves only
the four named scripts' finite parsed predicates, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton},
Theorem~\ref{thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-implementation-upgrade-absence} identify the
six-coordinate tuple $\mathcal I(g)$ as the exact missing extension for any
implementation reading.  For $\mathrm{SrcBound}$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded-source-interface-maximality}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation} bound the
positive source import to the pinned finite fields and reject semantic source
completeness without a separate formal-source or semantic-audit coordinate.  For
$\mathrm{ArtWitness}$, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-witness-manifest-record-interface},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary} give exactly the finite
manifest/witness reading and the separate artifact-validation upgrade.  For
$\mathrm{ThmInv}$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary},
Theorem~\ref{thm:extractor-domain-exactness-non-gluing},
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem-obligation-ledger-boundary} give only syntactic
environment-label coverage, inventory inclusion, and the post-inventory
rerun/digest condition; they do not parse proofs or rebuild formal sources.

It remains to show that the five rows do not glue into a stronger claim.  The
coordinates read in the five positive clauses are disjoint finite field families:
record-gate rows and dispatch data, parsed script projections, source-interface
snapshot fields, artifact manifest/witness fields, and theorem-inventory
extractor/digest fields.  A stronger reading changes at least one field family by
adding an unconditional RGS row, an implementation tuple, a formal-source or
semantic-source audit, an artifact-validation tuple, or a proof-checking,
semantic-extractor, formal-source, upload, or archive coordinate.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}, a conclusion that
depends on such an unread field is not determined by the present finite
certificate.  By Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, bounded
rows from the remaining channels cannot reconstruct the missing field.  Finally,
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} gives the
inclusion-minimal bad-subrecord form: the first absent upgrade coordinate plus
the stronger tag is rejected, while removing the stronger tag returns exactly to
the accepted bounded finite-record reading.\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Local issue-coordinate normal form]
\label{prop:local-issue-coordinate-normal-form}
For the current presentation route, the five live support-boundary
coordinates have the following complete normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The canonical post-inventory support coordinate is positive exactly for
the local current-byte tuple of
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}: the accepted
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes, the
post-inventory theorem-environment extraction log, the three retained
finite-record verifier logs, and the final digest manifest regenerated after
those logs exist.
\item The upload/archive support coordinate is absent from this local package
unless an exact supplemental-upload receipt or an archive-equivalent public
byte-equality locator is added.  Local paths, local manifest rows, and local
digest rows therefore support only the local/path-verified bundle boundary.
\item The formal-source coordinate is the bounded pinned-path source-interface
coordinate only.  It is not a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker-existence audit,
or axiom-purity audit unless a separate command-result row with those predicates
is supplied.
\item The Rule110/GroundCompiler coordinate is historical limitation evidence
only.  It is not a dynamic artifact-semantic validation unless evaluator source,
semantic criterion, artifact bytes, environment, command, exit code, log path,
and digest binding are supplied.
\item The venue/bibliography coordinate is dated local readiness evidence only.
It is not an upload-time venue-compliance record unless the final finite record
also contains the actual upload timestamp, upload receipt or form-state record,
and an unchanged-rule bridge from the dated check to the upload action, or a
replacement check made immediately before upload.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the first coordinate can be closed by the canonical local rerun and
digest refresh, while the latter four coordinates remain deliberate
noninstantiation boundaries rather than hidden hypotheses or conclusions of the
article.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Item~1 is exactly the accepted-inventory fixed point of
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}.  Those results
separate the inventory bytes from the command logs and require the digest
manifest to be regenerated last; hence a stale extractor log or stale digest row
is not the canonical coordinate, while the ordered rerun tuple is sufficient at
the local finite-record level.

Item~2 follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.
They list the positive external-support fields and prove that local bundle paths,
manifest entries, and digest rows do not imply a venue upload, DOI-bearing
supplement, or public archive-equivalent byte-equality fetch.  Therefore the
accepted package can expose a local support surface but cannot assert external
support until one of those finite locator records is added.

Item~3 follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness},
Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}.  These
results prove the path, commit, line-range, snapshot, and row-consistency
interface for the imported source spine, and they make the stronger
formal-source reading depend on separate rebuild, marker, and axiom-purity
command predicates.  Since no such command-result row is present here, the
source-interface theorem remains bounded.

Item~4 is the artifact analogue: Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:four-live-noninstantiation-coordinates} isolate the missing
semantic-evaluator fields.  The Rule110/GroundCompiler case rows identify a gate
lesson from historical limitation records; without the evaluator specification,
artifact byte set, semantic predicate, environment, command result, log path, and
digest binding, finite-coordinate determination prevents upgrading that lesson
to artifact-semantic validity.

Item~5 follows from Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}.  Those
results make the venue row depend on the rule state at the upload event, not only
on a prior local web check.  The current log is dated 2026--06--13 and supplies no
upload timestamp, upload receipt, form-state record, unchanged-rule bridge, or
replacement immediately-before-upload check.  It therefore remains preparatory
venue-readiness evidence and cannot be promoted to an upload-time compliance
record.

The final sentence is then the no-gluing
conclusion of Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}: the closed
inventory tuple supplies only its own coordinate, and absent coordinates cannot
be reconstructed by conjoining bounded rows from other channels.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Final support-surface dichotomy and inventory exactness]
\label{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}
In the final finite-record reading of this presentation-route package, the
support surface has exactly the following two-coordinate normal form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The files \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md}
are accepted only as the public bounded theorem-obligation ledger for labelled
theorem-like environments in the submitted sources.  They are synchronized
support records and indexes: they may expose the obligation set and the review
routing of those obligations, but the corresponding TeX statements and proofs
remain the objects that discharge the mathematical claims.
\item The technical supplement, theorem ledger, and review bundle are external
support only after either an exact venue-upload receipt for that support surface
or an archive-equivalent byte-equality locator for the same bytes is added to
the finite record.  If neither coordinate is present, every support-surface
claim using those objects is local/path-verified only, even when the local files,
local extractor logs, and local digest rows are present.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the submitted-support theorem chain closes at the local
finite-record level with the synchronized inventory artifacts, and it closes at
the external support level only after the independent upload/archive coordinate
is supplied.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the first item, the accepted-inventory coordinate is the local current-byte
tuple isolated in Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple},
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:local-issue-coordinate-normal-form}.  Those results
identify the two inventory files, the post-inventory extractor run, the retained
finite-record verifier logs, and the final digest refresh as the finite records
that close the inventory coordinate.  None of those statements promotes the
inventory from an index of labelled obligations to a proof object: the proof
obligations are the labelled TeX environments themselves, and the inventory is a
bounded synchronization and routing record for those environments.  Hence the
inventory artifacts may be used exactly as public theorem-obligation ledgers and
not as substitutes for the printed statements or proofs.

For the second item, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}
gives the only two positive instantiations of the external support coordinate:
an exact upload receipt or an archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator.
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-live-noninstantiation-coordinates}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:local-issue-coordinate-normal-form} prove the negative
direction for the accepted package: local paths, local manifests, local digest
rows, and venue-readiness observations do not imply venue upload, DOI-bearing
supplement, public byte equality, or acceptance.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, the missing external
coordinate cannot be reconstructed by conjoining the bounded inventory, digest,
review-bundle, or source-interface rows.  Thus absence of the upload/archive
field forces the local/path-verified reading, while presence of one of the two
listed finite fields is precisely the extra coordinate required for the external
support reading.

The final sentence is the conjunction of the two coordinates.  The inventory
coordinate is closed by synchronized local artifacts and their rerun/digest
records.  The external support coordinate is logically independent and requires
one additional upload/archive field.  Finite-coordinate determination therefore
allows the former without the latter and forbids any final submission claim from
reading local support records as external support unless the upload/archive
coordinate is actually present.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Terminal local-support acceptance normal form]
\label{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}
Let the accepted local package state contain the synchronized inventory pair
\(I\), namely \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md}, the post-inventory extractor and retained verifier
logs \(R\), and the post-log digest manifest \(D\), namely
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md}, produced in the order required by
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}.  Then the terminal support
reading of this package has the following exact normal form.  If that ordered
tuple is absent for the latest edited bytes, replace item~1 below by the single
negative coordinate ``post-inventory current-byte closure absent''; items~2 and~3
are unchanged.
\begin{enumerate}
\item When present, the coordinate \((I,R,D)\) closes the theorem-inventory support obligation
precisely as a local finite-record byte coordinate: it records current labelled
environment coverage, retained finite-record verifier outcomes, and the digest
rows binding those bytes.
\item The same coordinate does not instantiate external support.  External
support for the technical supplement, theorem ledger, or review bundle is present
only in extensions of the finite record that add either an exact venue-upload
receipt for the same support surface or an archive-equivalent byte-equality
locator for the same bytes.
\item Consequently every terminal package state has a unique two-coordinate
classification: local inventory closure may be present without external support,
external support is present only after the independent upload/archive coordinate
is added, and no state may infer the latter from the former by gluing inventory,
log, digest, or path rows.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For item~1, the hypothesis that \((I,R,D)\) was produced in the required order is
exactly the criterion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}: accepted
inventory files first, the post-inventory theorem-environment extractor run and
the retained certificate/source-interface/primary-claim verifier logs second,
and the final digest refresh last.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}
specializes this conditional tuple to the package state in which those bytes have
not subsequently changed, and supplies the positive theorem-inventory coordinate
only for that state.  The extractor component is
syntactic labelled-environment coverage, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point}; the retained
verifier components are command-result rows, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-command-result-closure}; and the manifest component is a
byte digest refresh, by Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion}.  Thus
\((I,R,D)\) closes exactly the local finite-record byte coordinate and no
stronger semantic coordinate.

For item~2, Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} lists the
two positive ways to instantiate external support: an exact upload receipt or an
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator.  Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation},
Theorem~\ref{thm:four-live-noninstantiation-coordinates}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness} prove the
negative direction for the current local support surface: inventory files,
extractor logs, verifier logs, digest rows, path availability, and dated
readiness observations do not imply venue upload, DOI-bearing supplement,
public byte equality, or acceptance.  Hence external support requires the
independent upload/archive coordinate stated in the item.

For item~3, suppose two terminal readings agree on whether the ordered tuple
\((I,R,D)\) is present.  If it is present, item~1 makes them agree on the local
theorem-inventory byte coordinate; if it is absent, they agree on the negative
post-inventory coordinate.  If neither reading adds an upload/archive field,
item~2 classifies both readings as local/path-verified only.  If one reading adds
such a field and the other does not, the two readings do not agree on the
external support coordinate, so the difference is exactly the independent
extension field isolated in
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record}.
Finally, Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} forbids producing
that missing external field by conjoining bounded inventory, log, digest, or path
rows.  These alternatives exhaust the finite-record support surface, proving the
unique classification.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Terminal support-coordinate discharge]
\label{thm:terminal-support-coordinate-discharge}
For the current CICM presentation-only package, the two residual support
coordinates at the end of the Stage--A theoremization pass have the following
complete finite-record classification.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The post-inventory current-byte coordinate is accepted exactly when the
accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes are
followed by rerun records for the theorem-environment extractor and the retained
certificate, source-interface, and primary-claim finite-record verifiers, and
then by a regenerated \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} digest
manifest whose rows bind those inventory and log bytes.
\item The external submitted-support coordinate is accepted exactly when the
same finite support surface is extended by either an exact venue-upload receipt
for the selected supplemental bundle or an archive-equivalent public locator with
byte-equality or digest-equality evidence for the selected bundle bytes.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the present local package may discharge the first coordinate by rerunning
the local extractor/verifier/digest tuple, while the second coordinate remains a
positive external receipt-or-locator field and cannot be discharged by local
inventory, digest, verifier, bibliography, or path-availability rows alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Item~1 is precisely the positive branch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}, specialized to
the concrete inventory pair, retained log tuple, and digest manifest named in
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}.  The
``exactly when'' direction follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple}: before the inventory pair exists,
or after it is edited without rerunning the extractor and retained verifiers, the
first absent member of the ordered tuple is a finite bad subrecord; after the
extractor and retained verifier logs exist, the coordinate is still open until the
digest manifest is regenerated last, because the manifest rows are the byte
bindings read by the final-support claims.  Once the ordered tuple is present,
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure} accepts exactly the syntactic
theorem-environment coverage and finite-record verifier outcomes stated in the
item, with no Lean rebuild, semantic proof check, or artifact-validation
upgrade.

Item~2 is the positive branch of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} together with the
update protocol of
Proposition~\ref{prop:upload-or-archive-instantiation-update-protocol}.  Those
results list the two and only two finite records that instantiate external
submitted support: a receipt for the exact selected upload surface, or an
archive-equivalent public locator whose byte or digest equality binds the same
surface.  The negative direction is
Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:four-live-noninstantiation-coordinates}: local paths, local
digest rows, verifier logs, dated venue/bibliography reachability, and candidate
manifest branch/path text lack the upload-or-public-equality field.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, conjoining those local
records cannot create the missing external coordinate.  Hence the first
coordinate is a rerunnable local fixed point, whereas the second is an
independent external receipt-or-locator extension.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current-inventory rerun exactness]
\label{thm:current-inventory-rerun-exactness}
Let $B$ be a source state obtained after editing either \path{main.tex},
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, or \path{theorem_inventory.md}.  A terminal claim
that the inventory bytes, verifier logs, and final digest rows form the current
local fixed point for $B$ is accepted by the finite-record interface if and only
if the following ordered finite tuple is present for the bytes of $B$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the accepted inventory pair \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} as byte strings of $B$;
\item a zero-exit syntactic theorem-environment extraction record whose input
hashes name the \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json} bytes of $B$;
\item zero-exit retained finite-record verifier logs for the certificate,
source-interface, and primary-claim records, produced after the accepted
inventory pair exists; and
\item a regenerated \path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} produced after
the logs in the preceding two items exist, with rows for the accepted inventory
files and those logs.
\end{enumerate}
If any member of this tuple was computed before the edited bytes of $B$ existed,
or if the digest manifest was not regenerated after the last retained log, the
same prose is only historical or conditional and does not discharge the current
post-inventory support coordinate.  Adding the tuple discharges only the local
syntactic inventory/verifier/digest coordinate; it does not add an external
upload receipt, archive-equivalent public locator, fresh formal-source rebuild,
record-gate implementation proof, upload-time venue-compliance record, or dynamic
artifact-semantic validation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward direction is the ordered fixed-point construction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-local-rerun-tuple} applied to the edited byte state
$B$.  Item~1 supplies the inventory byte coordinate.  Item~2 is exactly the
syntactic coverage coordinate of Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}: the
extractor is deterministic on \path{main.tex} and \path{theorem_inventory.json},
so its zero-exit log names the current labelled theorem-like environments and the
current inventory-label set, not an earlier pair of byte strings.  Item~3 supplies
the retained finite verifier command-result coordinates singled out in
Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple}.  Item~4 is the
digest-closure condition of Theorem~\ref{thm:digest-closure-refresh-criterion};
because the digest is produced last, the rows in the final manifest bind the same
inventory and log bytes used by the support claim.  Hence the local support row is
current for $B$.

Conversely, suppose the terminal claim is asserted without one member of the
ordered tuple.  If the inventory pair is absent, the claim lacks the byte surface
whose coverage is being asserted.  If the extractor log predates $B$, then the
deterministic extractor has been applied to a different finite input; changing
the inventory or manuscript can change the extracted label set or the inventory
label set, so the old log is not a coordinate of $B$.  If a retained verifier log
predates the accepted inventory pair, it is a command-result record for an older
support surface.  If the final digest manifest predates a retained log or the
accepted inventory bytes, it cannot contain the SHA--256 rows binding those byte
strings.  In each case two finite package states can agree on all earlier rows
while differing on the missing current-byte field, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary} rejects the current
fixed-point reading and leaves only the historical or conditional reading.

The last sentence follows from the separation theorems already used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-support-coordinate-discharge}: the rerun tuple contains
only local files, command results, and digest rows.  The independent external,
fresh-source, implementation-soundness, upload-time venue, and dynamic artifact
coordinates require their own finite fields, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade} forbids manufacturing those
fields by conjoining bounded local rows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current-package five-coordinate closure criterion]
\label{thm:current-package-five-coordinate-closure-criterion}
For the current CICM presentation-only package, the five support readings most
likely to be confused with stronger end-to-end claims have the following exact
finite-coordinate status.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Local theorem-inventory support is current-byte positive exactly for package
states containing the accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes together with post-inventory theorem-environment
extraction, certificate-verification, primary-claim-verification,
source-interface-verification, and final-digest records generated after those
accepted inventory bytes.
\item Publication-safety consequences for the concrete tuple
$(P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})$ remain conditional on
$\mathsf{RGS}_{S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})$ unless the submitted finite record
contains an accepted record-gate-soundness row for exactly that package, support
surface, ledger, and dispatch table.
\item The imported newmath/BEDC source interface is bounded source-interface
evidence only, not fresh formal-source correctness, unless the certificate is
enlarged by a fresh rebuild, marker-audit, and axiom-purity row with source
state, environment, command, exit code, and log path.
\item The finite witness and Rule110/GroundCompiler case rows are manifest and
limitation evidence only, not artifact-semantic validation, unless the certificate
is enlarged by a dynamic artifact-validation row naming the evaluator contract,
input bytes, semantic predicate, environment, command, output manifest, exit code,
and log path.
\item The technical supplement, theorem ledger, review bundle, and local digest
records are local/path-verified support only, not external availability or archive
equivalence, unless an exact upload receipt or archive-equivalent public
byte-equality locator is added.
\end{enumerate}
These five clauses are inclusion-minimal: deleting the named coordinate from any
clause leaves a finite package state with the bounded local record but without the
stronger reading, while adding exactly the named coordinate gives the corresponding
positive upgrade accepted by the same finite-record calculus.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Clause~1 is the positive and negative direction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure},
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure},
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}, and the explicit
stale-byte criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:current-inventory-rerun-exactness}:
inventory bytes alter the package state, so current-byte inventory support
descends only through the ordered post-inventory extractor, verifier, and digest
tuple computed from those edited bytes.  The listed certificate, primary-claim,
and source-interface verifier records are precisely the retained finite verifiers
named by that tuple; without them the state may agree on the printed inventory
files while disagreeing on the post-inventory log and digest coordinates.

Clause~2 is Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary}.  The
publication-safety spine constructs finite certificates from the external
record-gate predicate; absent an accepted row for the exact tuple
$(P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})$, there is no finite field proving the submitted
gate rows and evidence pointers needed for an unconditional current-package
instantiation.

Clause~3 follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}.  The present source record
contains path, commit, label, line-range, digest, and bounded-summary fields.  A
fresh formal-source reading asks for different fields---a rebuild, marker audit,
axiom-purity audit, source state, command environment, exit code, and log path---so
the bounded source-interface row cannot imply it.

Clause~4 follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  A case manifest records
the existence, path, and limitation role of finite artifacts; a semantic artifact
claim additionally reads an evaluator contract, concrete input bytes, a semantic
predicate, execution environment, command, output manifest, exit code, and log.
Since those fields are disjoint finite coordinates, manifest evidence cannot be
promoted to dynamic semantic validation.

Clause~5 is Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}.  Local
paths and digest rows identify the submitted local support surface; an external
availability or archive-equivalence claim reads an additional public locator or
upload receipt plus byte equality.  The current local rows do not contain that
field.

For minimality, each cited boundary theorem is an if-and-only-if finite-coordinate
criterion.  In each clause, remove the named upgrade coordinate while keeping the
bounded local rows fixed; the bad-subrecord theorem for that interface supplies a
state in which the bounded record remains true and the stronger reading is false.
Add exactly the named coordinate; by the positive direction of the same cited
criterion the finite verifier accepts the upgraded reading.  The five coordinate
families are separated by Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, so
no coordinate can be reconstructed by gluing bounded rows from another clause.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-interface current-package discharge criterion]
\label{thm:five-interface-current-package-discharge-criterion}
For the current CICM presentation-only package
\((P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\), the five challenged support interfaces have
the following exact finite-coordinate normal form.  A reading of the package is
accepted by the finite-record schema if and only if each of its uses of these
interfaces stays on the displayed bounded side or supplies the corresponding
positive upgrade coordinate.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The master publication-safety and compressed-presentation conclusions are
unconditional for this package only in an extension of the accepted ledger that
contains an accepted record-gate-soundness row for exactly
\((P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\), including the source state, command,
environment, exit code, log path, fixture or proof-obligation list, and checker
digest for the concrete row if implementation-level gate soundness is asserted.
Without such a row they remain conditional on
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S_{0}}(P_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\).
\item The theorem-inventory coordinate is discharged for a byte state only by the
ordered local tuple consisting of accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes, a post-inventory zero-exit theorem-environment
extractor log, zero-exit retained verifier logs for the certificate,
source-interface, and primary-claim records, and a final digest manifest
regenerated after those logs exist; any fixed-point or digest claim about a later
edited byte state must be recomputed from that later state.
\item The imported newmath/BEDC source interface remains a bounded path, commit,
line-range, manifest, and summary interface unless a fresh formal-source row adds
the relevant command, source state, environment, exit code, log path, rebuild
status, and axiom/assumption-audit result for this submission byte state.
\item The Rule110/GroundCompiler case rows remain limitation and manifest evidence
unless a dynamic artifact-validation row names the evaluator source, input bytes,
semantic predicate, command environment, exit code, output manifest, log path, and
digest binding; absent that row, the artifact claim is only finite witness or
limitation-disclosure support.
\item The technical supplement and review bundle remain local/path-verified
support unless a later row supplies either an exact venue-upload receipt for the
same bytes or an archive-equivalent public locator with byte or digest equality
for those bytes; until then no external submitted-support coordinate is present.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover these five coordinates are independent schema axes: supplying one of
them neither supplies nor weakens any other.  Thus the current theorem chain may
use a local inventory tuple only for the byte state for which the post-inventory
commands and digest manifest have actually been rerun, but every unrealized
stronger reading above is rejected by the first missing coordinate on its own
axis.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the ``if'' direction, inspect the five schema blocks in order.  Clause~1 is
exactly the current-package specialization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary}.  That theorem
identifies the accepted RGS row for
\((P_{0},S_{0},L_{0},\Gamma_{0})\) as the finite coordinate that turns the
conditional hypotheses of Theorems~\ref{thm:rgs-conditional-compact-spine},
\ref{thm:presentation-compressed-interface}, and
\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} into an unconditional current-package
instance.  If the stronger claim is implementation-level gate soundness, the
same block is refined by
Theorem~\ref{thm:gate-implementation-soundness-upgrade-obstruction}: the finite
record must also contain the concrete source-state, command, environment, exit
code, log, fixture or proof-obligation, and checker-digest fields for the gate
implementation.  With those fields the RGS block is filled; without them the
reading is not an unconditional concrete-gate-soundness theorem.

Clause~2 follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:current-inventory-rerun-exactness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:accepted-inventory-coordinate-realization}.  Those results prove
both directions: the listed ordered tuple is sufficient because it provides the
accepted inventory bytes, current syntactic extraction, retained finite-verifier
command results, and last digest binding; it is necessary because any missing or
pre-edit member leaves a stale-coordinate state indistinguishable from the prose
alone and therefore cannot discharge current-byte closure.  Since editing the
manuscript changes the byte state read by the extractor and digest manifest, the
same proof applies after every later edit: the tuple closes only after the
post-edit extractor, retained verifiers, and digest generator have been rerun and
their exit codes and log paths are recorded.

Clause~3 is the formal-source boundary of
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}, together
with Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}.  The available source
rows are finite records of paths, commits, labels, bounded summaries, manifest
agreement, and snapshot digests.  A Lean/BEDC rebuild, source-theory semantic
closure, marker-correctness assertion, or axiom-purity assertion reads additional
command-result and audit fields not present in that bounded projection.  Hence
the finite verifier accepts the current text only as a bounded source-interface
claim unless a separate fresh formal/source rebuild row supplies the current
source state, command, environment, exit code, log path, rebuild status, and
assumption-audit result.

Clause~4 is the artifact boundary of
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  The Rule110 and
GroundCompiler records currently identify case-study paths, manifests, and
limitations.  Dynamic semantic validation is a different predicate: it reads an
evaluator, input bytes, semantic predicate, environment, exit status, manifest,
log, and digest binding.  Since those fields are absent from the limitation rows,
the stronger semantic reading is rejected until the dynamic row is added; the
accepted case-study use is therefore finite witness and limitation disclosure.

Clause~5 is the external-support dichotomy of
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}.  Local
paths, verifier logs, and digest rows bind local bytes, but an upload or archive
equivalence statement additionally reads a receipt or public locator and a byte
or digest equality statement for the same support surface.  Those fields are not
created by the local digest manifest, so the finite schema accepts only the
negative or conditional external-support wording until such a row is added.

The independence statement is Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}
applied to the five displayed axes, with the schema partition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}.  Each axis has
its own bad-subrecord theorem and its own positive extension criterion; changing
one axis leaves the finite fields read by the others unchanged.  Therefore the
schema accepts exactly the conjunction of bounded claims and supplied upgrade
rows listed in the statement.  Conversely, if any stronger reading is asserted
without its listed row, hold all other fields fixed and vary only the missing
block.  The corresponding boundary theorem supplies a finite state with the same
bounded rows and a false stronger reading, so the missing block is the first bad
subrecord.  The current package may therefore close the local inventory axis only
after the ordered tuple is present for the current bytes, while RGS,
formal-source, dynamic-artifact, and external-support upgrades remain conditional
on their own finite rows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Stage-A issue discharge normal form]
\label{cor:stage-a-issue-discharge-normal-form}
For the current presentation-route manuscript, the five audit issues consisting
of unconditional record-gate-soundness discharge, fresh formal/source rebuild,
fresh artifact-semantic validation, external submitted-support upload, and
post-inventory digest acceptance are simultaneously resolved by the following
normal form.  Publication-safety theorems are read with the explicit
\(\mathsf{RGS}\) hypothesis unless the accepted RGS upgrade row of
Theorem~\ref{thm:five-interface-current-package-discharge-criterion}(1) is added;
source claims are read only at bounded source-interface level unless the fresh
formal/source row of item~(3) is added; artifact claims are finite witness or
limitation-disclosure claims unless the dynamic validation row of item~(4) is
added; external-support statements are negative or conditional unless the
upload/archive row of item~(5) is added; and theorem-inventory fixed-point or
digest claims are valid only for a byte state whose accepted inventory files are
followed by the post-inventory command tuple and digest refresh of item~(2).
No omitted row can be reconstructed from the other four rows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:five-interface-current-package-discharge-criterion} to the
five named issue coordinates.  Each sentence of the corollary is exactly the
bounded side or positive-extension side of the corresponding item of that
theorem.  The final no-reconstruction statement is the independence clause of
the theorem, which itself follows from the schema partition and no-gluing
corollary.  Thus the five issue coordinates are discharged together without
promoting any bounded row to a stronger unsupported reading.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Six-coordinate submission-boundary normal form]
\label{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}
For the current presentation package, every load-bearing support reading of the
manuscript factors through exactly the following six coordinate classes.  The
first coordinate is positive only in package states that contain the ordered
post-inventory extractor, verifier, and digest tuple of
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}; otherwise its value is the
negative stale-or-absent-rerun coordinate.
\begin{enumerate}
\item the local theorem-obligation ledger coordinate, consisting of
\path{theorem_inventory.json}, \path{theorem_inventory.md}, the theorem-environment
extraction log, the retained finite-record verifier logs, and the refreshed digest
manifest;
\item the external-support coordinate, consisting only of a venue-upload receipt
or archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator if such a record is later
added;
\item the formal-source coordinate for the imported newmath/BEDC interface;
\item the artifact-semantic coordinate for the Rule110/GroundCompiler case rows;
\item the implementation-soundness coordinate for the actual gate-producing
daemons, scripts, and human procedures; and
\item the time-indexed venue/bibliography-compliance coordinate.
\end{enumerate}
In the accepted package the first coordinate, when instantiated by the ordered
post-inventory tuple, is instantiated only at the local finite-record level,
while coordinates 2--6 remain exactly at the bounded levels
stated elsewhere in this supplement: no external support, no fresh Lean/BEDC
rebuild or axiom-purity audit, no fresh dynamic artifact-semantic validation, no
implementation-soundness audit of the actual workflow beyond the explicit
record-gate-soundness hypothesis and finite script projection contracts, and no
upload-time venue-compliance or venue-acceptance record.  Consequently every
accepted theorem-chain consequence of this supplement is a finite-record,
local/path-verified consequence unless one of the independent missing coordinates
above is supplied as a new finite row with its command, environment, source state,
exit code, log or receipt, and digest fields as appropriate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof is a finite-coordinate decomposition.  For coordinate~1,
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form},
Corollary~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure} identify the conditional inventory
tuple: the two inventory files, the post-inventory extractor record, the retained
finite-record verifier records, and the final digest refresh.  When this tuple is
present for the latest accepted bytes, Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:manifest-required-theorem-inventory-fixed-point} show that
the coordinate is syntactic theorem-like environment coverage and byte closure,
not semantic proof checking.  When it is absent, the same results classify the
first coordinate negatively as stale-or-absent post-inventory support.

Coordinate~2 is independent by
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}: local paths,
inventory rows, verifier logs, and digest tables do not instantiate a DOI,
venue-upload receipt, or public archive-equivalent byte-equality locator.  Thus,
absent one of those records, all bundle-backed support remains local/path-verified
by Proposition~\ref{prop:current-absence-external-support-surface-instantiation}.

Coordinate~3 is separated by
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction}.  The
imported BEDC/newmath interface is the pinned path, commit, line-range, and
bounded-summary surface; without a fresh formal-build row and an axiom/assumption
audit row it cannot be read as source-theory semantic completeness, Lean rebuild
success, marker correctness, or axiom purity.

Coordinate~4 is separated by Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  The
Rule110/GroundCompiler entries in the case table name historical limitation
surfaces and safe lessons.  They do not contain evaluator source, fresh input
data, a rerun command, environment, exit code, log, and output manifest; hence
they cannot be promoted to artifact-semantic validation.

Coordinate~5 is separated by
Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface},
Theorem~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction},
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-implementation-upgrade-absence}.  The theorem
chain assumes record-gate soundness for the abstract finite gate predicate and,
for the named scripts, proves only projection-contract exactness over the finite
fields they read and print.  It does not audit the whole daemon stack, Python
runtime, operating environment, or human workflow unless a separate implementation
tuple is submitted.

Coordinate~6 is time-indexed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:venue-rule-freshness-non-escalation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}, and
Proposition~\ref{audit:fresh-venue-record-criterion}.  The dated
venue/bibliography record is therefore a readiness observation for its own date,
not an upload-time compliance bridge, venue-upload receipt, or acceptance record.

The six coordinates are the axes isolated by
Theorem~\ref{thm:end-to-end-upgrade-decomposition-obstruction},
Corollary~\ref{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}.  Those results also give the
maximality and no-gluing clauses: conjoining bounded rows from other coordinates
cannot create a missing external, formal-source, artifact-semantic,
implementation-soundness, or upload-time venue coordinate.  Hence every accepted
presentation-package consequence factors through the instantiated local finite-record
coordinate together with the explicit bounded hypotheses, and any stronger
reading must add the corresponding independent finite row.  This proves the
normal form.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Current Stage-A2 support-coordinate realization]
\label{thm:current-stage-a2-support-coordinate-realization}
Assume the current presentation package is the local support state described in
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point} after the following finite
realization steps have been executed on the same source bytes: the accepted files
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} are present; the
syntactic theorem-environment extractor is rerun with exit code zero and log path
\path{review_bundle/theorem_environment_extraction_run.log}; the retained finite
record verifiers for certificate records, source-interface records, and the
primary-claim inventory are rerun with zero-exit logs; and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those files and
logs exist, with its command, source state, environment, exit code, and generation
log recorded.  Then the current package instantiates exactly the local
theorem-inventory and post-inventory digest coordinates.  It does not, by that
instantiation alone, instantiate any external upload or archive-equivalent
byte-equality locator, fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild or axiom-purity audit, dynamic
Rule110/GroundCompiler semantic evaluator coordinate, concrete gate
implementation-soundness audit, or venue acceptance coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first sentence supplies precisely the ordered tuple required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:post-inventory-package-fixed-point}: inventory bytes are fixed
before the extractor run, the finite-record verifier logs are computed from that
state, and the final digest surface is written only after those inputs exist.
Hence that theorem makes the theorem-ledger, verifier-log, and final-digest rows a
single local finite-record fixed point.  Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:accepted-inventory-final-verifier-digest-tuple} identify the
same fixed point as the post-inventory byte-closure coordinate, while
Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-theorem-environment-extractor-boundary} bounds its
meaning to syntactic coverage of labelled theorem-like environments by accepted
inventory labels.

It remains only to exclude the five stronger readings.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}, local paths
and digest rows are not an external upload receipt and are not an
archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator.  By
Theorems~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}, bounded source-interface rows are
not a fresh formal-source rebuild or axiom-purity audit.  By
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}, manifest-bounded
Rule110/GroundCompiler case rows are not dynamic semantic evaluator runs.  By
Theorems~\ref{thm:record-gate-implementation-overclaim-obstruction},
\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton}, and
\ref{thm:gate-implementation-soundness-upgrade-obstruction}, projection-contract
rows are not concrete implementation-soundness audits.  Finally,
Proposition~\ref{prop:dated-venue-record-instantiation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:historical-venue-record-non-escalation}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement} keep dated
route-readiness evidence separate from upload-time compliance and venue
acceptance.  These are independent finite coordinates by
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}, so the local
inventory/digest realization cannot glue them into existence.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Stage-A2 challenged-coordinate classifier]
\label{cor:stage-a2-challenged-coordinate-classifier}
For the current presentation-only support state, the four challenged coordinates
have the following exhaustive classification.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-inventory coordinate is positive only for the ordered
post-inventory fixed point: accepted \path{theorem_inventory.json} and
\path{theorem_inventory.md} bytes, followed by the theorem-environment extractor,
the three retained finite-record verifiers, and the final digest refresh on the
resulting bytes.
\item The upload/archive coordinate is negative unless the support surface adds an
actual upload receipt, upload form-state record, or public archive-equivalent
byte-equality locator for the final submitted bytes.
\item The formal-source coordinate is bounded to manual, pinned path-and-line
source-interface evidence unless a fresh Lean/BEDC source rebuild and
axiom-purity audit row records the command, source state, environment, exit code,
log path, and pass condition.
\item The artifact-semantic coordinate is bounded to manifest and limitation
evidence unless a dynamic evaluator row records the evaluator contract, input
bytes, semantic predicate, environment, command, exit code, output manifest, and
log path.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, the positive coordinate in item~1 cannot be used to infer any of the
three negative or bounded coordinates in items~2--4.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Item~1 is exactly the local theorem-inventory realization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-stage-a2-support-coordinate-realization}, expanded using
Corollary~\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}: the inventory files must be accepted
before the extractor and finite-record verifiers are rerun, and the digest is
computed only after those logs exist.  The proof of that theorem also identifies
the semantic content of the item~1 coordinate as syntactic theorem-ledger and
byte-closure support, not proof checking or external publication evidence.

Item~2 follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record},
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}, and
Coordinate~2 in Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}:
local paths, review-bundle rows, inventory files, and digest manifests are not an
upload receipt, upload form-state record, DOI-bearing replacement, or public
byte-equality locator.  Hence the coordinate remains negative until one of those
finite external records is added.

Item~3 is the bounded-source conclusion of
Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} together with
Theorems~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}.  Those results classify the
available source evidence as pinned path, commit, line range, extraction date,
JSON mirror, and bounded summary.  They explicitly exclude fresh rebuild,
marker-correctness, exact source-statement import, and axiom-purity readings in
the absence of the command-result row listed in the statement.

Item~4 follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}.  The Rule110 and
GroundCompiler rows available to the paper name case-study limitation surfaces
and manifest evidence.  They do not contain the evaluator contract, input/output
bytes, semantic predicate, command environment, exit status, and log fields needed
for a dynamic semantic validation row.

The final sentence is the no-gluing clause of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}.  The theorem
places inventory byte closure, upload/archive support, formal-source rebuild
evidence, and artifact-semantic validation in distinct finite coordinates.  A
record in one coordinate is therefore not a determinant of a missing field in any
other coordinate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Presentation-package five-coordinate support closure]
\label{cor:presentation-package-five-coordinate-support-closure}
For the presentation-only package, the five support-interface coordinates
have the following exact finite-record resolution.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The theorem-inventory coordinate is current only after
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} have their accepted
bytes, the theorem-environment extractor and retained finite-record verifiers are
rerun on that state with zero-exit logs, and
\path{review_bundle/FINAL_DIGESTS_SHA256.md} is regenerated after those logs.
\item Any claim supported by \path{review_bundle/}, the theorem inventory, or a
local digest row is local/path-verified unless an exact supplemental-upload
receipt or archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator is added.
\item The publication-safety spine remains conditional on
\(\mathsf{RGS}_{S_0}(P_0,L_0,\Gamma_0)\) unless the accepted ledger contains a
record-gate-soundness row for exactly \((P_0,S_0,L_0,\Gamma_0)\).
\item The imported newmath/BEDC source interface is bounded source-interface
evidence only unless a fresh formal-source rebuild and axiom-purity coordinate
with command, source state, environment, exit code, log path, and pass row is
added.
\item The Rule110/GroundCompiler case is limitation and manifest evidence only
unless a dynamic artifact-validation coordinate names the evaluator contract,
input bytes, semantic predicate, environment, command, exit code, output
manifest, and log path.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the terminal closure leaves absent exactly the following stronger
coordinates: an external upload receipt, upload form-state record, DOI-bearing
archive record, or archive-equivalent public byte-equality locator; a
clean-machine, fresh Lean/BEDC, fresh source-tree, marker-correctness, or
axiom-purity rebuild coordinate; a dynamic Rule110/GroundCompiler semantic
evaluator coordinate; a concrete gate-program implementation-soundness
coordinate beyond the finite-input projection contracts of the named verifier
scripts; and a venue-upload, upload-time venue-compliance, DOI-publication, or
venue-acceptance coordinate.  No conjunction of the bounded records in these
five clauses supplies any of these absent coordinates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-stage-a2-support-coordinate-realization} gives the
current-package realization of the local inventory/digest coordinate.  Clause~1
is coordinate~1 of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}, together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form} and
Corollaries~\ref{cor:post-inventory-rerun-closure} and
\ref{cor:current-byte-closure}: the ordered post-inventory rerun tuple is exactly
the syntactic theorem-ledger and byte-closure coordinate, and it has no semantic
proof-checking content.  Clause~2 is coordinate~2 of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}, equivalently
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-or-archive-instantiation-record} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}: local
paths and digest rows do not instantiate upload or archive equivalence.  Clause~3
is Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-rgs-instantiation-boundary}, which identifies
the exact accepted row needed to remove the record-gate-soundness hypothesis for
\((P_0,S_0,L_0,\Gamma_0)\).  Clause~4 follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:source-interface-semantic-completeness-obstruction} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-source-promotion-obstruction}: the pinned source snapshot
and line-range record is not a fresh Lean/BEDC rebuild, marker audit, axiom-purity
audit, or semantic source-theorem proof.  Clause~5 follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses},
Proposition~\ref{prop:artifact-validation-gate-unique-semantic-upgrade}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:artifact-semantic-validity-boundary}: the accepted case rows
name historical limitation surfaces, not a fresh evaluator run with the semantic
validation tuple.  The explicit absent-coordinate list follows by the same cited
boundary results.  External upload and archive locators are excluded by
clause~2.  Clean-machine, fresh Lean/BEDC, fresh source-tree,
marker-correctness, and axiom-purity rebuilds are excluded by clause~4.  Dynamic
Rule110/GroundCompiler semantic evaluation is excluded by clause~5.  Concrete
gate-program implementation soundness is excluded by
Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-script-projection-contract-support} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-gate-implementation-soundness-skeleton}, which
restrict the named scripts to finite-input projection contracts unless a further
semantic or program-verification coordinate is added.  Venue-upload, upload-time
venue-compliance, DOI-publication, and venue-acceptance readings are excluded by
Proposition~\ref{prop:dated-venue-record-instantiation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:upload-time-venue-compliance-record-requirement}, and the
venue coordinate of Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}.
The final no-gluing sentence is precisely the no-gluing part of
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}; the six
coordinates are independent finite boundary fields, so bounded evidence in one
field cannot create an absent coordinate in another.
\end{proof}
\section{Conclusion and support-boundary summary}

The supplement's theorem chain proves a finite-record certificate calculus for
publication claims under record-gate soundness.  The core mathematical/software
claim is not that AI output is proof evidence, that the workflow is a theorem
prover, that all BEDC declarations have been freshly rebuilt, or that the Rule110
artifact suite has been rerun for this submission.  Nor is it end-to-end workflow
correctness of the actual gate implementations, artifacts, proof-assistant runs,
support upload, or venue outcome.  It is that a theory-to-paper pipeline can
preserve traceability by separating source evidence, deterministic gates, agent
suggestions, human promotion decisions, and evidence-level boundaries, and by
rejecting stronger readings whose finite certificate fields are absent.  The
six-coordinate submission-boundary normal form,
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-coordinate-submission-boundary-normal-form}, collects these
interfaces into the terminal classification used by the presentation package.
The
closing obstruction theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:end-to-end-upgrade-decomposition-obstruction}, makes this sharp:
an end-to-end reading must pay the separate finite budgets for those stronger
coordinates, and without them the present result remains exactly finite-record
only.  The compressed terminal classifier,
Corollary~\ref{cor:primary-presentation-weak-interface-compression}, states the same
boundary as a primary-route consequence of the supplement-level maximality theorem for the five challenged interfaces: record-gate safety,
compiler and implementation-boundary rows, source imports, finite case witnesses,
and theorem inventories are accepted only at their bounded finite-record level
unless the matching upgrade coordinate is added.  Its no-gluing corollary,
Corollary~\ref{cor:no-finite-record-gluing-upgrade}, rules out obtaining those
stronger coordinates by conjoining bounded rows from different channels.  The
five-interface finite-skeleton classifier,
Theorem~\ref{thm:five-interface-finite-skeleton-classification}, applies this
same no-gluing rule directly to the five presentation-package interfaces: record-gate
soundness, finite script projection contracts, bounded source imports, finite
artifact witnesses, and syntactic theorem inventories.  The
upgrade-coordinate criterion,
Theorem~\ref{thm:three-upgrade-coordinate-exactness}, records the positive form of
the three upgrade paths most likely to be confused with the finite-record claim:
fresh formal/source rebuilds require source commit, environment, command, exit
code, and log path; external support requires an upload receipt or
archive-equivalent byte-equality locator; and implementation soundness of
concrete gate programs requires the six-coordinate audit tuple with the relevant
fixture or proof-obligation rows.  The scope-contract boundary theorem,
Theorem~\ref{thm:scope-contract-three-coordinate-boundary}, applies the same
finite-coordinate test to the three presentation-package support interfaces: external
submitted support, fresh formal-source verification, and fresh artifact-semantic
validation.  The presentation-package five-coordinate closure criterion,
Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-five-coordinate-closure-criterion}, then
collects the accepted current-byte inventory tuple, the still-conditional
record-gate-soundness coordinate, bounded source imports, finite artifact
witnesses, and local-versus-external support into one exact presentation-package
criterion.  Corollary~\ref{cor:stage-a-issue-discharge-normal-form} records this
criterion as the simultaneous normal-form discharge of the five Stage--A issue
coordinates.  The final support-surface dichotomy,
Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-dichotomy-inventory-exactness}, applies
that criterion to the two terminal support coordinates: the synchronized
\path{theorem_inventory.json} and \path{theorem_inventory.md} files close only
the bounded theorem-obligation-ledger coordinate, while the technical supplement,
theorem ledger, and review bundle become external support only after an exact
upload receipt or archive-equivalent byte-equality locator is added.  The terminal local-support acceptance normal form, Theorem~\ref{thm:terminal-local-support-acceptance-normal-form}, records the same conclusion as a two-coordinate classification for the accepted local package: the post-inventory rerun-and-digest tuple closes local inventory support without supplying the independent external-support coordinate.

The closing support records identify the selected route mode: the primary compact
article is the public presentation claim, while this technical supplement, the
bounded theorem-obligation ledger, and the review bundle are the submitted
source/support-package surfaces for finite-record proof discharge.  An additional
claim of DOI publication, public archive availability, external byte equality, or
venue-upload receipt requires its own finite upgrade coordinate.  In all cases
the theorem inventory indexes obligations only; the printed TeX statements and
proofs, not the inventory, discharge the mathematical obligations of the
finite-record safety theorem chain.
